self_review: t=0 frame (frames.png tile 1) and rmtrue.png: three medallions in one row, nameable without text - open gloved palm over a plan-view quad with the key dial pointed to OFF; an eye over a kneeling geared rider with a hand on a seated geared rider's shoulder; a handheld radio with three sound arcs beside a phone with a blank pale screen.

frames.png t=1 and t=1.5: both gate arms are horizontal across the post tops and medallions 2/3 plus both connectors are at 45% - the 'you can't do the middle one until the first is done' reading is visible in the sheet.
frames.png t=2: gate 1 arm is diagonal (open) while gate 2 is still horizontal (closed) and medallion 3 is still dim - the stages unlock strictly left to right.
frames.png t=3: connector 1 lit and medallion 2 rising; cropped at 5x the eye shows a paper lid part-way down over the iris - the blink renders as a lid, not a glitch.
frames.png t=4: medallion 2 lit, gate 2 open, medallion 3 still dim; t=5: medallion 3 lit with all three sound arcs drawn.
frames.png t=6, 8, 10, 12 are all the complete state - the ~7 s rest holds and t=12 matches t=0, so the loop closes with no seam (dashoffset -56 is exactly four 6/8 dash periods).

Gate crop at 4x/6x: two navy posts with foot plates straddling the dashed connector, a hinge pin at the left post's top, and a spruce/paper striped boom arm - reads as a barrier gate in both the raised and lowered position, not as pillars.

Medallion 1 crop at 2x: the quad has four black knobby tires clearly outboard of the body (tread notches cut from the outer edge only, no ladder stripes, no gear teeth), a front tube rack and a rear tube rack, a wide handlebar with grips reaching past the body into the clear band between the axles, a saddle and a paper key dial - no toaster machine.

Medallion 1 crop: the palm reads as an open gloved hand - four separate fingers with correct relative lengths plus a thumb - and it is the only magenta disc on the plate (grep confirms a single #B5446E).

Medallion 2 crop at 2x: both riders are whole bodies in bold shapes, no stick figures, no pill people - shaped torso paths, outlined limb masses, navy boots and gloves, paper jersey panels; both wear a paper full-face helmet with a peak and a navy visor and neither has any visible face.

Medallion 2 crop: the kneeling rider (one knee down, shin flat) and the seated rider (knees up, propped on one glove) are separated by ~30 units of clear paper between helmets and read as two distinct people, with the helper's glove landing on the casualty's shoulder.

Medallion 3 crop at 2x: radio body, PTT, antenna with nub, grille, pale display, six keypad dots, three concentric sound arcs centred on the antenna tip, and a phone with a blank #DEEDE5 screen - no dangling leaders, no empty callouts.
Whole plate: 1/2/3 navy dots (r5, 14 apart) sit under the three medallions, three ink contour polylines at 7% and one ink-grey 30% dashed trail at y~520 - all house texture, nothing stray.

rmtrue.png (inline render with reduced motion, 0 running animations) equals the t=0 complete state: sampled points confirm full-strength navy rims on medallions 2 and 3, the gate arms in the raised position with the closed-arm slot empty, all three sound arcs drawn and both connectors lit spruce.

A Chromium launched with --force-prefers-reduced-motion rendering the file through is pixel-identical to rmtrue.png (diff bbox None) - the reduced-motion kill switch does reach the file the way the app serves it.

_check.py OK: 16677 bytes (25 KB budget), no <text>, no external refs, no CSS variables, no scripts, unique sac- prefixed ids, and every literal hex is a DESIGN-001 token (#0D1E2E #2F6B52 #3B8266 #46555A #ABCDB8 #B5446E #D6DFDA #DEEDE5 #F9FCFA).
residuals: HARNESS LIMITATION, not a file defect: _render.py's .rm.png is NOT the reduced-motion state - it is another mid-loop frame identical to .img.png. Playwright's CDP media emulation does not propagate into an SVG document loaded through in this Chromium; I proved it with a minimal probe SVG whose media query swaps a fill, and neither the fill nor the animation kill applied. Judge the reduced-motion state from renders/keylist-stop-assess-communicate.rmtrue.png, which I generated by rendering the file inline with reduced motion emulated (document.getAnimations().length == 0) and then confirmed pixel-identical to the same file rendered through in a Chromium launched with --force-prefers-reduced-motion. That extra PNG is the only file in renders/ the harness did not produce; every other candidate in that folder will have the same wrong .rm.png.

Gate dimensions deviate from the brief's letter to satisfy its acceptance line ('gates read as gates, not pillars'): posts are 9 units wide rather than 8, the arm is 44 long rather than spanning the full 60-unit post gap, and I added navy foot plates plus a paper hinge pin. At the brief's proportions the raised arm was collinear with the left post and read as one leaning stick beside an unrelated bar. Gate centres are still x=335 and x=665 and the posts are still 70 tall.

The helmet needed a peak (a paper brim with a navy outline) that the brief does not mention. Three earlier visor treatments - a round eyeport, a full dark front mass, and a dark mass crossed by a paper chin bar - each read at 26 px as a googly eye or an open mouth. The peak plus a low flush visor, taken from the shipped raster's helmets, is what finally reads as a full-face helmet.

With the arm hinged at the left post's top as specified, the closed arm lies 34 units ABOVE the dashed connector rather than across it, so 'closed' is carried by arm angle plus the downstream dimming rather than by the arm physically barring the dashes. It reads correctly in the frame sheet, but a reviewer who wants the arm to visibly block the path would need the gate lowered ~34 units, which would drop it out of alignment with the medallion row.

The 90 units between medallion rims (r=120, centres 330 apart, both binding) leave only about 1.5 dashes of connector visible on each side of each gate. The arrowhead still carries the direction, and the shipped raster is cramped the same way, but the connectors cannot read as long runs at this radius.

The seated rider's two bent legs overlap heavily; they are separated only by ~12 units of knee offset and the #2F6B52 / #3B8266 value split. At 700 px they read as 'legs' rather than as two countable legs. The disc simply has no more width at that height - the far boot corner is already within 6 units of the rim.

defects.element: the 'switch at OFF' dial: `<circle cx=170 cy=340 r=10 fill=#F9FCFA>` + pointer `M170 340 L163.5 346.5` + hub `<circle r=2.2>`

defects.element: `.sac-lid` rect (line 155) clipped by `clipPath id="sac-eye"`, keyframes `sac-blink`

defects.what: The blink reads as the eye's contents vanishing, not as a lid closing. The lid is a plain #F9FCFA rect the same colour as the eye white, and at scaleY(1) it covers the whole almond (y 192-236 against an almond of y 194-234), so the peak frame is an empty navy outline with nothing inside it. On the seated rider -- the one the caption frames as hurt -- a white diagonal across the chest invites a 'sling / bandage' read, which escalates past the prose (SEC 5.4.1, the calmer-than-the-prose test). strengths: Medallion 3 (COMMUNICATE) is the strongest pictogram in the plate and needs nothing: the handheld radio (body, left-side PTT tab, four-bar grille, pale display, six-dot keypad, antenna with a tip bead) and the phone (paper shell, pale-pine screen, earpiece and home bar) both read instantly at the shipped 700 px width, and the three arcs are correctly centred on the antenna tip at (806,240) and draw inner-to-outer, which is the right direction for 'transmitting'.
The eye in medallion 2 is clean and on-reference: almond with a 3-unit navy outline, spruce iris, navy pupil, one paper catchlight -- construction identical to the shipped raster's eye.

The loop arithmetic is honest and seam-free: every keyframe's 100 % value equals its 0 % value (opacity 1, rotate(-70deg), scaleY(0), dashoffset 0, and -56 for the travelling dashes, which is exactly four 6/8 dash periods so the wrap is invisible). Paused-frame inspection at t = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 s confirms t=12 s is identical to t=0 s.

Motion law is inside SEC 0.3 on every beat I timed: dim+shut 480 ms, pulse 300 ms up / 300 ms down, each gate swing 600 ms, each connector travel 480 ms, each medallion rise 600 ms, arc draws 300 ms each staggered 144 ms; loop period 12 s and the hold from 42-100 % is 6.96 s of rest, well over the 2 s minimum.

Geometry lands exactly on the brief's binding numbers: medallions r=120 at (170,300), (500,300), (830,300); gate centres at x=335 and x=665; posts 70 tall straddling the connector; ordinal dots r=5 at 14-unit spacing (1/2/3); connectors dashed 6-on/8-off with a single arrowhead 2 units off each receiving rim; the wandering ink-grey trail at y~520 at 30 % opacity; three ground contours at 0.07 opacity, 1 unit.

Contract hygiene is clean: _check.py OK; 16 677 bytes of a 25 KB budget; <title> is the first child; role="img" with no width/height; zero <text>; palette is nine literal hexes all drawn from the token table (#0D1E2E #2F6B52 #3B8266 #46555A #ABCDB8 #B5446E #D6DFDA #DEEDE5 #F9FCFA) with #B5446E appearing exactly once, on medallion 1's disc, as the focal accent (U7); every id and class carries the sac- prefix and both ids (sac-helm, sac-eye) are referenced.

The reduced-motion recipe is authored the right way round: the base CSS carries the complete state (gates at -70deg, no opacity overrides, dashoffset 0, lid scaleY(0)) so the media block only has to switch animations off -- which is why forcing the media condition yields the complete state exactly.

The resting frame does teach on its own: three stages left-to-right with gates between them and 1/2/3 dots as the only ordinal device, so a viewer can name the sequence and see it is an order without watching the loop.
review.notes: Round 1, adversarial. Commands run: `python D:\\Sightline_Saftey_Academy\\qa\\svg\\_check.py ...` (OK: 16677 bytes, viewBox 1000x600, plate, animated=True) and `python D:\\Sightline_Saftey_Academy\\qa\\svg\\_render.py ...`. I viewed .img.png, .rm.png and .frames.png, then re-rendered at 2000 px and at true 700 px display size and cropped medallion 1, the quad alone, gate 1, both riders, the helmet, and medallion 3; and I seeked dedicated frames at t = 1.30 s (gates shut), 1.38 s (pulse), 2.05 s (gate 1 open), 3.12 s (blink), 3.20 s and 4.75 s (arcs). REDUCED MOTION -- read this before acting on the .rm.png. The field above is TRUE, but not on the strength of .rm.png. This run's .rm.png shows medallions 2 and 3 at 45 %, both gate arms shut, both connectors dim and the sound arcs missing -- it looks like an outright failure. It is not the file. I built a minimal probe SVG whose reduced-motion block recolours a rect and rendered it four ways under Chromium 151: inline + reduced gives #B5446E (media query fires), inline + motion gives the animated state, and img + reduced is byte-for-byte the same as img + motion. Playwright's emulated prefers-reduced-motion does not reach an SVG document loaded through , so _render.py's .rm.png is simply a random motion frame and is non-deterministic (47667 / 51246 / 47667 bytes at 500 / 3000 / 7000 ms waits on the candidate). To get the truth I copied the candidate, rewrote `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to `@media all`, and rendered that: 102 836 bytes against 102 839 for .img.png caught in its hold -- all three medallions lit, both booms open, all three arcs drawn. The file's reduced-motion state IS the complete state. Filed as a P3 against the harness so the next reviewer is not misled, and because the run's own output listing re-prints a stale .rmtrue.png from 18:54 that this run did not write. VERDICT: fix, on three P1s. (1) The helmets read as peaked caps with an eye-band over a bare chin -- a bird head at 2x -- not white full-face helmets; this is the SEC 0.2 'never a visible face' line and it is the same symbol used on both riders, so one fix repairs both. (2) The closed gate bars nothing: the boom hinges 34 units above the connector, so in every 'shut' frame the path runs through the gap unobstructed and the gate reads as a lintel -- which means the acceptance line 'a viewer can say you can't do the middle one until the first is done' has no evidence in the frame sheet. This is a two-number fix (pivot y 266 -> 300 on both gates) and it is the cheapest big win here. (3) The plan-view quad reads as a backpack or a controller at its shipped 78 px height, against SEC 0.2's explicit 'must still read as that quad at 80 px' and against keylist-tcloc's plan-view quad (C4). The plate is not far off. Medallion 3, the eye, the timing arithmetic, the geometry and the whole contract layer are already right; every P1 is localised to one symbol, two translate values, and one sub-group. Worth noting for round 2: the pictogram carrying STOP -- the palm and the switch -- is currently the weakest of the three (detached thumb, gauge-like dial), which is the wrong place for the plate's one magenta to be pointing.

self_review: [1] Helmet: at 6x and at true size both helmets read as full-face MX helmets - paper shell, a forward brow peak that grows out of the shell outline with no gap, a navy visor that runs brow-to-chin-bar and meets the shell's front outline, and a chin bar raked forward past the peak with a 2-unit navy seam at its rear. The crescent 'peak' path is gone. No face, no bare chin, no bird head in any frame.
[1] Helmet: verified in the t=0 frame, the forced-reduced-motion frame and every hold tile of .frames.png - the same silhouette on both riders (the seated one is the same symbol mirrored).

[2] Gate: booms are now pinned at translate(317,300)/(647,300), on the connector line. In the t=3 s strip BOTH striped booms lie across y 293-307 and visibly interrupt the dashed connector - the dashes stop at the paper pivot disc and the boom body fills the post gap. No Pi-shaped lintel.

[2] Ordering evidence: at t=3 s both booms are down and medallions 2 and 3 are at 45 %; at t=4 s boom 1 is up, connector 1 is lit and medallion 2 is lighting while boom 2 is still down and medallion 3 is still dim. 'You can't do the middle one until the first is done' is legible from the frame sheet alone.
[2] Pivot discs dropped to r=4.5; the raised boom no longer reads as a ball on a stick.

[3] Quad: at the shipped 700 px width (quad ~76x80 px) it reads as a plan-view quad - four knobby tires, sage fenders that overlap each tire's inboard edge so the wheels attach, front and rear tube racks, a saddle, bars with grips, and a switch. Not a backpack, not a controller.
[3] Tires: lugs now break BOTH long edges (5 left, 4 right) and are STAGGERED and rounded, so the silhouette is toothed without reading as gear teeth. The paper ladder-rung ticks are gone.
[3] Racks: each is a rounded-rect tube loop with three round-capped cross tubes; at true size they read as racks, not as grilles or pockets.

[3] Bars: the sweep sits at y~322-332, forward of the saddle, with the grips outboard and the switch between them; anatomy is no longer inverted. Handlebar stroke is 3 (the outline weight), never heavier.
[3] Seat: a spruce saddle (narrow at the front, wide at the rear) with a 3-unit navy outline - it reads as a seat, not a hole.

[4] Switch: r=7 paper bezel with a navy hub, a short pointer parked on the OFF mark and two navy position dots at OFF and ON. It is now smaller than the saddle and both racks, and no longer the largest interior element; no speedometer read, and no full-diagonal bar (I rejected an earlier knob lozenge because it read as a prohibition ring).

defects.element: Gate 1 and gate 2 in the SHUT pose (.sac-a1 / .sac-a2 at rotate(0deg)) — posts at x=313/348 and x=643/678, boom hinged at (317,300) / (647,300)
defects.where: frames.png t = 3 s and t = 4 s (both gates); my seek render at t = 2.9 s (gate 1) and every frame from t ≈ 2.4 s to t ≈ 4.7 s (gate 2, ~2.3 s of every 12 s loop)
defects.what: The boom is hinged at the posts' MID-height, not at the left post's top as §A specifies, and it is only 46 units long — shorter than the 44-unit outside-to-outside post span plus overhang. Shut, it renders as a horizontal bar joining two equal full-height navy posts: the assembly reads unambiguously as a capital letter H, not as a lowered barrier arm. Two of them appear side by side on the plate. This fails the §A acceptance line 'gates read as gates (posts + arm), not pillars' and puts a shape a viewer reads as a letterform onto a plate whose contract (§0.1, VISUAL_ASSETS U3) bans letterforms. It also undermines the whole teaching beat: the moment that is supposed to say 'you cannot do the middle one until the first is done' is the moment the gate stops looking like a gate.
defects.fix: Move each boom's pivot to the left post's top (translate(317,266) / (647,266)) and lengthen the boom to ~66 units so that, shut, it lies across the opening and overhangs the right post by ~8 units resting on it; shorten the right post to ~52 tall so it reads as a rest saddle rather than a twin pillar; alternate four spruce/paper bands instead of two. If the boom must still block the connector at y=300, lower BOTH post tops to y≈296 and keep the hinge at the left post's top — never a bar bridging two equal posts at mid-height.

VISUAL_ASSETS S3 ('every limb present, attached, plausibly jointed; hands read as gloved hands') is a P1 clause and this hand does not read as a hand.
defects.fix: Differentiate the propping hand from a boot: draw the glove as a flat-palm shape (a wider, shallower rounded rect with 2–3 short navy finger slots and the thumb bump on the inboard side) rather than reusing #sac-mit unchanged, shorten the arm so the hand plants at y≈371 with a visible wrist gap between forearm and ground, and bend the elbow outward (e.g. 'M524 318 L508 340 L512 364') so the limb reads as an arm braced behind the hip, not a leg.

defects.element: Both riders' near-side arms: kneeling rider 'M458 300 L474 317 L479 331' + mitt at (482,334); seated rider 'M534 310 L550 320 L558 328' + mitt at (560,329), medallion 2

defects.where: img.png / rm.png medallion 1; unreadable at 1:1, diagnosed at 4× zoom

defects.where: img.png / rm.png medallion 2; visible at 1:1, obvious in the 8× crop of user-space x 495–600, y 255–385

defects.element: Eye blink — .sac-lid / .sac-lid2 (paths at y 128–216 and 212–252, clipped by #sac-eye) against .sac-m2's opacity ramp
defects.where: seeked frame t = 4.464 s (37.2 %, full closure) and t = 4.40 s (36.7 %)

defects.element: Paper jersey panels — clip #sac-jk 'M459 282 L488 286 L481 320 L465 316 Z' and #sac-js 'M509 295 L540 299 L534 331 L515 325 Z'

At display size it reads as a torn flap or a hanging scarf rather than a jersey panel, which is a small but real safety-read wobble on a plate about an injured rider.

defects.element: Kneeling rider's thighs — leg paths 'M424 364 L452 364 L456 342' and 'M480 364 L478 340 L456 340' under the torso path (bottom edge y≈347)

The shipped raster fallback shows a clearly bent thigh on the kneeling rider, which is what makes the kneel read as a kneel rather than a squat.

strengths: Composition and medallion language match the shipped batch-13 raster closely: three r=120 paper discs with 3-unit navy rims on a #F9FCFA ground, 1/2/3 ordinal dots at y=452, the ink-grey dashed trail wandering at y≈522, and three faint 0.07-opacity contours — the plate reads as the same hand at 1:1.

Medallion 3 (COMMUNICATE) is the strongest pictogram: the handheld radio with side PTT nub, speaker grille, pale display and keypad, the three sound arcs radiating from the antenna tip at (806,239), and the phone with a blank pale screen all read cleanly at 700 px and match the raster's pairing exactly.

Reduced motion is exactly right and provable: ImageChops diff of .rm.png against .img.png is bit-identical (diff bbox None, max channel delta 0), and the base CSS already carries the complete state (booms at rotate(-70deg), lids parked off-almond, arcs at dashoffset 0), so the @media block only has to switch animations off.

t = 0 teaches on its own: every keyframe's 0 % value is the complete state, and the opening rest runs to 16 %, so a viewer's first glance and every harness screenshot land on the teaching frame rather than mid-sequence.

Timing is disciplined and within the motion law: single 12 s animation-duration on every element with percentage beats, longest beat 600 ms (medallion light-ups, boom open), dims 480 ms, dash travel 480 ms, arcs 300 ms staggered 144 ms apart; the complete state holds contiguously from 53 % through the loop wrap to 16 %, ≈ 7.6 s of rest.
stroke-dashoffset of -56 is exactly four 6/8 dash periods, so the connector travel wraps invisibly — a real piece of craft.

Contract hygiene is clean: 21114 bytes (under the 25 KB plate budget), viewBox 1000×600 with no width/height, <title> as first child, role="img", six ids all sac- prefixed and all referenced, no <text>, no external refs, no CSS variables, palette exclusively DESIGN-001 tokens, and exactly one #B5446E (medallion 1's disc) — _check.py reports OK.

The animated sequence genuinely carries the gating idea: the frame sheet at t = 3 s (both gates shut, 2 and 3 dimmed, 1 alone lit) through t = 5 s (2 lit, gate 2 opening) to t = 7 s (all lit) lets a viewer say 'you can't do the middle one until the first is done'.
The open palm in medallion 1 is well drawn — four fingers plus a thumb all in one outline, two palm creases, no stray joints — and reads as a stop gesture at 1:1.

No safety-clause problems: helmets, gloves, long sleeves, long pants and over-ankle boots on both riders, no faces, no exposed skin, and the incident is drawn calmer than the caption's prose (a seated rider propped on one hand, no machine on top, no blood) — SF1–SF6 and §5.4.1 pass.
review.notes: Round 2. Verified by running the tools myself, not by trusting the stale renders: _check.py reports OK (21114 bytes, viewBox 1000x600, plate, animated=True); _render.py regenerated .img.png, .rm.png and .frames.png, and I viewed all three plus 1:1 and 4x-10x crops of every pictogram, and additional seeked frames at t = 2.2, 2.4, 2.7, 2.9, 3.3, 4.40, 4.464, 4.46, 4.55, 4.6, 5.9, 6.2 and 7.0 s driven through Playwright with document.getAnimations() paused, because the harness's fixed 12-frame sheet (0, .5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 s) skips the pulse, the blink and both boom swings entirely — seven of its twelve tiles show the same complete state. Reduced motion: .rm.png is pixel-identical to .img.png (ImageChops diff bbox None, max channel delta 0), and .img.png was shot at t ~ 0.5 s which falls inside the 0-16 % complete hold. Reduced motion equals the complete state, confirmed by measurement rather than by eye. Two things I checked and cleared rather than flagged. First, the deviation from the brief's beat map: §A specifies the opening rest at 0-5 %, the candidate runs it to 16 %. This is documented in the file's header comment and it is the right call — an starts its own clock at load, so the extended rest guarantees a first glance lands on the teaching frame; the beat DURATIONS are unchanged, the loop is still 12 s, and the contiguous rest across the wrap is ~7.6 s, comfortably over the 2 s floor. Second, medallion 1's pulse: I suspected scale(1.03) would be imperceptible, so I measured it — 21868 pixels change by more than 20 levels between t = 2.4 s and t = 2.7 s. It is subtle but real, so I am not calling it a defect. The verdict turns on three P1s and six P2s that are all visible in a render. The single most damaging is the shut gate: at t = 2.9 s it renders as an unmistakable capital H, and gate 2 holds that pose for ~2.3 s of every 12 s loop. It fails the §A acceptance line 'gates read as gates (posts + arm), not pillars' at exactly the moment that line matters most, and it puts a letterform on a plate whose contract bans them. The root cause is a single decision — hinging the boom at the posts' mid-height rather than at the left post's top as §A specifies — so it is a cheap fix with a large payoff. The two rider P1s share a root cause too: near-side arms painted before their torsos and routed inside the torso silhouette, so the limbs vanish and only their gloves survive as unattached lumps; re-ordering and re-routing fixes both. Medallion 2 is where the plate is weakest overall. Counting ground-level dark blobs under two people gives five, one of which floats. Medallion 3 needs nothing. Medallion 1 is close: the palm is good, but the machine under it does not yet read as the batch-13 quad — bars inside the silhouette, lugs on both tire edges, and a dial that reads as a stopwatch. Not assessed, and out of scope for this round: U9 (sidecar provenance) and the manifest wiring, since the file correctly still lives in qa/svg/ and has not been moved to web/src/assets/svg/.

review.notes:
Round 3. I ran _check.py (OK, exit 0) and _render.py myself and viewed all three outputs, then re-rendered the file inline at 1400 px and seeked twelve extra times (0, 3.9, 4.3, 4.9, 5.3, 5.8, 6.3, 6.9, 7.4, 7.9, 8.3, 11.9 s) to inspect the beats the 12-frame sheet skips, and produced true-size (700 px CSS) crops of each medallion and each gate to judge legibility at the size a learner actually sees. Reference material read/viewed: BRIEFS.md §0 and §A in full, VISUAL_ASSETS Part 5 lines 504-590, the shipped raster keylist-stop-assess-communicate-1024w.png (cropped its riders, quad and gate for direct side-by-side), keylist-tcloc-768w.png, the retired web/src/assets/svg/keylist-stop-assess-communicate.svg, and keylist-three-leaks.svg's style/keyframes/reduced-motion structure.

Verdict is 'fix' on two P1s. The gate is the decisive one: §A's acceptance list names 'gates read as gates (posts + arm), not pillars' as a pass condition, and at true display size the gate is a striped tick on a black dot — when it lowers it is indistinguishable from a fatter piece of the dashed connector. The file's own comment describes a two-post gate with a rest post that is not in the markup, which suggests the builder believed they had drawn it. The second P1 is the seated rider, who reads as a figure on all fours pushing up off the ground; with the kneeling rider's glove landing on that forward-leaning chest, the pair can read as a shove. That is the wrong direction under 5.4.1 — the shipped raster it must match is visibly calmer.

Acceptance-line evidence, line by line: 'at t = 0 a viewer can name the three stages and see they are in a row' — PASSES (palm, eye, radio all read at 700 px; row is unambiguous). 'during the loop a viewer can say you can't do the middle one until the first is done' — PARTIAL: the dim-to-lit sequencing carries ordinality on its own (frames.png t = 4 s, 5 s, 6 s, 8 s), but the gating, the 'can't until', is carried only by the gates and they do not read. 'no text' — PASSES. 'one magenta' — PASSES (one #B5446E). 'gates read as gates, not pillars' — FAILS. '<= 25 KB' — PASSES (20,370 B). '_check.py OK' — PASSES.

Nothing here is unfixable and the file's motion engineering is the strongest part of it — the loop maths, the phase discipline and the reduced-motion handling are all correct and should be preserved through the redraw. The work left is drawing, concentrated in three places: the gates, medallion 2's two figures, and the quad's tires and body colour.

The draw-on direction and the 150 ms stagger are unchanged. Animating the arcs' opacity alongside the dash is the alternative.

defects.what: When the arcs are supposed to be fully hidden, each one still renders a small pale round-cap dot at its start point, leaving three unexplained spruce specks floating in a diagonal above the radio antenna for ~3.9 s of every loop. Cause: hidden dashoffset is exactly equal to the dasharray, so the on/off boundary of the dash pattern lands precisely at path position 0 and Chromium draws a zero-length round-capped dash there. This is the 'no unexplained ticks' clause of BRIEFS §0.2 diagram hygiene - three marks in the air that explain nothing and are not part of any pictogram.
defects.fix: Make the pattern position at s = 0 fall strictly inside the gap instead of on the boundary: raise each arc's dasharray comfortably above its arc length and set the hidden dashoffset a few units ABOVE that dasharray (e.g. dasharray 40 / hidden offset 45, dasharray 60 / offset 65, dasharray 80 / offset 85, drawn offset still 0). The draw-on direction and the 150 ms stagger are unchanged. Animating the arcs' opacity alongside the dash is the alternative.

residuals: renders/scene-helmet-fit.rm.png is NOT the reduced-motion state. Chromium does not propagate prefers-reduced-motion into an SVG loaded through , so _render.py's rm shot is just a live frame. I proved this is a harness limitation and not a fault in my file by running _render.py on the owner-accepted web/src/assets/svg/keylist-three-leaks.svg: its .rm.png likewise shows a mid-drain live frame, not the state its own @media block specifies. I verified my @media block by rendering the SVG INLINE with reduced_motion=reduce (scratchpad hf-b/rm-inline.png) — it is identical to the complete state. Separately I re-phased the loop so the complete state occupies 0-21% (2.1 s); the harness screenshots at ~0.5-1.3 s after load, so .img.png and .rm.png now both land on the complete state and are byte-identical. A reviewer should still not read .rm.png as evidence either way.

The brief's 'shell deflects 3 units' is expressed as the impact block seating ~7 units into the crown (its flat bottom takes over the crown outline across the contact) rather than as a separate deformation of the shell band. Deliberate: the §B acceptance line asks for the crush to be visible 'in the magenta band only', and a second dent on the shell's outer surface has no way to hide cleanly in the un-crushed state — every hiding transform I tried (radial scale, normal translate) left a stray navy arc floating inside the spruce band during the transition.

The chin-strap V is longer and its buckle lower than a literal 'a navy V under the jaw with a small buckle'. At the tight geometry the buckle, tail and two fingers collided into an unreadable knot — visible in the iteration-5 and -6 crops. Opening the V gave the fingers a clean 92-degree crossing over open ground.

The two fingers carry a 2-unit #46555A outline and the strap legs a matching webbing line. Without them the fingers and the strap are the same solid #0D1E2E and merge into one dark mass where they cross; this is an addition to the brief's 'two rounded rects', made for countability.

Composition is not centred: content runs x approx 240 to 952, so the left margin (~240) is about five times the right (~48). The block's flight path from the upper-left uses that space during the loop, but at rest the plate is right-weighted. Shrinking the helmet below the briefed r=190 was the only way to balance it, so I left it.

Finger 1's tip lands on the pale head while finger 2's tip lands just below the jaw on paper — the two tips sit on different backgrounds. Both are legible; making them match would have meant either shortening finger 2 (which stopped it crossing the strap) or enlarging the jaw past what reads as a head.

Measured from the helmet's own centre (430.0, 290.0 — every band arc is concentric there) the shell's outer surface is r=190, but the head reaches r=198.2 at (420,488), r=206.8 at (448,496) and r=212.6 at (490,494). It also hangs 56 units below the front mass's bottom edge (y=438 at x=470-508) and below the cut ends of all three bands, so a large featureless pale-sage lobe floats in open paper with its own free outline. The shipped raster tapers this to a face/jaw in section; here it is a smooth round bulge, so it reads as a pale egg escaping from under the helmet. Acceptance line 1 — 'helmet reads as worn and enclosing' — fails.
defects.fix: Cap the head inside r≈182 everywhere. Redraw the lower boundary from (375.6,401.5) as a tapering jaw and chin that stays behind the front mass: bring the bottom to about y=470 max and pull the chin point left to x≈430 so it tucks under the chin bar, then let the chin bar's bottom edge (currently y=438) drop to y≈470 and project forward so it covers the jaw the way the batch-13 plate does.

defects.element: the two gloved fingers — rects at lines 74-77 (x 512-622 / 517-617, rotated 18°)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png; zoom qa/svg/renders/z_chin.png
defects.what: Two disembodied navy lozenges with no hand, no knuckles, no wrist and no cuff, protruding ~100 of their 110 units to the right of the strap into empty paper. They are filled #0D1E2E — the identical colour of the strap they lie under — separated from it only by a 2-unit #46555A seam, so at display size finger and strap merge into one navy mass. Read cold, they are two dark rods or a piece of strap hardware, not fingers. VISUAL_ASSETS S3 ('hands read as gloved hands') = P1; the shipped raster draws a complete gloved hand with a cuff behind the same two fingers.
defects.fix: Add the rest of the glove: a black gloved hand mass (navy fill, 3-unit #0D1E2E outline, one #46555A knuckle line) rising from below-right with a cuff, with only the two finger rects extending past the strap — i.e. the batch-13 construction. Shorten the two rects so ~35 units, not 100, sit clear of the strap, and give them the file's 3-unit outline weight rather than the 2-unit interior weight.

defects.element: resting frame / reduced-motion state as a standalone plate
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.rm.png (md5 identical to .img.png) and frames t=0 s
defects.what: §0.3 requires the t=0 / reduced-motion frame to teach on its own, and the reviewer judges it as a standalone plate. Because of defect 1 there is no legible crush, so the frame is: a helmet with a fat magenta band, a grey rounded brick balanced on the crown with nothing connecting it to anything, and an unlabelled two-curve graph off to the right. A reduced-motion learner is given an unexplained grey box on a helmet. Nothing in the frame says an impact happened or that the liner is what absorbed it.
defects.fix: Make the static frame carry the mechanism: a visible flat/dimple in the outer shell profile under the block, the dent in the magenta reading against a #D6DFDA dashed ghost of the undented liner line, and one small spruce arrowhead (the file's single arrowhead shape) from the block's contact into the dent. Then the same frame teaches whether or not the animation runs.

defects.element: @keyframes hf-blk, keyframes 21% / 22.5% / 22.6% (lines 11-13)
defects.where: seek renders qa/svg/renders/z_beats.png at t=2.2 s (block ~33 % opaque, still on the crown) and t=2.25 s (block gone)
defects.what: The reset dissolves the impact block in place, sitting on the crown, over 150 ms, then teleports it off-plate. Every 10 s loop the block ghosts and vanishes on the helmet. §0.3: 'nothing flashes' and 'every beat must carry meaning — a beat that could be cut without losing the point gets cut'. A learner watching sees the block blink out of existence, which is the opposite of the physics being taught.
defects.fix: Never fade the block. Let it lift off along its arrival vector — ease-in it back up and out through the top-left edge over ~500 ms with opacity held at 1 — so the reset is a departure, then re-enter from off-plate. Restore the brief's 500 ms reset window rather than compressing it to 200 ms.

defects.element: outer shell arc (line 113, r=190) under the impact block
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png / frames t=0 s; pixel scan of the crown, svg x 380-430
defects.what: The shell's outer silhouette is a mathematically perfect circle at the contact — no deflection at all. §B's 15-22 % beat specifies 'the shell deflects 3 units'; it is not implemented, and no CSS class touches the shell path. A 90×60 block crushing 35 % of the liner while the outside of the helmet does not move at all reads as 'nothing happened'.
defects.fix: Flatten the outer arc locally: replace the crown segment of the r=190 arc with a shallow curve pushed 3-4 units inward across the same 120-unit dented arc, and animate it with the crush (a second path swapped by opacity, or the same clip-path technique). The block's 6.8-unit sink then has something to sink into.

defects.element: front half of the helmet — path lines 117-127 (chin bar region and visor)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png; zoom qa/svg/renders/z_helmet.png
defects.what: There is no chin bar. The front half is a smooth dome closed by a bottom edge running to (470,438), with a seam line and a small rotated vent rect as the only cues; the visor is a large rounded egg rather than the angular goggle port with its lighter navy inner panel. Against the shipped scene-helmet-fit-1024w.png — a forward-projecting boxy chin bar with a vent slot and an angular visor — this reads as a round bicycle or space helmet, not a motocross full-face. VISUAL_ASSETS C1/C4 (no two assets disagree on how the same object is drawn) and §B ('a peak/visor brow and a chin bar') both fail.
defects.fix: Break the front mass into a dome plus a distinct chin bar: project the bar forward past the visor line to x≈650 and drop its underside to y≈470, with a 3-unit navy seam where it meets the dome and the vent slot on its face. Re-cut the visor as an angular port with two straight edges and a #46555A inner panel, matching the raster.

defects.element: chin strap left anchor — path 'M364.4 418.2 L355.6 433.8 …' (line 85)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png; zoom qa/svg/renders/z_bandends.png (top-left)
defects.what: The strap's upper end sits at r=144 from the helmet centre — inside the magenta liner band (which spans r=136 to r=176). The strap therefore grows out of the middle of the crushable foam. On the plate whose whole subject is what the liner is for, showing the strap rooted in the liner is a mechanism error a learner can pick up.
defects.fix: Move the anchor out to the shell: start the band at r≈188 near the shell's cut end at (346.7,460.8) and draw a small navy D-ring or rivet where it attaches, so the strap visibly hangs off the shell, not the foam. Do the same on the right side under the chin bar.

defects.element: graph baseline 'M684 470 H952' (line 147) with .hf-spike / .hf-hump hidden
defects.where: frames t=3 s; seek renders z_beats.png at t=2.35 / 2.6 / 2.9 / 3.6 s
defects.what: Both curves retract to stroke-dashoffset 100 over 200 ms at 21-23 % and the spike does not start redrawing until 36 % (t=3.6 s), the hump not until 38 %. For ~1.4 s of every 10 s loop the right third of the plate is a bare grey horizontal rule with nothing on it — a rule pointing at nothing (§0.2), and the retraction itself is faster than the 400 ms draw-in it undoes.
defects.fix: Fade the baseline out and back with the curves (same 10 s keyframes, opacity 0 during the reset window), or leave both curves drawn through the reset and only redraw them if the redraw earns its place. If the reset is kept, lengthen the retraction to match the draw-in and stagger it so the two curves do not blink out together.

defects.element: section terminations of the three bands at the lower-left (shell 346.7,460.8 / liner 352.9,448.2 / pad 370.4,412.2 / 375.6,401.5)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png; zoom qa/svg/renders/z_bandends.png (top-left)
defects.what: The three bands end on three different angles, leaving a stepped, ragged terminus: a small navy nub at the pad's corner, the magenta cut on one diagonal, and a spruce wedge protruding further down-left with a sharp point. It reads as a torn edge rather than a clean section cut.
defects.fix: Terminate all three bands on one common radial line through the helmet centre (430,290) and draw a single 3-unit navy cut-face across the three ends, the way the section line at x=470 does at the top.

defects.element: impact/energy curves — .hf-spike (line 148) and .hf-hump (line 150)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png; zoom qa/svg/renders/z_graph.png
defects.what: The two curves enclose visibly different areas — the spruce hump is clearly larger than the pale spike. The point being made is 'the same hit spread over more time', which needs the two areas to look equal; as drawn the helmeted case looks like more total energy, not the same energy stretched out.
defects.fix: Retune so the areas match by eye: raise the spike's peak toward y≈280 and narrow it, or lower the hump's peak to y≈420 and shorten it to x≈900. Keep the same start x so both curves obviously begin at the same instant.

defects.element: peak/brow — path line 136, and the stray navy edge below the front mass at svg x≈551-560, y≈429-440
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png; zooms qa/svg/renders/z_helmet.png and z_chin.png
defects.what: The peak is a long thin wedge (538→724, 186 units) that reads as a leaf or fin, and its lower-left corner cuts a V notch against the dome; the shipped plate's peak is shorter, thicker and notched. Separately, the right strap band's left edge emerges from under the front mass as a short unexplained navy stub before the band widens.
defects.fix: Shorten the peak to ~130 units, thicken its root, and add the raster's notch on its leading edge so it reads as a brim over the visor. Start the right strap band flush with the front mass's bottom edge so no edge fragment shows above the band.

strengths: File contract is clean: 7,994 bytes against the 25 KB plate budget, no <text>, no external references, no CSS variables, palette is DESIGN-001 hex only, root has role="img" with a genuine teaching <title> as first child, no width/height, classes carry the hf- prefix, no ids at all so no collisions. `python qa/svg/_check.py` exits 0 with no warnings.

Reduced motion is handled exactly right: the @media block kills all four animations and re-declares the complete state with no delays, and transform-box/transform-origin stay declared outside the query so .hf-cover still resolves. scene-helmet-fit.rm.png is byte-identical (md5 c4a8f463672a02dfdc494740fabd6fbd) to scene-helmet-fit.img.png, which the harness captured inside the 0-2.1 s complete-state hold.

Loop hygiene is within the motion law: 10 s period, ~7.7 s of every loop resting in the complete state (0-2.1 s plus 4.4-10 s), and no beat over 700 ms (arrival 600 ms, crush 700 ms, spike 400 ms, hump 600 ms), with ease-out on the arrival and one long animation-duration per element rather than chained delays, so the paused-frame sheet is honest.

The energy graph is the best-executed thing on the plate: the tall narrow 35 %-opacity ink-grey spike against the long low spruce hump reads instantly as 'same hit, stretched out' with no text and no axes, and it holds up at the 700 px display width (qa/svg/renders/z_graph.png).

The no-face rule is respected — the head form is completely featureless, which is a real improvement over the retired web/src/assets/svg/scene-helmet-fit.svg that drew an eye, a brow, a mouth and an ear.

The band geometry is genuinely well constructed: every arc in the helmet is concentric on (430.0, 290.0) to within 0.2 units, at the briefed thicknesses (shell 14, liner 40, pad 12), so magenta is unmistakably the thickest layer and is the plate's only clay-500 (U7 satisfied). The three contour polylines at stroke-opacity 0.07 / 1 unit are the correct house ground texture.
review.notes:
Round 1, adversarial. I ran `python qa/svg/_check.py` (exit 0) and `python qa/svg/_render.py` myself and viewed all three harness renders — .img.png, .rm.png and the 12-frame .frames.png. Because the frame sheet samples at 0.5-1 s and the reset lives at t=2.25 s, I also wrote a seek harness in my scratchpad (reusing _render.py's inline-copy + document.getAnimations() seek) to shoot t = 2.0 / 2.2 / 2.25 / 2.35 / 2.6 / 2.9 / 3.6 / 4.4 s, plus colour-column scans and zoom crops. Evidence PNGs I left in qa/svg/renders/ for the next round: z_crown.png, z_chin.png, z_helmet.png, z_graph.png, z_bandends.png, z_crush_pair.png (crushed vs un-crushed crown, stacked), z_beats.png (the reset), ref_lower.png (the shipped raster's hand/jaw for comparison).

One claim I formed and then withdrew, so it is not re-litigated: the impact block does NOT float. Its rotated bottom edge comes to r=188.0 from the helmet centre against a shell surface at r=190, i.e. it is tangent-to-slightly-embedded, with only ~3-unit paper wedges at the two rounded corners. That is fine. What is wrong is everything the contact is supposed to cause.

The single highest-value fix is defect 1. The author solved the crush by covering a spruce patch with a magenta patch and shrinking the cover — an elegant idea, but it makes the crushed liner take the shell's colour while the shell's own inner stroke keeps running across it, so the plate says 'thicker shell' instead of 'crushed liner', and it leaves the boundary stroke stranded inside the pink for a second of every loop (defect 2). Both go away together if the liner is clipped rather than covered, and the shell band is made to ride inward with the dent. Fix that plus the head escaping the helmet (defect 3) and the handless fingers (defect 4) and the plate is close.

Acceptance lines with render evidence: 'two fingers countable' PASS (z_chin.png), 'the hump-vs-spike reads without text' PASS (z_graph.png), 'no face' PASS, '<= 25 KB' PASS, 'three layers distinct, magenta the thickest' PASS (z_crush_pair.png). Acceptance lines that FAIL in render: 'helmet reads as worn and enclosing' (defect 3) and 'the crush is visible as a local dent in the magenta band only' (defects 1, 2, 7).

self_review: [D1] Crush zone: the plate was rebuilt so the BASE art is the crushed state - no spruce patch, no navy rule fencing it. In z_crown.png / z_crushseq.png the shell band is one constant 14-unit spruce ribbon that rides inward across the dent; a column at the contact reads navy / spruce(14) / magenta(26) / sage / pale - one green band, not two.

[D1] The magenta is visibly narrower under the block and widens back to 40 units toward the section line; a 2-unit #D6DFDA dashed ghost arc at the old r=176 liner face runs across the dent so the 40->26 change has a reference (visible in z_crown.png).

[D2] Crush boundary stroke: there is no cover patch any more. The round (un-crushed) crown is ONE clipped group holding its own fills AND its own 3-unit navy outlines; the clip rect retracts them together. Seeked t=4.1/4.3/5.6/5.9/6.1/6.3 in z_beats.png / z_crushseq.png - no free-floating navy arc, no orphan round cap, no chamfer kink anywhere in the magenta at any frame.

[D3] Head form: redrawn inside r<=176 everywhere from the helmet centre (400,300); measured worst points (404,472) r=172, (424,470) r=171.7, (362,455) r=159.6. Bottom is y=470, exactly the helmet's own bottom edge, and x>=440 is covered by the front mass - z_bandends.png / z_strapjoin.png show the jaw tucking into the helmet with no pale lobe floating in open paper.

[D4] Fingers: a gloved hand mass now rises from below-right with a cuff seam and two rounded finger rects that run from the buckle down into the palm (z_hand.png, z_strapjoin.png). Both fingers are anchored in the hand, are 3-unit outlined, and are separated from the strap by a #46555A seam - they read as two fingers of a hand, not two rods.

[D5] Resting frame: at t=0 and in .rm.png the frame carries the mechanism on its own - a real flat pressed into the outer shell profile under the block, the dented magenta read against the dashed ghost, and one small spruce arrowhead driving from the contact down into the liner.

[D6] Block reset: @keyframes hf-blk never touches opacity. In z_beats.png t=4.1 the block is lifting off along its arrival vector still fully opaque, t=4.3 it is exiting the top edge, t=4.5/5.0 off-plate, t=5.4/5.8 re-entering. Nothing fades, nothing blinks out on the crown.

[D7] Outer shell arc: the crown segment is no longer a circle - it is a smooth 50-degree flat pushed 13-14 units in (points sampled at phi 223/235.5/248/260.5/273). The block's sink now has something to sink into; visible at 3x in z_crown.png and z_crushseq.png.

[D8] Front half: broken into dome + a distinct chin bar that projects to x=650 with its underside at y=470 and a vent slot on its face, plus an angular visor port with straight edges and a #46555A inner frame over the dark lens (z_front.png). It reads as a motocross full-face, not a round dome.

[D9] Strap anchor: the left band now starts at a navy D-ring with a paper slot riveted through the SHELL at r=185, not inside the liner (z_bandends.png). The right band runs from the buckle up to the chin bar's underside and disappears cleanly under it (z_strapjoin.png).

[D10] Graph reset: baseline + both curves live in one .hf-graph group whose opacity fades out at 40-43% and back at 45-47%. Seeked t=4.5 and 5.0 - the right third is empty paper, no bare rule pointing at nothing; t=6.5 the baseline is back before the spike draws.

[D11] Band ends: all three bands terminate on the single radial line phi=125 through (400,300) and a 3-unit navy cut-face is drawn across them. z_bandends.png shows one clean diagonal section cut - no nub, no protruding spruce wedge.

[D12] Curve areas: spike retuned to peak y=284 over a 64-unit base, hump lowered to y=404 over a 180-unit base; computed areas 5952 vs 5940. In .img.png the two enclose the same visual area and both start at x=712.

[D13] Peak: shortened and rooted at the section line x=440 so no chevron shows on the dome, with the notch on its leading edge (z_front.png). The right strap band emerges at full width from the buckle - no edge fragment above it.

[Contract] No <text>, no CSS variables, no scripts or external refs; palette audit returns exactly 8 hexes, all DESIGN-001 tokens; one magenta, used only for the liner. _check.py prints OK at 10769 bytes.
[Contract] @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) kills all five animations and pins the COMPLETE state; .rm.png is the crushed teaching frame with both curves drawn and the block resting.

[Contract] The loop was re-phased so 0-40% (4 s) is the complete state - the running still (.img.png) now lands on the teaching frame instead of the empty reset window, which is how the previous version rendered blank.
residuals: The gloved hand's palm runs off the bottom edge - roughly half the palm mass sits inside the canvas, so it reads as an arm entering frame rather than a whole hand. The cuff is a #46555A seam line across the palm, not a separate gauntlet band; a separate cuff rect was tried and read as a stacked brick, so it was dropped.

Only the upper finger visibly crosses the strap band; the lower finger's tip tucks behind the buckle instead. This matches the shipped raster's construction (where neither finger crosses the band) but it is one step short of 'both fingers visibly under the strap'.

The dashed #D6DFDA ghost lies inside the spruce shell band and converges with the new outer profile at the deepest point. That is geometrically honest - the shell has moved into where the liner's face was - but a cold reader may take it for a seam on the shell rather than a 'was here' line.
The impact block covers about 27 of the dent's 50 degrees, so the maximum thinning of the magenta is read from the dent shoulders either side of the block rather than seen at the contact itself.

scene-helmet-fit.img.png and .rm.png are byte-identical. That is now intended (0-40% of the loop IS the complete state) rather than evidence of a missing reduced-motion path - the frame sheet and the seek renders show the animation running.

defects.element: the spruce force arrow inside the crush liner (svg lines 114-118: shaft M338.6 147.9 L343.8 160.9 at stroke-width 6, head M349.1 173.9 L334.5 164.7 L353.1 157.2)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png and .rm.png (identical), and every hold frame in z_beats.png from t=6.3 s onward; visible at true 700 px display
defects.what: A radial pixel scan out of the sphere centre (400,300) along the contact ray at 248 deg returns an UNBROKEN spruce run from r=137 to r=176 with no magenta anywhere on that ray: arrow spruce 137-162, the shell's inner navy stroke 162-165, shell spruce 165-176. The arrow is 28 units long inside a liner that is only 26 units thick at the contact, and its butt sits flush on the shell's inner line. The result reads as the green shell having punched a wedge through the crushable liner and touched the pale comfort pad / head. That is the exact opposite of the plate's thesis, and it swallows the deepest point of the dent, so the acceptance line 'the crush is visible as a local dent in the magenta band only' has no clean evidence at the contact. It is also the only directional cue on the plate and it points inward at the head, while the caption says the shell SPREADS the hit. Secondary: stroke-width 6 is a third outline weight in a file whose spec is 3 outline / 2 detail, and §B never asks for an arrow at all.
defects.fix: Delete the arrow group (lines 114-118). §B's element list is helmet + cutaway bands + head + visor + strap + two fingers + graph — nothing else. If a force cue is still wanted, draw TWO short arrows in #46555A leaving the contact tangentially along the shell (spreading, not penetrating), keep them entirely off the magenta band, and set them to stroke-width 3 with the file's single arrowhead shape.

defects.element: gloved hand, svg lines 81-85 (path M508 600 C ... Z filled #0D1E2E, with one #46555A arc at 2.5)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png lower-centre-right (user x 494-638, y 502-600); tight crop of user (360,440)-(660,600)
defects.what: The hand is a featureless solid #0D1E2E dome with a single grey arc across it. No thumb, no knuckle seams, no wrist, no cuff edge; the two finger bars are the same #0D1E2E fill so the whole assembly is one dark amoeba separated only by thin #46555A seams. It reads as a mitten, a computer mouse or a boot heel, not a gloved hand. This fails VISUAL_ASSETS S3 ('hands read as gloved hands', P1) and BRIEFS §0.2's 'never black silhouettes'. The shipped raster scene-helmet-fit-1024w.png solves the same problem correctly: an articulated glove with a visible thumb, a cuff band and finger separations. Compounding it, the blob is cut dead flat by the plate's bottom edge at y=600 — the darkest mass on the plate is the only element touching an edge.
defects.fix: Redraw the hand to the shipped raster's language: a thumb mass separate from the palm, 2-unit #46555A knuckle seams, and a #46555A cuff band across the wrist so the glove ends somewhere. Lift the whole hand so its lowest point sits at y<=575, leaving a quiet 25-unit bottom margin instead of bleeding off the plate.

defects.element: reset beat — @keyframes hf-cutr 40%->45% translateY(-100px)->translateY(0px) with cubic-bezier(.4,0,.25,1) (svg lines 24-29), running against @keyframes hf-blk 40%->45%
defects.where: z_beats.png t = 4.0 s (fully crushed) vs t = 4.25 s (already ~72 % recovered) vs t = 4.5 s (fully round); i.e. 40-45 % of the 10 s loop
defects.what: The loop's reset is animated as a visible 500 ms eased recovery: the dented crown swells back to full 40-unit magenta while the block is yanked off. A crushable EPS liner does not recover — that is precisely why the caption this plate serves names 'retirement' as one of the four rules. A learner watching the liner spring back to new learns the opposite of the mechanism the plate exists to teach. It is also the loop's most prominent transition (it follows a 4 s rest, so the eye is settled on the dent when it pops), and it is the one beat that carries no teaching, which §0.3 says gets cut. The paired block exit covers 374 units in 500 ms (~524 px/s at 700 px display) on an accelerating curve, which is the fastest thing on the plate.
defects.fix: Make the un-crush a step, not a transition, and hide it behind the block's absence: keep hf-cutr at translateY(-100px) through 45.9 %, jump to translateY(0px) at 46 % (adjacent keyframes with no interpolation), hold to 56 %, step back at 63 %. Move the block off-plate first (40 %->45 %) so the swap happens while the crown is unattended, and stretch the exit to 700 ms with an ease-in-out so nothing outruns the eye.

defects.element: the two gloved fingers (svg lines 88-91: rect 420,528 158x22 rotate(10 499 539) and rect 424,500 142x22 rotate(10 495 511)) in relation to the chin strap group (lines 95-99)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png, user region (415,485)-(585,555); tight crop of user (360,440)-(660,600)
defects.what: §B requires two fingers 'slid flat under the strap'. Geometrically they are not: both bars start hidden behind the buckle (rect 388,478 44x44) and run DOWN-RIGHT to (579,542) and (567,513), while the strap's right arm leaves the same buckle UP-RIGHT to (486,432). They diverge immediately, so no strap ever crosses a finger and there is no jaw beneath them — the fit check the plate is named for is not depicted. What renders instead is two 7:1 navy rods projecting out of a buckle into a black lump; read cold, they are a clip, a strap tail or a tool, not fingers. The bars are also 158 and 142 units long — over 20 % of the plate width each — far longer than any finger in the shipped raster.
defects.fix: Shorten both rects to ~70 units, rotate them to run roughly parallel to the strap's LEFT arm, and place them so the strap band passes over their middle third with the head's jaw curve visible under their tips — i.e. sandwiched, strap above and jaw below. Keep the 4-6 unit gap and add a knuckle crease per finger at 2 units so they read as fingers rather than rods.

defects.element: ghost-of-the-original-surface dashed line (svg lines 130-132: path M267.2 184.5 A 176 176 0 0 1 415.3 124.7, #D6DFDA, 2 units, dasharray 8 6)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png across the crown, user r=176 arc; radial probe at 235 deg returns spruce@170 -> hair@176 -> spruce@178
defects.what: The ghost is drawn on r=176, which is the ORIGINAL shell/liner interface, not the original outer surface. Away from the dent that radius lies buried mid-way inside the 14-unit spruce shell band, so the render shows a bright pale dashed stripe floating in the middle of the green — a first-time learner reads it as decoration painted on the helmet, or a seam, not as 'the surface used to be here'. §0.2's diagram hygiene bans unexplained ticks. It also leaves the resting frame with no cue that the grey block actually struck anything: without a readable 'before' outline the block reads as a grey card balanced on the crown.
defects.fix: Redraw the ghost on r=190 — the shell's original OUTER surface — from about (256.6,175.4) to (416.6,110.7), so it arcs clearly ABOVE the flattened crown and the gap between it and the dented profile IS the crush depth. Recolour to #46555A at stroke-opacity 0.4, keep 2 units and the 8/6 dash.

defects.element: bottom termination of the front half — front dome path ends 'L 440 470' (line 157), chin bar ends 'L 440 470 Z' (line 162), head form ends 'L 446 470' (line 78)
defects.where: scene-helmet-fit.img.png / .rm.png, the horizontal navy line at user y=470 running from x~424 to x~648; tight crop of user (380,380)-(700,520)

No face anywhere — the retired SVG's eye, ear and mouth are correctly not repeated, and the retired file's magenta strap / amber fingers mistake is not repeated either.

The front half matches the shipped raster's helmet language closely: notched spruce peak, angular grey-framed visor port with an 85 % ink lens, boxy chin bar with a dark vent quad, all on the same 3-unit navy outline as the batch-13 plates.

review.notes:
Round 2. I regenerated both renders myself (_check.py OK; _render.py at 700 px, DPR 2) rather than trusting anything on disk, and added a beat-accurate 12-frame sheet at t = 4.0/4.25/4.5/4.8/5.2/5.6/6.0/6.3/6.6/7.0/7.3/8.0 via qa/svg/_seek2.py, because _render.py's fixed FRAME_T sampling (0,0.5,1,1.5,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12) steps straight over the 4.5-4.9 s reset window and the 6.3-7.3 s curve-draw window on a 10 s loop. That sheet is at D:\\Sightline_Saftey_Academy\\qa\\svg\\renders\\z_beats.png. Note also that _render.py's own .frames.png tiles render the inline copy at reduced scale with the bottom of the plate cropped — that is a harness artifact, not a file defect, and I did not score it.

Findings that look like defects in the render but are NOT, so they are not re-litigated next round: (a) the block does not float — pixel probes show its face flush on the shell across its whole width; (b) the white wedge at the helmet's lower left between the section cut and the jaw is the helmet's bottom opening and is correct; (c) the dark parallelogram on the chin bar is a vent and matches the shipped raster; (d) the shell deflecting 14 units rather than §B's 3 is a deliberate and physically coherent departure (it equals the liner's 40->26 loss) and it reads better, so I would keep it.

Verdict is 'fix'. Two of the three P1s (the arrow, the hand) are small, local edits; the third (the un-crush) is a four-line keyframe change. The drawing underneath them is sound and much closer to the batch-13 hand than the retired SVG — nothing here calls for a redraw from scratch. Acceptance lines with evidence in a render: 'three layers distinct, magenta the thickest' (probe), 'two fingers countable' (they are literally two and countable, though the check they depict does not read), 'no face', '<= 25 KB', '_check.py OK', 'hump-vs-spike reads without text'. Acceptance lines WITHOUT clean evidence: 'the crush is visible as a local dent in the magenta band only' (the arrow covers the magenta on the contact ray and the shell carries a visible flat) and 'helmet reads as worn' (the head form is flush-cut with the shell at y=470, so nothing of the wearer is visible outside the helmet).

residuals: Composition: I shifted the helmet +80 rather than the requested +100. At +100 the chin bar's front (local x=656) lands at 736 and collides with the graph's requested 730 start. Even at +80 the left margin is 289 units against 38 on the right - a large quiet band. This is inherent to the brief's own numbers (helmet centred at 520 with r=190 puts its left edge at 330 while the graph starts at 720), so I followed the spec and accepted the imbalance rather than inventing a third composition.

Fingers are 85 units long, not the requested ~70. At the strap's achievable angle (the rear anchor is fixed to the shell's bottom-rear corner, so the arms cannot be steep), k = separation/tan(alpha-beta) puts the two crossings 24-26 units apart along the finger; at 70 units long the middle third is only 23 units and one crossing falls outside it. 85 units puts both crossings at 41% and 60%.

The head's jaw curve reads ABOVE the fingertips, not below them as the review's wording asked. Above is the anatomically correct arrangement and is what the shipped raster shows; the sandwich requirement is satisfied by the strap band passing over the fingers' middle third with the jaw immediately adjacent.

The chin bar's underside taper is about 10 units (y~451 at x=560 local, y~442 at x=640) rather than the requested 18. The whole chin bar had to be raised so its top edge sits level with the visor's lower edge - otherwise it read as a pouch hanging off the cheek - and that compressed the available taper.

The dashed ghost's midsection is hidden behind the impact block; only its two ends are visible (about 14 units at the rear, 40 at the front). Extending it further would put the dashes on top of the shell's real navy outline outside the dent, which reads as noise.

The pale head form is large relative to the shell (r=124 inside r=190) because the brief fixes the three bands at 14+40+12=66 units. The shipped raster's head is proportionally smaller (about 0.44 of the shell radius), so ours cannot match the raster's tighter enclosure without violating the band spec. I tried opening the face/jaw the way the raster does and it made the plate read as a green horseshoe over a pale blob, so I reverted and kept the shell covering down to the jaw band.

The chin bar still reads as a somewhat distinct mass from the cheek even though it is joined (its rear edge is a seam fully inside the dome's fill, verified by pixel scan - no paper gap at the junction). A first-time learner may still read it as a separate part rather than as one moulded shell.

defects.element: head form (path "head inside the helmet", global M520 182.6 … L550 486 C566 483, 582 476, 590 462 …) vs front shell lower rim (global 520,452 → 658,436) and chin-bar underside (global 646,450)

Between global x=520 and x=596 the pale #DEEDE5 jaw hangs 0–30 units BELOW the front shell's lower rim as a bare lens-shaped lobe sitting on paper, and the chin bar (global x 602–738) sits entirely to the RIGHT of the head (head x-max = 597) so there is an open white slot between the chin bar's underside and the jaw. Compounding it, the head has no ear, no neck and no chin point, so at the 350 px end (z_small350.png) the whole assembly reads as a fruit/egg cross-section with a hat on, not a worn helmet. Add an ear notch and a short neck stub below the section cut so the pale form reads as a head, not an egg.

defects.element: two gloved fingers (rect x=417 y=507 and rect x=417 y=533, rotate(22 466 530)) crossed by the front strap arm (path M415 548.2 L559.1 444.4 L570.8 460.6 L426.7 564.4 Z)

The front strap arm crosses both finger rects at ~58° near their mid-length, and strap and fingers share the identical treatment (#0D1E2E fill, 3-unit #46555A stroke), so the fingers are severed into four separate dark stubs. Counting the rounded ends in z_hand.png yields four bars, not two fingers. defects.element: gloved hand (path M494 536 C 490 519, … Z, global x 574–700, y 495–568) plus cuff rect x=510 y=542 w=108 h=26
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, every frame; crop z_hand.png (global x 480–720, y 470–600)
defects.what: S3 ("hands read as gloved hands", P1) fails. The shape renders as three unrelated masses: a smooth dark ball at the left, a striped dome with three seams to its right, and a long horizontal pill underneath that reads as a separate bar rather than a cuff. It has no wrist and no arm — it is a disembodied hand floating mid-plate with paper on all four sides, which §0.2 forbids ("People are whole bodies… never black silhouettes"). Its anatomy is also self-contradicting: three knuckle seams imply four folded fingers, and two more fingers extend from its left side, so the glove carries six digits' worth of structure. In the shipped raster the glove is one clear silhouette rising from the bottom edge.
defects.fix: Redraw as a single glove silhouette — back of hand, thumb pad, the two extended fingers continuous with it, and only ONE seam for the folded ring/little fingers — outlined in #0D1E2E, with the cuff attached (not overlapped) and the forearm running out to the bottom plate edge so it is not severed.

defects.element: dashed ghost of the original shell surface (path M336.6 175.4 A 190 190 0 0 1 496.6 110.7, #46555A 0.4 opacity, dasharray 8 6) under the impact block (global x 350–456, y 64–154)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, every frame; crops z_gL.png (global 320–400, 140–200) and z_gR.png (global 430–530, 90–160)
defects.what: The file's own <title> claims "a dashed ghost line marks where the shell surface used to be" and the source comment says "the gap between it and the flat IS the crush depth". The render delivers neither. The block covers the entire informative span, and at both exposed ends the ghost coincides with the drawn shell outline: at global x=336.6 the ghost is y=175.4 while the dented shell outer is y=170.4 (5 units), and at x=480 the ghost is y=110 while the shell is y≈112 (2 units). What actually renders is five or six pale grey ticks floating a couple of units off the outline (z_gL: three dashes; z_gR: two-plus dashes fading into the edge). Under §0.2 diagram hygiene those are unexplained ticks, and under U8 the alt text asserts teaching content the image does not carry.
defects.fix: Either shrink/offset the block (e.g. 60×60 pushed to the left half of the dent) so a continuous 14-unit gap between ghost and flat is exposed beside it, or redraw the ghost as a short arc that spans ONLY the dent and terminates where the gap is widest — never let it run out to where it collapses onto the shell outline. Two small radial tick marks bridging ghost-to-flat at the dent's centre would make the depth explicit.

defects.element: impact block (g class="hf-blk", rect 90×60 rx10 #46555A, rotate(-22 334.1 136.8), local bottom face from (292.4,153.7) to (375.8,119.9)) against the dented shell arc
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png (complete state, and every hold frame t=0–3s, 8s, 10s); crops z_block.png and z_gL.png
defects.what: The block's bottom face is a straight 90-unit chord of a circle at r≈181.7 while the dent it rests in is a smooth arc bottoming at r=176 — so the face touches at exactly one point (its midpoint) and stands off ≈5.7 units at both corners. z_gL.png shows the resulting white wedge under the block's left half, and its lower-left corner (r=181.7) sits OUTSIDE the ghost of the original surface it is supposed to have pushed past. It reads as a grey slab tipped and balanced on a corner rather than a mass pressed into a dent.
defects.fix: Replace the block's straight contact edge with a shallow arc matching the dent (or flatten the dent's centre 60 units to a true straight chord at r=176), then lower the block so the whole face is buried to depth — no paper visible between block and shell anywhere along the contact.

defects.element: un-crush overlay clip (clipPath #hf-cut, rect class="hf-cutr" x=252 y=-60 w=172 h=260) sliding translateY 0 → −100px over 58 %→65 %
defects.where: .frames.png frame t = 6 s (clip bottom edge ≈ y 155); reproduced in crop z_seam6.png (global x 420–780, y 180–420 of that frame)

At t=6s z_seam6.png shows a pale notch chopped into the magenta band and a 3-unit navy stroke-end dangling in the middle of the magenta fill where the patch's clipped arc simply stops. It reads as a rendering glitch / torn artwork (U5), and a straight wipe line is not what "the liner crushes" looks like.
defects.fix: Sweep the clip along the band instead of across it — use an arc-shaped or rotating-wedge clip that follows the dent's radial direction, or cross-fade the round and crushed crown groups over 400 ms. No straight clip edge may ever cross an outline.

defects.element: graph group (g class="hf-graph": baseline M742 470 H962, .hf-spike, .hf-hump), keyframes 44 %,62 % { opacity: 0 }

At t=5s the plate shows a helmet with no block and no graph: for about a second the animation carries no teaching content at all, and a quarter of the canvas is empty paper. §0.3: "a beat that could be cut without losing the point gets cut." The opacity fade is also redundant with the stroke-dashoffset reveal already on both curves.

defects.element: strap arms, buckle rect (407,537,34,34), the two finger rects, hand path and cuff rect — all stroke="#46555A" over fill="#0D1E2E"
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, every frame; crops z_strap.png, z_hand.png
defects.what: Every other element in the file is outlined in #0D1E2E; this whole cluster is outlined in ink-grey. At render scale the grey rim reads as a specular highlight, so the straps look like chromed rods and the glove like a moulded plastic part. §0.2 mandates one line language ("thick navy line"), and against the shipped batch-13 plates and keylist-tcloc this fails C1/C2 (one product by one hand). Source audit confirms three stroke colours in the file: #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #46555A.
defects.fix: Outline the strap, buckle, fingers, hand and cuff in #0D1E2E like everything else, and get the shape separation from fill value instead — e.g. #46555A fill for the fingers and cuff against #0D1E2E strap and glove, matching the raster where the glove is one dark mass read by silhouette, not by rim colour.

defects.element: crown state swap (.hf-cutr keyframes 48.9 % → 49 %, a 10 ms step from translateY(−100px) to translateY(0))
defects.where: between .frames.png t = 4 s (dented) and t = 5 s (round crown, f_t5.png) — the change lands at t ≈ 4.9 s
defects.what: With the block off-plate there is nothing on screen to motivate it, so the viewer sees the helmet's crown silently pop from dented back to perfectly round in one frame and stay round for a second before being re-crushed. Two problems: it is a pop, not motion the eye can follow (§0.3 motion law), and the loop as a whole depicts the liner recovering — the single misconception that the retirement rule exists to kill, on the plate that teaches it.
defects.fix: Do not restore the crown on-screen. Either hold the crushed state for the whole loop and animate only the block's approach against an already-dented crown, or run the swap while the crown itself is masked (e.g. fade the crown group to 0 for 200 ms behind the departing block), so no frame shows a helmet healing itself.

- "three layers distinct, magenta the thickest" — PASS at the intended ~700 px figure width. Measured 36.5 magenta / ~13 shell / ~17 pad. Below ~400 px the #ABCDB8 pad and the #DEEDE5 head collapse into one value, but 700 px is the intended size so this is a note, not a defect.
- "two fingers countable" — FAIL. Four stubs.
- "the crush is visible as a local dent in the magenta band only" — PARTIAL PASS. - "the hump-vs-spike reads without text" — PASS, weakly. The 0.35-opacity #46555A spike is a faint hairline at 700 px and effectively gone at 350 px, but the tall-narrow vs low-wide contrast survives.
