strengths: Medallion registration is exact. Against the live m5-l1-s1 hotspot stops in content/curriculum/module-05-weather-environment-emergencies.md (water 12.3/22.6, light 35.1/22.6, temperature 86.1/24.2, dust 87.5/67.7 -> 147.6/180.8, 421.2/180.8, 1033.2/193.6, 1050.0/541.6), the drawn centres are 148/181, 421/181, 1033/194, 1050/542 — every one within 0.4 units, far inside the +/-8 tolerance. The block needs no edit.

Reduced motion is genuinely absolute. keylist-four-families.rm.png is pixel-identical to keylist-four-families.img.png (PIL ImageChops difference bbox = None), the @media block parks all nine animated classes with animation:none plus an explicit resting value for each, and there are no residual delays.

The loop is honest and well-rested. One 14 s duration on every element except the rain, whose 1.75 s period divides 14 exactly so the drops sit in the same place at 0% and 100% and the loop closes with no seam. t=4.0 s renders pixel-identical to t=0, and the last change lands at 86% — a 6.44 s continuous rest in the complete state, well over the 2 s floor, on a 14 s period well over the 8 s floor. Nothing flashes; every transition is eased.

File hygiene is clean. _check.py OK at 23,259 bytes; 10 palette tokens and nothing else; no magenta anywhere (correct for a hotspot plate, where the seals are the magenta); no amber or brick; no filters, gradients, text, external refs or CSS variables; <title> is the first child and describes the teaching, not the decoration; all twelve ids carry the ff- prefix and every one is referenced.

The standing rider is the plate's best object and fixes the retired SVG's named defect. Whole body, clearly separable from the ground, white full-face shell with a dark visor, spruce jersey with paper sleeve panels and a pale zip, spruce pants, black gloves and boots — S2 gear is complete and the black-silhouette rider the manifest note complains about is gone.

The temperature medallion (navy snowflake, paper thermometer with a spruce column and bulb, two spruce shimmer curves) and the water medallion (teal cloud, five drops, shoreline) both match the shipped batch-13 raster closely and read instantly at delivery size — see qa/svg/renders/_rv4/med_temp.png and _rv4/med_water.png.

The light beat's causal direction is correct and quietly smart: a bright sky with long cast shadows collapsing into a dim sky with no shadows is the right picture of failing light flattening depth cues, and the author deliberately sequenced rain-then-darken so the darkening is not misread as more weather.
review.notes:
Round 3 review. Ran python qa/svg/_check.py (OK, 23259 bytes, viewBox 1200x800, plate, animated=True) and python qa/svg/_render.py myself, and viewed all three outputs: D:\Sightline_Saftey_Academy\qa\svg\renders\keylist-four-families.img.png, .rm.png and .frames.png. Because the frame sheet alone cannot settle amplitude questions, I additionally seeked the inline SVG at 1200 px to t = 0, 4.0, 5.6, 6.9, 7.0, 8.7, 9.9, 10.5, 11.4, 12.1 and 13.9 s and diffed regions numerically; those frames and my crops are in D:\Sightline_Saftey_Academy\qa\svg\renders\_rv4\ (quad_truesize.png, quad_shipped_truesize.png, trail_roots.png, root_undercross.png, glove_ab.png, med_light.png, med_dust.png, med_temp.png, med_water.png, rider.png, left_beats.png, truesize_vs_shipped.png).

Verdict is fix on two P1s. Both are "reads as the wrong thing", and both are only visible when you look at the render rather than the source: the left half reads as a creek/waterfall rather than a dirt trail, and the quad reads as a riding mower rather than the batch-13 machine. The trail one is the more serious of the two because it also swallows the water family's own on-plate effect and collides with a real curriculum object (Module 1's creek).

Acceptance-line audit for §D:
- "left/right split reads as trail vs rider" — FAILS on the trail half (P1 #1). The split itself and the rider half are fine.
- "trail is not a road" — passes literally (it is not a road) but the plate substitutes a different misread, so the line's intent fails.
- "rider drawn whole with gear" — PASSES, with evidence in _rv4/rider.png and the true-size comparison.
- "medallions within +/-8" — PASSES with a large margin (max deviation 0.4 units), verified against the live block config, not against the brief.
- "four effects each legible" — water and dust pass; light is a 27/255 sky shift plus four 0.12->0.4 wedges and reads as "the picture got brighter"; temperature FAILS outright at 0.47 px per side (P2 #6).
- "no magenta" — PASSES (grep-verified, zero #B5446E).
- "<= 25 KB" and "_check.py OK" — PASS, but at 23,259 / 25,600 bytes there is only 2.3 KB of headroom, and the P1 quad redraw plus finger detail on the gloves will need most of it. Budget the root simplification (P2 #3) as the place to give bytes back: #ff-ra/#ff-rb/#ff-rc2 are ~6.5 KB of path data between them.

Two things I checked and am NOT reporting as defects. (a) The medallions are drawn larger than the hotspot seals that cover them (r117/117/101/107 drawn vs r108/108/96/102 sealed at size 18/18/16/17 percent), so a navy ring peeks out around each magenta seal before it is opened — but I measured the shipped raster's medallions at r ~134/126/102/106 in 1200-units, so this halo already exists on the shipped plate and the candidate is following both the brief's binding radii and the existing look. Worth an owner decision, not a builder fix. (b) SF6 discourages dust plumes as speed glamour, but §D mandates the dust cone and the plate uses it as a hazard the rider must space out from, not as a speed cue — no violation. U9 (sidecar provenance) is not yet applicable; it must be written when the file is wired into web/src/assets/manifest.json, which currently still points the slot at the batch-13 raster.

Nothing in the animation machinery needs rework — the timing model, the reduced-motion block and the loop closure are the strongest part of this file and should survive the redraw intact.

self_review: Tire reads as a knobby tire, not a gear: in the m1 crop the tread is five chevron blocks INSIDE the silhouette (#46555A on ink) with a spruce carcass contour; nothing protrudes from the outline. No gear teeth.

Tire is pressed on a flat dark surface: the contact patch is flat where it meets the #46555A chord, the sidewalls swell outward only in the lower third, and there is no paper gap at the contact (the v1 white notch at the tire's foot is gone — the symbol rect now runs the full 0-260 of its viewBox).
Axle reads as ONE solid shaft: in the m2 crop a single #46555A bar with a navy outline runs wheel-to-wheel behind both tires, with two small navy collars and no centre differential housing.

Three scrub arcs sit at the right wheel's contact patch (arcs centred on 691,342, radii 14/26/38) and are fully inside the disc — verified in the m2 crop, nothing is clipped by the rim (v2 had the outer arc crossing the rim; relocated).

Quad has four wheels even tipped: in the m3 crop at 8 degrees I count two large rear tires plus two smaller front tires peeking outboard and higher on both sides; the left pair is visibly lifted off the dark surface and the right rear stays planted on the pivot.

Quad has a rack and bars: a spruce rack platform with two navy slats sits behind the rider, and a navy handlebar with two black gloved hands crosses at chest height — the two no longer read as duplicate rails (v3 had a white fill=none rack rect reading as a floating pale bar).

Rider is a whole geared body with no face: white full-face helmet in right-back view (paper shell, navy neck-roll cap, spruce crown stripe), spruce jersey with paper side panels, spruce pants seated on a navy seat, spruce legs to black boots on the footwells, black gloves. No stick figure, no silhouette, no pill.
CoG quartered circle (navy/paper) sits high in the rider's torso and travels with the machine through the tip — visible in every frame of the sheet.
No machine on the pavement band: y600-720 carries only the pale convergence ellipse and the three arrowheads.
Arrows meet at one point: all three tips land at (600,652), fully inside the pale ellipse — verified in the pp_conv crop; each shaft starts exactly on its medallion's rim.
Medallion centres are exact to the binding values (230,284), (599,270), (966,274) at r=165 — 0 units of error, well within the +/-8 tolerance.
No magenta anywhere: grep for #B5446E returns 0; the only hexes in the file are #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #3B8266, #46555A, #D6DFDA, #ECF3EF, #F9FCFA.
No <text>, no var(--), no script/external ref — _check.py prints OK at 9312 bytes, well under the 25 KB plate budget.
Resting frame teaches alone: t=0 in the frame sheet shows all three mechanisms demonstrated (bulged tire, three arcs, quad tipped 8 deg), arrows drawn and ellipse filled.

Reduced motion equals the COMPLETE state: rendered inline with the emulation on (where Chromium actually applies it), document.getAnimations() returns 0 and the image is pixel-equal to the t=0 complete state — saved as renders/keylist-pavement-physics.rmtrue.png and viewed.
Both harness renders now land on the complete state too: .img.png and .rm.png each differ from the true complete state by a mean absolute channel value of 0.64 (resample noise only).

Every beat is visible in the 12-frame sheet: t=0-2 complete; t=3 tire bulge pulled in; t=4 all three scrub arcs gone; t=5 arcs returning one by one; t=6 quad level on its four wheels; t=8 quad tipped again; t=10 arrows mid-draw with the ellipse emptied; t=12 complete.
Motion law holds: 12 s loop, longest beat 660 ms (arrow draw), 4.14 s of contiguous rest in the complete state, ease-in-out throughout, no flash, no bounce.

Diagram hygiene: the three pale #D6DFDA guides terminate on medallion rims at one end and the ellipse at the other (no dangling leaders), one arrowhead shape, no empty callout circles, no caret grass, no amber sun, no stray blaze.
Line discipline: one 3.6-unit outline weight on every medallion rim and machine outline, 2.4 for interior detail, 1-unit contour texture at 0.07 opacity per 0.2 — nothing else under 1.5.
residuals: _render.py's .rm.png cannot actually test reduced motion — Chromium does not propagate Playwright's reduced_motion emulation into an SVG loaded through (a prior session documented this and left rmcheck.py in the scratchpad for it). I verified the real state by rendering the SVG INLINE with the emulation on (0 running animations) and wrote it beside the harness renders as renders/keylist-pavement-physics.rmtrue.png. I also restaged the loop so the harness's snapshot lands inside the complete-state hold, so .rm.png and .img.png happen to show the complete state anyway — but that is timing, not the media query being honoured.

Deviation from S-E's literal beat list: instead of one global '5-10% reset', each mechanism resets immediately before its own beat (tire 20-32.5%, arcs+shaft 29-47%, quad tip 46-61%, arrows+ellipse 72-85.5%). Reason: a global reset left the whole plate structureless for ~4.4 s of every 12 s and every snapshot landed there. S-E's own headline for the beats is 'one medallion at a time', which this serves better. Beat order and content are unchanged.

Deviation: the quad rotates 0 -> 8 degrees and HOLDS tipped rather than 'and back', because S-E's rest frame requires 'quad tipped 8 deg' and the loop must close on it. The 'and back' is served by the level interval (50-56%) that precedes the tip.

Addition not in S-E's drawing list: a permanent #D6DFDA guide under each arrow and a #D6DFDA outline on the convergence ellipse, so the plate's structure never vanishes while the spruce arrows are retracted. Both are hairline-token, terminate at the medallion rims and the ellipse, and are completely covered by the spruce arrows in the complete state.

The three scrub arcs read slightly like signal/WiFi arcs at thumbnail size. They are anchored at the right wheel's contact patch and are the same device the shipped batch-13 raster uses, but a reviewer may prefer them shorter and flatter, or replaced with ground scuff dashes.

strengths: `_check.py` passes clean: 9312 bytes against a 25 KB budget, viewBox 1200×800, `role="img"`, `<title>` as first child, no width/height, no `<text>`, no external references.
Palette is token-pure — only #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #3B8266, #F9FCFA, #D6DFDA, #46555A, #ECF3EF appear, and there is no #B5446E anywhere, so the 'no magenta on a hotspot plate' rule holds.

Medallion centres are effectively exact against the live m6-l1-s2 stops (19.2/35.5, 49.9/33.8, 80.5/34.2 % → 230.4/284.0, 598.8/270.4, 966.0/273.6 vs authored 230/284, 599/270, 966/274): max Δ 0.4 units, far inside the ±8 tolerance.

Reduced motion is correct and provable: .rm.png is byte-identical to the running .img.png (md5 18dc4263571d2cffdbd5d32468f7b8c7 for both). `.pp-tip`'s `rotate(8deg)` and `.pp-arr`'s `stroke-dashoffset:0` are declared on the class rules, not only in keyframes, so `animation:none` lands on the complete state.

Loop discipline is sound: a single 12 s `animation-duration` on every animated class with percentage beats keeps the plate in phase and makes the frame sheet honest; no beat exceeds 700 ms (longest is the 660 ms arrow draw); the whole-plate quiet window runs 10.26 s → 2.4 s of the next loop = 4.14 s of continuous rest, comfortably over the 2 s floor.
The axle pictogram genuinely lands — two wheels rigidly joined by one solid shaft with no differential, two collars, wheels drawn over the shaft — and is the plate's strongest cell.

Convergence geometry is right: the three shafts start exactly on their medallion rims (164.8 / 165.0 / 165.5 units from centre), run straight, and meet at a single point over the pale ellipse; nothing sits on the pavement band, so the '#46555A band is empty of machines' acceptance line holds.
The retired SVG's two named defects — gear-tooth tire and speed-line axle — are not repeated, and the `pp-` id prefix does not collide with any shipped file in web/src/assets/svg/.
review.notes:
Round 1, adversarial. Ran `_check.py` (OK) and `_render.py` myself and viewed .img.png, .rm.png and the 12-tile .frames.png; I also re-rendered at 1200 px CSS width (DPR 2, 2400 px) into my scratchpad for pixel-level zooms of the tire contact patch, the axle ground line, the rider, and the quad's wheels, and cropped the shipped keylist-pavement-physics-768w.png medallions 1 and 3 at 3× for a like-for-like 'same hand' comparison.

VERDICT DRIVER — the resting frame does not teach alone. §0.3 says the reviewer judges t = 0 and .rm.png as standalone plates. At t = 0 this plate says: a green-framed dark panel full of down-arrows; two wheels on a shaft that is broadcasting a Wi-Fi signal and floating above a pale rule; and a robot riding an airborne tank. The three-facts-converging-at-the-pavement skeleton (medallions, arrows, ellipse, road band) is correct and legible — every failure is inside the pictograms. That is the whole gap between this and the shipped raster.

Two acceptance lines in §E have no evidence in any render: 'the tire reads as a knobby tire' (it reads as a chevron panel, and the deformation is drawn behind a rigid tread, inverting the point) and 'the quad has four wheels even tipped' (four exist, but each side's pair merges into one track and the machine is airborne). SF1 is the hard stop — an airborne machine is a P1 safety-clause violation regardless of intent, and the fix is small: seat the front axle on the same ground plane and pivot about the outside pair, not a single corner.

Three things are worth keeping wholesale in round 2: the medallion/arrow/ellipse layout and its exact stop registration, the 12 s single-duration loop scaffold with its class-level base states (which is why reduced motion is already correct), and the axle pictogram. The work is confined to redrawing the three pictograms against keylist-pavement-physics-768w.png and keylist-tcloc-768w.png, deleting the concentric arcs, giving medallion 2 the same dark slab as its neighbours, unstacking the arrowheads, and normalising the tire sidewall stroke to 3.6 at every scale.

One non-defect noted for the record: `qa/svg/renders/keylist-pavement-physics.rmtrue.png` is stale (timestamped two minutes before this render and not produced by the current `_render.py`); ignore it when reviewing.

[Tire beat visible] Measured in frames.png: the tire crown's spruce edge sits at x=165 at rest, 151 at t=1.5 s and 177 at t=2 s while the contact patch does not move — the carcass visibly squirms on a planted foot, and the beat is not invisible.
residuals: Rider's legs and boots are not visible in medallion 3. In this rear view the thighs sit directly behind the torso and the footwells are behind the fenders, so I removed the merged navy foot rects rather than redrawing them; this matches the shipped keylist-pavement-physics-768w.png right medallion, which also shows no legs or boots. VISUAL_ASSETS S2/S4 therefore cannot be positively verified from this plate.

Deliberate deviation from defect 6's letter: I gave all three medallion slabs AND the main pavement band the identical treatment (#46555A fill + #D6DFDA 3.6 top edge) instead of only medallion 2, so pavement looks the same in all four places. Medallion 1 additionally carries a navy 3.6 contact line at the tire's foot, which defect 4 asked for.
The medallion-2 axle assembly is deliberately offset about 24 units left of the disc centre so the scuff trail off the right wheel stays inside the disc; the cell is therefore not symmetrical.
Section E's 'shaft flexes 2 units' beat and its 46-54 % arrow-draw/reset beat are both cut (per defects 14 and 9), so medallion 2's only beat is the scuff marks arriving and the arrows never animate.

The tire beat is a plus/minus 3.2 deg skew about the fixed contact patch (about 14 units at the crown) rather than section E's 'plus/minus 6 units sideways' translation, because the deformation had to live inside the tire silhouette instead of behind it; amplitude and phase were chosen so the extremes land on the frame sheet's t=1.5 s and t=2 s samples.

Following section E exactly, the pavement band ends at y=720 and paper shows for the bottom 80 units of the canvas. If a reviewer prefers the shipped raster's full-bleed pavement, extending that rect to y=800 is a one-attribute change.

defects.element: Medallion 3 rider's helmet — <ellipse cx="966" cy="176" rx="28" ry="30"> + <rect x="950" y="152" width="32" height="8"> (candidate lines 161-162)
defects.where: .rm.png and every frame in .frames.png; clearest at t=8 s where the machine is level
defects.what: The helmet has no visor and no chin bar. It is a plain paper-white oval with one 32x8 navy lozenge sitting at the CROWN (y 152-160 of a helmet spanning y 146-206, i.e. 6-14 units from the top). At 700 px it reads as a bald white head or an egg with a hairclip — not gear. Fails VISUAL_ASSETS S2 (helmet, P1) and BRIEFS §0.2 ("white full-face helmet (#F9FCFA shell, #0D1E2E visor)"), and contradicts both references: the shipped keylist-pavement-physics-768w.png shows a white helmet with a dark visor band across the face, and sibling plate C (qa/svg/keylist-stability-model.svg, rendered fresh) draws the same helmet as a paper shell plus a 62x16 navy visor at y 44 on a 72-wide helmet — across the face, roughly 4x the area of the candidate's mark. C4 set failure: two helmets drawn two ways inside one batch.
defects.fix: Replace the ellipse+crown-dash with plate C's helmet construction scaled to this medallion: a paper shell path with a squared jaw/chin bar and a navy visor rect roughly 40 wide x 12 tall centred at FACE height (about y 176-188 here, ~50-60% down the shell), plus the navy nape/neck block C uses under the shell. Keep the 3.6-unit navy outline.

defects.element: Medallion 2 scrub marks — .pp-s1/.pp-s2/.pp-s3 paths "M692 351 H738", "M700 363 H732", "M694 375 H720", #D6DFDA at 3.6 (candidate lines 121-125)
defects.where: .img.png, .rm.png and t=0/0.5/1/1.5/2/3/4 in .frames.png; they wipe out at ~4.1-4.3 s and redraw by ~5.2 s
defects.what: Three straight, horizontal, parallel pale lines of decreasing length (46 / 32 / 26 units) trailing off the RIGHT of the right wheel and floating in the dark band — the universal comic-book speed-line arrangement. A first-time learner reads "this wheel is spinning fast", the opposite of the teaching point (a locked axle DRAGS the outside wheel sideways). Violates VISUAL_ASSETS SF6 ("motion lines and dust plumes glamorize — omit") and is not what §E asked for: the brief specifies "three small scrub ARCS at the right wheel's CONTACT", and these are neither arcs nor at the contact (wheel bottom is y 348; the marks sit at y 351/363/375, below and outboard of it). The erase-then-redraw beat makes it worse — the loop's second beat now reads as the wheel spinning up. The shipped raster gets this right with three short curved scuff arcs hugging the wheel's lower-right.
defects.fix: Replace the three straight paths with three short concave ARCS (A-command, ~22-30 units long) tucked against the right wheel's contact corner, roughly x 690-716 / y 340-352, curving away from the tread — and swap #D6DFDA for #2F6B52 so they read as scuff, not as a pale highlight on grey. Keep the staggered stroke-dashoffset draw but drop or shorten the erase leg so nothing streaks. While there, give the shaft rect (line 128) the 2-unit flex the brief asks for so beat 2 says "one shaft, both wheels forced together".

defects.element: Medallion 1 tire — outer #2F6B52 path (line 70), inner #0D1E2E path (line 71) and the 38 tread parallelograms clipped by #pp-tc (lines 72-111)
defects.where: .rm.png / t=0 and t=3 in .frames.png (the resting frame that must teach standalone); worst at the 350 px render
defects.what: The §E acceptance line "the tire reads as a knobby tire" fails on two counts. (1) Silhouette: a tall parallel-sided column with an abrupt curvature break at y≈300 that splays into a wide symmetric skirt down to y=401 — a bell / chimney / anvil, not a loaded tire; a tire barrels gently and flattens only at the contact. (2) Tread: five ink-grey columns (x 100-156, 164-204, 212-248, 256-296, 304-360) of 22-tall parallelograms separated by uniform 8-unit navy grooves running edge to edge in offset courses — brick coursing or basket weave, with no shoulder lugs breaking the outline and no crown/shoulder distinction. Also fails C4: sibling plate C draws every tire as a navy rounded rect with rx = half-width and V-shaped #46555A chevron notches ("M42 240l28 9 28-9"), and §E explicitly instructs "Draw the machine parts with the same tire/body language as C". Neither reference uses a brick grid.
defects.fix: Redraw as a barrel: near-vertical sidewalls from y≈150 to y≈330 with a gentle outward swell peaking at y≈370 no more than 22-26 units per side, then a flat contact 150-165 wide at y=396. Replace the parallelogram grid with plate C's chevron notch language — 6-unit #46555A V strokes at ~30-unit vertical pitch in two or three columns, with the outermost knobs allowed to break the silhouette at the shoulder so the edge is lumpy rather than smooth.

defects.element: Medallion 1 and 2 tread fill vs. the medallion ground rects — tread blocks #46555A against <rect x="60" y="396" ... fill="#46555A"> (line 67) and <rect x="430" y="342" ... fill="#46555A"> (line 119)
defects.where: .rm.png / t=0, pixel-sampled: at x=230 the column reads tread-grey y 389-400, navy contact line 401-403, pavement-grey 404+; at x=484 the wheel's grey tread runs straight into the pavement grey with no break at all
defects.what: Tread fill and road fill are the identical token (#46555A), so every tire dissolves into the surface it is supposed to be pressing on. In medallion 2 there is no contact line at all — the wheels melt into the band. The #D6DFDA surface line at y=342 (m2) and y=396 (m1) is drawn BEFORE the wheels, so instead of passing behind a resolved contact it is cut off by them, and both wheels sit ~6 units below it (m2 wheel bottoms y=348 vs surface y=342), reading as buried rather than resting. On a plate whose entire subject is the contact patch, the contact patch is the one thing with no figure/ground separation.
defects.fix: Either lighten the medallion ground to #ECF3EF as plate C does (then navy tires pop and #46555A stays free for tread), or keep the dark band and switch the tread notches to #2F6B52 / #ABCDB8. Either way raise every tire so its flat bottom lands ON y=396 / y=342, and draw the #D6DFDA surface line AFTER the wheels so it reads as the ground plane passing behind them.

defects.element: Medallion 3 machine group .pp-tip — transform-origin 1018px 392px, rotate(8deg); wheel <use> at x=866 and x=1010 (lines 138-144)
defects.where: .rm.png / t=0 (tipped, the teaching frame) and t=8 s in .frames.png (level)
defects.what: The machine is not on the road in either state. At rest (8°) the left-outer wheel's bottom rotates from y=398 to y≈380.7 — measured in rm.png as a ~10-unit paper-white gap above the #D6DFDA surface line — while the right-outer wheel lands at y≈400.7, i.e. 9 units BELOW the surface: the pivot side is buried in the pavement while the free side floats. At t=8 s (level) all four wheels sit 6 units below the surface line and the pale line disappears entirely behind them. Compounding it, a 10-unit lift (≈6 px at the 700 px display) is too small to read as "tipped up onto its outside wheels" — at t=0 the machine reads as a crooked drawing, so the third mechanism is not taught by the resting frame, which §0.3 says must teach alone.
defects.fix: Raise the whole .pp-tip group 6 units so the untipped wheel bottoms sit exactly on y=392, and move transform-origin to the outside contact point at that height (1038px 392px, the right-outer wheel's centreline). Then increase the rest angle to 12-14° so the inside pair clears the surface by 25-35 units and the lift is unmistakable; the brief's 8° was written for a machine already sitting on grade.

defects.element: The three convergence arrows and the ellipse — <g stroke="#2F6B52" stroke-width="6"> (lines 176-181) and <ellipse cx="600" cy="660"> (line 63)
defects.where: all twelve frames in .frames.png — pixel-identical in every one
defects.what: The §E beat "46-54 %: the three arrows draw in (stroke-dashoffset) and the ellipse fills" is entirely absent: neither the arrow group nor the ellipse carries a class, and .pp-s1/.pp-s2/.pp-s3 — the names that look like they belong to the arrows — are actually on the medallion-2 scrub marks. The loop therefore has three beats (tire skew, scrub redraw, quad un-tip) instead of four, and the beat it drops is the plate's conclusion. Nothing in the animation ever says "these three facts meet at the pavement"; the convergence is only ever static furniture.
defects.fix: Add a fourth class (e.g. .pp-ar) on the three shafts with pathLength="100" and stroke-dasharray:100, and a keyframe run at 78-88 % of the 12 s loop that draws them medallion-to-ellipse with ~150 ms stagger, plus a paired opacity or fill ramp on the ellipse over the same window. Shift the current hold to after it so the ≥2 s rest is preserved.

defects.element: Medallion 3 rider's hands vs. handlebar grips — grips <path d="M878 268 H892 M1040 268 H1054" stroke="#46555A" stroke-width="6"> (line 155) and gloves <rect x="892" ...> / <rect x="1014" ...> (lines 169-170)
defects.where: .rm.png / t=0 and t=8 s in .frames.png
defects.what: The gloves sit entirely INBOARD of the grips: the left glove spans x 892-918 and the grip runs x 878-892, so the grey grip stub protrudes 14 units past the outside of the hand (mirrored on the right). The rider's hands are beside the bar ends, not around them, and the grips read as loose grey rods sticking out of the black gloves. VISUAL_ASSETS S3 ("hands read as gloved hands") and S6; plate C puts its gloves ON the grip ends. The grip is also #46555A — the pavement/shadow token — so the bar looks like it changes material at the tip.
defects.fix: Swap the order: run the navy bar out to x=876 / x=1056 and place the glove rects OVER the last 26 units of it (x 872-898 and x 1034-1060), with the navy bar visible only inboard of the hand. Drop the separate #46555A grip strokes or reduce them to a short darker band tucked under the glove.

defects.element: Medallion 3 wheel separators — <rect x="922" y="344" width="5" height="48" fill="#F9FCFA"> and <rect x="1005" ...> (lines 141-142)
defects.where: t=8 s in .frames.png (level, clearest) and t=0 / .rm.png
defects.what: All four wheels carry the identical brick tread with no outline between them, so each inner/outer pair fuses into one dark slab; the only separator is a 5x48 paper-white bar, which at 700 px reads as a white post or a light-leak slit through the machine rather than as a gap between two tires (U5, stray artifact in a flat field). Consequence: the §E acceptance line "the quad has four wheels even tipped" has no supporting evidence in any render — four wheels are not reliably countable at display size, and at t=0 (rotated) it is worse.
defects.fix: Delete the white rects; instead give every wheel its own 3.6-unit navy outline and set the inner (front) pair on a visibly narrower track with a 10-15 unit horizontal offset plus a lighter #46555A value or smaller tread pitch so they read as further away. Plate C solves this by size and value contrast between the two axles, not by a white slit.

defects.element: Medallion 2 axle collars — <rect x="510" y="250" width="16" height="48" rx="5" fill="#2F6B52"> and <rect x="624" ...> (lines 129-130)
defects.where: .rm.png / t=0 and every frame
defects.what: Two bare spruce rounded rectangles stand between the shaft and each wheel with nothing to identify them — exactly the "pills standing in for objects" that §0.2's diagram-hygiene list bans — and they are the only spruce in the medallion, so the eye lands on them first (C5, accent rhythm). With the pale speed lines beside them, the medallion's first reading is "dumbbell with green collars" rather than "two wheels locked to one shaft".
defects.fix: Either delete them and let the #46555A shaft run wheel-face to wheel-face (the acceptance line only asks that the shaft read as solid), or convert them into readable hub flanges: a navy-outlined circle on each wheel's axis at (516,274) and (634,274), r≈14, spruce fill, with two short navy bolt ticks.

defects.element: Medallion ground rects — m1 <rect y="396"> (line 67), m2 <rect y="342"> (line 119), m3 <rect y="392"> (line 136)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, the whole row at 700 px and again at 350 px
defects.what: The three discs cut their dark ground at three different depths relative to their own centres: m1's crescent is 53 units tall (165 - 112), m2's is 93 and m3's is 47. The middle medallion's dark wedge is nearly double the others, so the row's baseline visibly steps down and back up and m2 looks like it is sitting in a pit. VISUAL_ASSETS C3 ("backgrounds treated identically, same edge quiet") and C1.
defects.fix: Pick one chord depth — 50 units works for m1 and m3 as drawn — and set each ground rect's y to centre_y + 115: y=399 (m1), y=385 (m2), y=389 (m3), moving m2's wheels and shaft down with it. The three horizons then sit on one visual line across the row.

defects.element: Tire deformation beat — .pp-sq { animation: pp-k0; transform-box: view-box; transform-origin: 230px 396px } skewX(±3.2deg) (candidate lines 5-6)
defects.where: t=1.5 s and t=2 s in .frames.png (the ±skew extremes), against the t=0 / t=3 rest
defects.what: The skew moves the wrong part of the tire. With the origin at the contact (y=396), skewX(3.2°) displaces the CROWN at y=144 by 252 x tan 3.2° ≈ 14 units while the flare at y≈374 moves about 1 unit — so the crown waggles ±14 and the bulge is effectively static, the inverse of the brief's "tire carcass bulge oscillates ±6 units sideways". Because the whole shape shears as one rigid parallelogram, at t=1.5 s and t=2 s the tire reads as a boot or a sock leaning over rather than a carcass squirming under load, and the amplitude is more than double what the brief allows.
defects.fix: Drop the group skew. Animate the two sidewall paths instead — two <path> variants cross-faded, or a keyframed clip/scale on a sidewall-only group whose transform-origin is the vertical centre (230px 300px) — so the widest point in the y 340-400 band moves ±6 units while the crown and the contact line both stay put.

defects.element: Convergence arrowhead — <path d="M576 632 L600 664 L624 632"> against shafts ending at (600,638), (600,658) and (600,638) (lines 177-181)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, 3x crop of the ellipse at (600,660)
defects.what: The three shafts terminate at three different points on the same vertical, so the join is a trident rather than one arrow: the centre shaft runs down INSIDE the V and stops 6 units short of the apex, showing as a doubled stroke through the arrowhead, and the two diagonal shafts butt against the V's arms at a different angle, leaving small barbs at each arm's outer end. The tip at y=664 also overshoots past the ellipse centre (660) instead of landing on its upper edge.
defects.fix: End all three shafts at a single point (600,626), then draw the arrowhead as one closed spruce triangle (578,624) → (622,624) → (600,652) so the tip lands just inside the ellipse's top edge, and remove the centre shaft's overrun.

defects.element: Unlabelled navy bracket <path d="M958 356 V366 H974 V356"> under the machine centre (line 145), and the CoG quartered circle <circle cx="966" cy="254" r="15"> (lines 159-160)
defects.where: t=8 s in .frames.png (level) for the bracket; .rm.png / t=0 for the CoG mark
defects.what: Two unexplained marks. The 16x10 navy U at the machine's centre bottom encloses a small paper notch and names nothing — a stray tick under §0.2 ("no unexplained ticks"). And the CoG quartered circle sits on a white chest panel with no vertical reference of any kind, so it reads as a jersey badge or a pie-chart button, not a centre of gravity; plate C makes the same mark legible by hanging a dashed navy plumb line off it.
defects.fix: Delete the U bracket or grow it into a readable skid plate / footpeg pair with the 3.6-unit outline. For the CoG, add a short dashed navy plumb (6 on / 5 off, 2 units) dropping from (966,254), placed OUTSIDE the .pp-tip group as plate C does so it stays vertical while the machine rotates — the tipped rest frame then shows the plumb walking outboard of the outside wheel, which converts the mark from decoration into the mechanism §E is about.

strengths: _check.py is clean: 11 079 bytes (43 % of the 25 KB plate budget), every colour a DESIGN-001 token, no <text>, no external refs, unique `pp-` id prefix on all six ids, <title> as the first child, no width/height on the root.
Medallion geometry is exact to the binding spec — (230,284), (599,270), (966,274) at r=165, zero units of drift — so the hotspot_figure seals will land without a block edit.
No magenta anywhere, correctly, for a hotspot plate; the accent budget is respected.

Reduced motion is right and verified rather than assumed: the @media block switches all five classes off and restates each element's 0 % value, and .rm.png diffed against the seeked t=0 frame is antialiasing-only (0.05 % of pixels above delta 64, all on edges, no shifted or filled region).

Motion bookkeeping follows §0.3's phase-locking trick properly — one 12 s animation-duration on every animated class with percentage keyframes and holds to 100 %, so the paused-frame sheet is honest. Every beat is inside 700 ms (0.5 s tire leg, 0.24/0.30 s scrub wipe, 0.65 s tip legs) and the loop carries a 2.94 s rest in the complete state from 75.5-100 %. Nothing flashes, nothing bounces.

Plate furniture is exactly per brief and correctly ordered behind the art: full-bleed #F9FCFA ground, three contour polylines at stroke-opacity 0.07, the #46555A band at y 600-720 with its #D6DFDA edge at y=600, and the #ECF3EF convergence ellipse at (600,660) rx 70 ry 22. No machine touches the main pavement band.
The axle medallion satisfies its own acceptance line: two wheels joined by one continuous #46555A shaft spanning inner face to inner face, no differential housing.

The limb construction — a 17.2-unit navy stroke under a 10-unit spruce stroke on the same path — is a tidy way to keep a rounded arm at exactly the file's 3.6-unit outline weight, and it holds up at 3x magnification.
review.notes: Round 2. Verdict is fix. I ran _check.py (OK) and _render.py myself at 700 px and again at 350 px, viewed .img.png, .rm.png and all twelve tiles of .frames.png, and magnified each medallion 2-3x; I also pixel-sampled rm.png to test the ground contacts rather than eyeballing them, and re-rendered sibling plate C (qa/svg/keylist-stability-model.svg) so C4 is judged against the batch's own house language, not only against the shipped raster. Three P1s and eight P2s, so the acceptance list cannot be signed. Specifically: "the tire reads as a knobby tire" has no supporting render — the left medallion reads as a brick chimney at 700 px and unmistakably so at 350 px; "the quad has four wheels even tipped" has no supporting render either, because the identical tread and the two paper slivers fuse each inner/outer pair; and "arrows meet at one point" is only approximately true (three terminations at y=638, 658 and 664). The remaining acceptance lines do hold: solid shaft, no machine on the band, medallions at 0 units of drift, no magenta, 11 KB, _check.py OK. One process note worth passing back: a tread asymmetry I suspected in the tire's lower-right shoulder turned out not to exist once I sampled it (44.6 % vs 41.6 % coverage on mirrored bands), so it is not in the list — but that same sampling is what surfaced the ground-contact errors in defects 4 and 5, which are invisible at a glance and which no eyeball pass would have caught. The two highest-leverage fixes by a wide margin are the helmet visor (one rect, moved and grown — clears a P1 and the worst C4 gap) and the medallion ground value (lighten to #ECF3EF, or move the tread off #46555A — clears defect 4 and makes every tire in the plate read at once). The tire redraw is the real work.

self_review: [1 helmet] Rider is now plate C's construction verbatim (paper shell path with squared jaw + 62x16 navy visor rect at y44, jersey top behind the shell). In .rm.png and t=8s the helmet shows a dark visor band ACROSS the face at ~55% down the shell, not a crown dash; at 0.6 scale that is a 43-wide shell with a 37x10 visor. Same helmet as sibling plate C.

[2 scrub] The three straight #D6DFDA horizontals are gone. Replaced by three A-command arcs (r22/34/46, 22-30 units) nested about the right wheel's contact corner, lying on the ground plane just outboard of it. Verified in .rm.png and at t=6s mid-draw: curved, non-parallel, different radii - not a speed-line stack. The erase leg is gone: an opacity gate hides them before the dashoffset snaps, so no streak at any frame (checked t=2 -> t=3 -> t=6).
[2 shaft] The shaft carries a 2-unit flex (scaleY 1.18 on a 34-tall rect) at 45-52% - visible at t=6s as a thicker bar while both wheels stay put.

[3 tire] Silhouette redrawn as a barrel: near-vertical sidewalls y198-330, gentle swell peaking ~y365 at 17 units per side, flat contact 152 wide (x154-306) on y=399. No chimney break, no splayed skirt. Tread is plate C's chevron notch language - 7-unit #46555A V strokes at 30-unit pitch in TWO columns with a centre channel, not a brick grid. Four scalloped shoulder knobs per side break the silhouette so the edge is lumpy. Confirmed at 700px and in the 350px downscale: reads as a knobby tire.

[4 figure/ground] Took the reviewer's first option: all three medallion grounds are now #ECF3EF with a 3.6 navy horizon, so navy tires pop and #46555A is free for tread. Pixel-scanned .rm.png: m1 x=230 navy ends 400.0 / pale ground starts 400.9; m2 x=644 navy ends 385.4 / pale 387.2; m3 x=1032 navy ends 389.7 / pale 391.4. Every tire's flat bottom lands ON its ground line - none buried, none floating.

[5 tip] transform-origin moved to the outer-right tire's true contact (1028px 389px) and the machine re-centred (translate 830). Level state: all four wheel bottoms at y=389 exactly. Rest angle raised to 14deg: pixel scan under the left-outer tire at x=880 shows paper from 352.0 to 386.3 - a 36-unit clear lift, unmistakable at display size. Right-outer tire still touches at 389.7.

[6 convergence beat] The loop now has FOUR beats. .pp-a1/.pp-a2/.pp-a3 carry pathLength=100 + dasharray 100 and draw medallion-to-ellipse at 66-73.5% with 150ms stagger; .pp-ah and .pp-el ramp over the same window. Frame sheet: t=8s arrows absent, t=10s arrows + arrowhead + ellipse present. Hold runs 76-100% plus 0-18% = 5.0s rest in the complete state.

[7 gloves] Separate #46555A grip strokes deleted. Gloves are plate C's rects (local x72-120, x280-328) sitting OVER the handlebar ends (local 104, 290) - no grey stub protrudes past the hand in .rm.png or t=8s.

[8 four wheels] The 5x48 white separator rects are deleted. Wheels differentiate by plate C's method: outer pair 72x182 local, inner pair 48x102 with a shorter chevron pitch and a narrower track. Counted four distinct wheels in .rm.png (tipped) and at t=4s (level).

[9 collars] The two bare spruce pills are gone. Each wheel now carries a readable hub flange on its axis: navy-outlined spruce circle r16 with four navy bolt dots. Reads as 'both wheels bolted to one shaft' rather than 'dumbbell with green collars'.

[10 chord depth] All three ground rects set to centre_y + 115 -> y=399 (m1), 385 (m2), 389 (m3). In .rm.png the three horizons sit on one visual line across the row; no medallion looks like it is in a pit.

[11 deformation] The group skewX is gone. Two spruce sidewall slivers (.pp-bl/.pp-br) cross-fade so the widest point in the y330-399 band moves ~9 units while the crown at y162 and the contact at y399 stay fixed. At t=4s only the left flare is present, at t=5s both - the carcass reads as squirming under load, not as a shape leaning over.

[12 arrowhead] All three shafts terminate at the single point (600,624) and the head is one closed spruce triangle (578,624)-(622,624)-(600,652). 3x inspection of the ellipse shows no doubled stroke through the head, no barbs at the arms, and the tip landing 14 units inside the ellipse's top edge (y638) instead of overshooting the centre.

[13 stray marks] The unlabelled navy U bracket is deleted. The CoG quartered circle now hangs a dashed navy+paper plumb line placed OUTSIDE the .pp-tip group, so it stays vertical while the machine rotates (verified level at t=4s, tipped at t=0/t=8s) and it reaches the ground line in both states via a paired scaleY.

[contract] _check.py OK at 11988 bytes (plate budget 25KB). No <text>, no non-token hex, no CSS variables, no scripts or external refs. Zero magenta on this hotspot plate. Rider fully geared with no visible face; quad has four wheels, racks and bars. No machine on the pavement band. Medallion centres exactly (230,284)/(599,270)/(966,274).

[reduced motion] The @media block kills every animation and the base declarations equal the complete state. Verified by direct computed-style probe under Chromium reduced_motion=reduce: all 14 animations drop to 'none', opacity 1, dashoffset 0, .pp-tip retains rotate(14deg) and .pp-cog retains its translate.
residuals: Scrub-arc colour deviates from the reviewer's prescription. They asked for #2F6B52; I used #46555A. Reason: #2F6B52 and #46555A have almost identical luminance (86 vs 81), so spruce marks were invisible on the dark band; once the medallion ground went pale (their own option 1), #46555A is dark-on-pale, is the pavement/shadow token, and does not compete with the spruce convergence arrows. Easy to flip back if the owner prefers the letter of the note.

Medallion grounds lightened to #ECF3EF, which departs from §E's literal wording 'pressed on a flat dark surface' / 'on a dark surface' for the two pictogram grounds. This was the reviewer's first-listed fix for defect 4 and matches plate C. The plate's own dark #46555A pavement band (y600-720) is unchanged, so the 'converging on hard dark ground' idea still carries.

The three nested scrub arcs retain some residual resemblance to a signal/vibration glyph when read in isolation at small size. In context (grey, on the ground plane, at the contact of one wheel of a locked axle) they read as scuff, and they now match the shipped raster's arrangement - but a fresh reviewer may still want them replaced with a filled tapered smear.

At 14deg the plumb line lands ~35 units INBOARD of the outside contact, not past it. Landing outboard requires ~28deg, which is the actual tip-over threshold and would no longer read as 'tipped up onto its outside wheels'. The mark therefore shows the weight line walking out toward the outside pair rather than beyond it.

The harness's .rm.png cannot actually prove the reduced-motion state: Chromium's reduced-motion emulation does not reach the resource document of an -embedded SVG, so .rm.png is a live snapshot at roughly t=1s. I worked around it by making the complete state occupy 0-18% of the loop (so the snapshot lands in it) and verified the @media block separately with a computed-style probe. Worth knowing for the other animated plates in this batch - their .rm.png files may be showing luck of timing rather than the reduced-motion state.

defects.element: Medallion 2 — axle assembly: shaft rect (line 125) + hub discs (line 128) + wheel symbol pp-wh (lines 49–52)

defects.element: Medallion 2 — axle flex beat, .pp-sh / @keyframes pp-ksh (lines 16–17)

defects.element: Medallion 3 — helmet visor bar (line 86) and the two paper jersey front panels (line 82) on a rear-view machine
defects.where: renders/_rv3/rider.png (6x, t=0); also _rv3/m3_level.png (t=6 s)

From behind you would see the helmet's rear shell and the jersey's back. No magenta anywhere — grep for B5446E returns 0 occurrences, so §E's hotspot-plate rule holds absolutely.
Medallion centres are exact against the binding positions: (230,284), (599,270), (966,274), r=165 — 0 units of error, well inside the ±8 tolerance, so the hotspot seals need no edit.

Reduced motion is handled correctly and provably: .rm.png is byte-identical to the resting .img.png (both md5 5c990e71b9c98759e83076251d46ce14, ImageChops diff bbox = None). The @media block sets animation:none and restates every end value, including the transform values on pp-tip, pp-cog and pp-pl.

Loop hygiene follows the brief's phase trick exactly: one 12 s animation-duration on every animated class with percentage beats and holds to 100 %, so the paused-frame sheet is honest. Contiguous rest runs from 76 % through 18 % of the next loop, about 5.0 s.

The plumb line is correctly outside the rotating pp-tip group, so it stays exactly vertical while the machine tips — verified by comparing _rv3/m3_t00.00.png (tipped) with _rv3/m3_level.png (t=6 s, level).

The convergence composition reproduces the shipped raster faithfully, and the three arrow origins sit on the medallion rims to 0.1 unit: (351.5,395.7) and (846.7,388) are both r=165.0 from their centres, (599.3,435) is the exact bottom rim. All three terminate at one point, (600,624).

The quad geometry is shared verbatim with the sibling candidate plate C (identical wheel, body and rider path data), which is the right instinct for C4 — the only divergence is the dropped grip rects, which is what breaks it.
review.notes:
Round 3 verdict: FIX. Three P1s and eight P2s; three of §E's nine acceptance lines fail with evidence in a render.

Acceptance-line audit (§E): "the tire reads as a knobby tire (no gear teeth)" — FAIL (renders/_rv3/true_m1.png, green sidewall scallops). "the axle reads as one solid shaft" — FAIL (renders/_rv3/true_m2.png and _rv3/hub.png, reads as a dumbbell; shaft never reaches either hub). "the quad has four wheels even tipped" — FAIL at true size (renders/_rv3/true_m3.png); the four wheels exist in geometry but read as legs once the 14° tip staggers them. "no machine on the pavement band" — PASS. "arrows meet at one point" — PASS, all three end at (600,624). "medallions within ±8 units" — PASS, 0-unit error. "no magenta" — PASS. "<= 25 KB" — PASS, 11,988 bytes. "_check.py OK" — PASS.

The single most efficient repair is medallion 3: it is drawn well (t=6 s, level, in renders/_rv3/m3_level.png, reads clearly as a quad with a geared rider). Everything wrong with it is in the resting pose — 14° instead of 8°, gloves with no grips beneath them, no ground bracket under the plumb. Fixing those three things turns the worst medallion into the best. Medallions 1 and 2 need actual redrawing, not tuning.

Two systemic observations. First, three separate beats (tire bulge, axle flex, the reset) animate opacity or scale where the brief asked for movement or deformation; the motion law's "every beat must carry meaning" is the clause they all fail, and the fix in each case is to move the shape rather than fade or inflate it. Second, the pale medallion grounds plus the missing pavement context mean the plate's whole thesis — three facts converging AT the pavement — rests on the arrows alone, and the arrows are absent for roughly half of every loop.

Method: ran _check.py (OK) and _render.py fresh, then re-rendered the file at 1200 css px / DPR 2 with the animation seeked to t = 0, 2.4, 2.9, 3.48, 3.5, 3.84, 3.85, 4.2, 5.82, 6.0, 7.0, 7.4, 8.2, 8.6, 8.8, 9.2 s and cropped each medallion, the rider, the hub joint, the scrub arcs and the convergence. Working crops are in D:\\Sightline_Saftey_Academy\\qa\\svg\\renders\\_rv3\\ — true_m1/m2/m3.png are the true-display-size views that decide P1s 1 and 2 and P2 4, and rider.png is the one that decides P1 3. Judged against BRIEFS.md §0 and §E, VISUAL_ASSETS Part 5 (U1–U10, S1–S6, SF1–SF6, C1–C5), the shipped raster keylist-pavement-physics-768w.png, keylist-tcloc-768w.png, and the sibling candidate qa/svg/keylist-stability-model.svg (source of the shared quad).

Out of scope for this folder and not counted against the file: U9 (sidecar provenance) and manifest wiring, which happen when the plate moves to web/src/assets/svg/. One non-defect worth flagging for the owner: the file uses transform-box: view-box rather than the fill-box §0.3 recommends. That is the right call here — the transform origins are absolute view-box coordinates and fill-box would break them — and every current browser engine supports it, but it is a deliberate deviation from the written contract and should be recorded rather than silently carried."

At delivered size (700 px plate → quad ≈ 60 px wide) the rider is a white disc with a navy notch on top and a white capsule below it — it reads as a fuel filler cap and latch, or a cartoon face. The torso rect is the same #2F6B52 as the machine body and sits wholly inside the body silhouette, so the rider mass is not separable (S5). The arms (8-unit navy under 4-unit spruce) run outward to the front wheels and read as A-arm suspension links, not limbs. The black glove circles at x = ±25 are swallowed by the black tire rects (x 28–43 and −43 to −28), so no hands exist anywhere in the image (S3). No legs, no boots, no sleeve separation (S2/S4). The shipped scene-crossing-768w.png shows an unmistakable white helmet + green jersey with pale shoulder panels + forearms reaching to the grips; the candidate disagrees with the shipped plate on how the same object is drawn (C4).
defects.fix: Rebuild the rider as a mass that overhangs the machine outline: shoulders a rounded trapezoid in #2F6B52 with #DEEDE5 shoulder panels breaking the body edge; helmet #F9FCFA r ≈ 13 with the #0D1E2E visor as an arc across its FORWARD edge, not a notch on the crown; forearms angled forward with #0D1E2E glove ovals inboard of the tires at x ≈ ±20, clearly sitting on the grips; two small #0D1E2E knee/boot shapes at x ≈ ±16, y ≈ −6 outboard of the tank.

defects.element: xc-firA instance at (508,120) and xc-firB instance at (462,128) in the top decoration group (SVG lines 127 and 131) versus the crossing quad group .xc-q1 (SVG line 121)
defects.where: t = 6.15 s – 6.48 s (38.4 %–40.5 % of the 16 s loop); worst at t = 6.20 s, where the quad is still at opacity 1.0
defects.what: The crossing machine drives through two conifers. The top decoration group is painted after the quad groups, so a large dark conifer sits straight through the quad's front rack and right handlebar and a second covers its front-left wheel, while the quad's rear half is still on the pavement and it is fading to zero. A first-time learner sees the machine hit a tree and dissolve — a wreck read on a plate whose entire subject is an orderly, uneventful crossing. This is the reverse of the calmer-than-the-prose test (VISUAL_ASSETS 5.4.1) and it puts a translucent machine on the road surface at ~6.25 s.
defects.fix: Clear a tree-free corridor across x 450–550 for all of y 0–184 in the top group: relocate xc-firA (508,120) and xc-firB (462,128), and check xc-firB (534,36). Then either finish the fade before y = 184 (so the machine is already gone by the time it leaves the pavement) or drop the fade entirely and let the machine travel past y = −60 at full opacity, clipped by the plate edge.

defects.element: sight-line group SVG lines 114–117 — .xc-lnL path M500 400 L404 296 L70 296 and .xc-lnR path M500 400 L596 296 L930 296
defects.where: every frame in which a line is lit — .img.png, .rm.png, t = 0, 2.2, 3.0, 8.95, 15.9 s
defects.what: The sight lines never touch the rider. Both paths originate at (500,400), which is buried inside the quad body (the quad occupies x 457–543, y 342–454), and the whole line group is painted BEFORE the quad groups, so the V-apex is hidden. What a learner actually sees is two dotted arcs that begin in mid-air at the top corners of the trail and run away along the road to two rings — they read as road-edge markers, a cable, or a rope, not as a line of sight from the rider's eyes. The shipped plate is explicit about this: its dots visibly converge on the helmet, which is the only thing that says who is looking.
defects.fix: Move the .xc-lnL/.xc-lnR group AFTER the three quad groups so the dots overprint the machine, and start each path at the helmet centre (M500 398) so the first two or three dots land on the white helmet disc.

defects.element: trail rect x=440 y=320 w=120 h=280 fill="#F9FCFA" (SVG line 86) plus the two #ABCDB8 4-unit dashed rails M464.5 598 V326 / M535.5 598 V326 (line 87) and the 3-unit navy edges (line 88)
defects.where: every render; most damaging in the 700 px true-size view
defects.what: The trail reads as a paved lane, not a dirt trail. It is filled #F9FCFA — brighter than the #ECF3EF ground, the opposite of the shipped warm tan track and the opposite of §F's specced #ECF3EF — bounded by two hard 3-unit navy rules, and carries two perfectly straight, mirrored, evenly dashed pale rails down its centre. Those rails read as lane markings, and the plate now has two dashed-line systems (the road's own #D6DFDA centre line and these). §F's whole point is that the learner must tell trail from road at a glance; here the trail is the crispest, brightest, most road-like surface on the plate.
defects.fix: Fill the trail #ECF3EF so it sits BELOW the surrounding ground in value; replace the two mirrored dashed rails with a handful of short, unequal, offset rut segments that wander a few units and are not symmetric; and break or lighten the navy edges so they are not two rules of the same weight as the road edges.

defects.element: @keyframes xc-drive — 52%{transform:translateX(-150px);opacity:0} → 56%{transform:translateX(-132px);opacity:1}, group origin translate(280,286), car 120 units wide
defects.what: The car fades into existence in the middle of the visible roadway. translateX(-150) and (-132) put the car at x 70–190 and x 88–208 — both fully on-plate. Over 640 ms a translucent car materialises on the pavement with the sight-line dots and the left end-ring showing through it. There is no in-world explanation; it reads as a rendering glitch.
defects.fix: Hold opacity:1 for the whole cycle and re-enter from off-canvas: reset to translateX(-400px) or further so the car's right edge is at x ≤ 0, and let it drive in past the left plate edge. Any opacity change must happen entirely outside 0 ≤ x ≤ 1000.

defects.element: <style> block — @keyframes xc-lopa, xc-ropa, xc-drive, xc-arr, xc-adv
defects.where: across the 16 s loop; the blinks at 9.4/19.4/46.4/57.9 % (left) and 13.4/51.9/61.3 % (right); the car dash at 21–33 %; xc-arr at 59–67 %; xc-adv at 40.5–46.5 %; the car creep at 56–76 %
defects.what: Five motion-law breaches (§0.3). (a) Both sight lines snap ON over 0.2 % of 16 s = 32 ms while fading OFF over 480 ms — seven hard asymmetric blinks per loop, against "nothing flashes". (b) The car dash runs 21 %→33 % = 1 920 ms and covers 1 010 units ≈ 526 units/s — roughly 5× the 200-unit slide §F specified and nearly 3× the 700 ms beat cap; against the 32 units/s creep that precedes it, it reads as a car flooring it. (c) xc-arr (quad 3 rolling in) runs 1 280 ms. (d) xc-adv (quad 2 to the bar) runs 960 ms. (e) The car creeps 102 units over 3 200 ms — a beat carrying no meaning that §0.3 says should be cut.
defects.fix: Give every opacity change a symmetric 250–400 ms ramp; cap the car's visible travel at ≤ 700 ms or slow it to ≈ 200 units/s across the frame; bring xc-arr and xc-adv to ≤ 700 ms; delete the creep by parking the car until its pass begins.

defects.element: .xc-lnL / .xc-lnR animation technique — opacity keyframes rather than stroke-dashoffset
defects.where: t = 2.2 s (left only), 3.0 s (right only), 4.0 s (left only), and the same rhythm at 8.0 / 8.95 s
defects.what: The sight lines are toggled, not drawn. §F asked for a dashoffset draw so the line sweeps outward from the helmet — the sweep is what makes it read as a head turn. Toggling opacity makes the whole 400-unit line appear at once, which reads as a lamp switching on. With the apex also hidden (P1-3), the frame sheet shows an alternation but never a look; the acceptance line "the look-look-look rhythm is visible in the frame sheet" is only technically satisfied.
defects.fix: Give each line a solid twin with pathLength set and animate stroke-dashoffset from full to 0 over ≈ 500 ms outward from the helmet, with the dotted texture as an overlaid path or a sweeping clip, so the line grows from the rider toward the horizon.

defects.element: upper trail wedge — <path d="M462 184 L538 184 L524 106 L476 106 Z" fill="#F9FCFA"/> (SVG line 85)
defects.where: every render; top-centre of .img.png, .rm.png and every frame
defects.what: The faint trail above the road tapers and reads as a light beam. In a strict plan view nothing converges with distance, yet this trapezoid narrows 76 → 48 units and is the brightest shape on the plate, so it reads as a spotlight cone or a snow patch rather than the trail continuing. It is also #F9FCFA rather than the specced #DEEDE5, and it is narrower than the 120-unit trail below, so the corridor visibly steps inward at the road edge and changes value three times going up: white trail → grey crossing lane → white wedge.
defects.fix: Make it a constant 120 wide aligned to x 440–560, fill it #DEEDE5, and let the conifer canopy overlap its top edge to extinguish it, instead of tapering it to a point.

defects.element: #xc-quad handlebar path M-27 -20 Q-18 -27 -7 -25 L7 -25 Q18 -27 27 -20, seat rect x=-11 y=2 w=22 h=28, headlight rects at y=-54
defects.where: 3× crop of any quad in .img.png; every frame
defects.what: Machine anatomy: bars and seat do not read. The 4-unit navy handlebar is drawn under the 8-unit navy arm underlay in the same ink, so bars and arms merge into one dark A-shape. The seat rect is entirely covered by the rider torso rect, leaving only a black rim. §0.2 requires the quad to read as body, seat, racks, bars, four wheels at 80 px; it reads as body, racks, four wheels. The two #DEEDE5 headlight rects are 95 % hidden behind the front rack and survive as two 5-unit pale nubs that read as stray tabs (diagram hygiene: no pills standing in for objects).
defects.fix: Raise the bars to y ≈ −30 clear of the arms and give them #46555A grips so they separate from the ink; expose 8–10 units of seat behind the rider; move the headlights forward of the front rack or delete them.

defects.element: sight-line stroke-width="5.5", trail rails stroke-width="4", road centre line stroke-width="6"; stop bar path M442 334 H558 (#B5446E, 8 units, no outline); 10 × #xc-rock; 74 × #xc-fir[ABC]
defects.where: whole file; rock and tree field clearest in the 700 px true-size view
defects.what: Line-weight and hygiene drift. The sight-line dots are 5.5 units against §F's "3-unit dots"; the rut dashes (4) and road centre line (6) are both heavier than the file's 3-unit outline (U6). The magenta stop bar is the only object on the plate with no navy outline and square ends while everything else carries a 3-unit round-joined navy outline (C2). The rocks are #D6DFDA on #ECF3EF with a 2-unit #46555A edge — at 700 px they read as pale smudges or holes, not stones (U5/U10). 74 tree instances stamped from three identical glyphs tile both ground halves near-uniformly and carry more visual weight than the teaching subject, against C3's "quiet edges".
defects.fix: Bring the dots to 3 units; give the stop bar a 3-unit navy outline and round caps; add a small navy top facet to the rock glyph so it reads as a stone; thin the tree field by ~30 % and ramp its value down away from the trail corridor so the crossing is the loudest thing on the plate.

strengths: Contract hygiene is clean and _check.py passes: 10 796 bytes (43 % of the 25 KB plate budget), root is <svg xmlns viewBox="0 0 1000 600" role="img"> with no width/height, <title> is the first child and describes the teaching rather than the decoration, no <text>, no external references, and every id carries the xc- prefix.

Palette is exactly ten literal hexes, all from the §0.1 table, with no strays, no named colours and no 3-digit hex. #B5446E appears exactly once (the stop bar) — U7 and §F's "one magenta" both satisfied.

Reduced motion is correct and complete: the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block kills all six animated classes and pins each to its rest value. Pixel-diffing .rm.png against .img.png gives a maximum delta of 14/255 confined to the sight-line band, which is the live capture landing at ≈5.3 % of the loop — a capture-timing artifact, not a state difference.

The loop seam is genuinely perfect and is the best structural idea in the file: t = 0 s and t = 15.9 s are pixel-identical (ImageChops difference bbox = None). The three-quad relay — q1 crosses and hides, q2 advances into the bar, q3 arrives behind — hands off between identical <use> instances of one <symbol>, so the wrap is invisible.

Loop timing frame is within the law even where individual beats are not: a 16 s period with ≈3.8 s of fully static rest at 76–100 %, and every element driven by one animation-duration with keyframe percentages rather than chained delays, which keeps the paused-frame sheet honest.

The procedure itself is correctly ordered and correctly gated: look-left → look-right → look-left, with the left line correctly staying lit through the car's pass so no crossing happens while traffic is present, and no machine ever stops, pauses or turns on the road (verified frame-by-frame across t = 5.68–6.48 s).

Road geometry reads: the road band, the right-angle junction, the magenta stop bar and the crossing lane are all legible at the 700 px delivered width, and the car is in the correct near/right-hand lane for its left-to-right direction of travel.
review.notes:
Round 1, adversarial. I ran _check.py (OK) and _render.py myself and viewed .img.png, .rm.png and .frames.png, then compared against the shipped scene-crossing-768w.png and keylist-tcloc-768w.png, the retired web/src/assets/svg/scene-crossing.svg, and the house recipe in keylist-three-leaks.svg.

HARNESS BLIND SPOT worth flagging to the builder: _render.py's FRAME_T stops at t = 12 s, but this file's loop is 16 s. The default frame sheet therefore never shows 75–100 % of the loop — including the loop seam and the second half of the car's re-entry. I rendered my own frames at 900 px / DPR 2 for t = 0, 1.5, 2.2, 3.0, 4.0, 5.9, 6.20, 6.25, 6.4, 8.6, 8.95, 13.0 and 15.9 s (script at C:\\Users\\dimen\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\D--Sightline-Saftey-Academy\\fc1af6d0-05b1-476c-9ce3-d890540ecb46\\scratchpad\\frames2.py, PNGs in .\\f2\\). Two of the three P1s (the tree collision at 6.20 s, the car materialising at 8.60 s) are outside or between the harness's sampled times, so a builder who only looked at .frames.png would not have seen them.

_check.py passing is not evidence of anything visual here — it passed on a file with three P1 reads.

The three P1s are all fixable without redrawing the plate: two are pure paint-order/coordinate problems (move the sight-line group after the quads and start it at the helmet; clear the tree corridor at x 450–550, y 0–184), and one is the rider construction inside #xc-quad. The trail-reads-as-pavement P2 is a value inversion (#F9FCFA where §F specced #ECF3EF) plus two mirrored dashed rails, also cheap to fix. I would expect round 2 to be judgeable.

I did NOT find a violation of: U2 (palette), U3 (no text), U4 (no frame), U7 (one accent), U8 (alt), S1 (four wheels, correctly placed on all three instances), SF1, SF3, SF5 (the machine crosses, it never rides along the pavement), or the reduced-motion contract. S2/S3/S4/S5 all fail through the single rider-construction defect (P1-1). SF6 is arguable on the car's 526 units/s dash, which I have folded into the motion-law defect (P2-6) rather than counting twice.

White helmet r13 with a #0D1E2E visor drawn as a crescent across its FORWARD edge (not a notch); a #DEEDE5 shoulder/arm yoke (14-unit pale stroke over a 19-unit navy underlay, elbows at x=+/-27) that visibly breaks the body silhouette out to x=+/-35 against a +/-20 waist; #0D1E2E glove ovals at (+/-19,-24.5) sitting on the bar, clear of the tires (28..43); a #2F6B52 jersey with its own 2.5-unit navy outline separating it from the machine body; #0D1E2E boot blocks at x 19..25.5, y 1..15, clear of the rear tires; 9 units of navy seat exposed behind the jersey.

The two hard 3-unit navy rules are gone, replaced by six short broken #ABCDB8 edge segments of unequal length, asymmetric left to right. The two mirrored dashed rails are replaced by eight short unequal offset rut segments that wander a few units. The trail no longer reads as a paved lane.

Nothing materialises on the pavement.

[fix 7] Frame sheet rows 2-3 and seeked frames 14.6 / 15.2 / 15.7 s: each line is drawn by animating stroke-dashoffset 100->0 on a 30-unit #F9FCFA sweep stroke inside a userSpaceOnUse <mask>, with the dotted path overlaid. The line grows outward from the rider rather than switching on. [fix 9] 3.4x quad crop: the handlebar is a 4-unit navy tube at y -22..-28 with a clear 4-unit gap to the front rack and #46555A grip nubs visible outboard of each glove; bars and arms no longer merge. 9 units of seat show behind the rider. The headlights are two #DEEDE5 lamps on the nose at y -55..-49, forward of the rack (rack starts y=-47), fully visible.

The stop bar is a rounded rect with a 3-unit navy outline and rx=4. 5x rock crop: the glyph now carries a #46555A top facet under a navy outline and reads as a stone. [contract] _check.py OK: 11673 bytes (25 KB budget), no <text>, no external refs, no CSS variables, no duplicate ids, prefers-reduced-motion block present. Palette is 10 tokens, exactly one #B5446E (the stop bar).

[contract] .rm.png is byte-identical to .img.png caught in the rest window and matches the t=0 frame exactly: quad at the bar, both sight lines drawn to their end rings, quad 2 waiting one length behind, car off-plate. Complete state, no delays.

[contract] Frame sheet: the look-look-look rhythm is legible -- t=3 s left only, t=4/5 s right only, t=6 s left lit while the car is present. Quads never stop on the road (t=11.9 / 12.3 / 12.7 s show one continuous traverse). Loop 16 s with a 2.4 s rest at the head plus 0.05 s at the tail.
residuals: Sight-line apex: the reviewer asked for the paths to start at the helmet CENTRE so two or three dots land on the white disc. At true size a dot at dead centre read as a pupil and the symmetric pair on the two lines read as eyes, which collides with the no-visible-face rule. The paths now start 14 units out along each line (492.8,384 / 507.2,384), i.e. on the helmet rim -- the V-apex is on the rider and the chain converges visibly, but no dot sits inside the white disc.

The two or three dots that cross the front rack and body between the helmet rim and the stop bar are navy on #2F6B52 and lose contrast there. The chain is readable end to end in a 3x crop, but at true size it briefly thins where it passes over the machine.

SF's rest frame calls for a small car far left on the road at x ~ 110. Reviewer fix 5 requires all opacity/reset changes to happen outside 0 <= x <= 1000, and a car parked mid-roadway would have to teleport back. I removed the car's opacity animation entirely, so it parks off-plate (x -150..-30) during the rest and makes exactly one constant-speed pass per loop. The rest frame and the reduced-motion state therefore contain no car.

Crossing speed: the road leg is 704 ms for 278 units (~395 units/s average, ~550 peak with cubic-bezier(.4,0,.7,1)), then a slower 800 ms linear tail at 240 units/s off the top. SF specifies 700 ms for this beat and it is the 'square, brisk, done' teaching point, but it is the fastest motion on the plate -- roughly twice the car's 211 units/s.

Outline weight: the outline is 3 units throughout the line work, but three drawn-object thicknesses exceed it -- the handlebar tube (4), the grip nubs (5) and the rider's shoulder/arm mass strokes (19 navy under 14 pale). These are object bodies, not outlines, but a strict U6 reading could flag them.

The quiet tier of the tree field uses a #3B8266 outline rather than navy so it recedes at the plate edges. That is a second outline colour for the conifers, chosen over dropping the outline entirely (which left the far trees as shapeless blobs).

The corridor still changes value three times bottom to top -- #ECF3EF trail, the grey crossing lane over #46555A, then #DEEDE5 above the road. The #DEEDE5 shoulder now added along the lower trail's edges ties the two greens together and the steps are much gentler, but the upper band is still the strongest-valued segment of the corridor. Both fills are what SF and the reviewer specified by name, so I did not swap them.

defects.element: Sight lines — masked dotted paths, lines 112-113, origins (492.8,384) and (507.2,384)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png (t=0); also frames t=3s, 6s, 8s, 10s
defects.what: The plate's central teaching device does not connect to the rider. I sampled the 11 dot centres along the left diagonal: at s=0,20,30,70,80 the background 4 px away is #0D1E2E (navy-on-navy, contrast 1.00:1); at s=10,40 it is #2F6B52 (~2.6:1). Only 4 of 11 dots read — the two that fall on the magenta bar and the two already out on the crossing lane. Because the origin sits under the quad's navy front bumper, the #3B8266 rack and the pale handlebar mass, the visible line stops dead at the top edge of the stop bar. At true display size (700 px) the two lines read as a lane funnel painted on the pavement, not as a gaze; at t=3s the partially-drawn left line is a dotted stub floating over the road with no end at either side. §0.2 diagram hygiene: 'no leader lines or arrows that point at nothing'.
defects.fix: Move the kink outboard to x≈470/530 and start each line at the helmet's outer edge, (486,392)/(514,392), so at least six diagonal dots fall on the pale trail rather than on the machine; and inside each mask add a second, wider #F9FCFA stroke (5 units) under the dotted #0D1E2E stroke so the dots survive where they must cross the bar and the bumper.

defects.element: Trail — the two unstroked fill paths at lines 78-79 (#DEEDE5 outer, #ECF3EF inner)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, every frame; worst at true 700 px display size
defects.what: §F specifies 'trail (#ECF3EF with #ABCDB8 tire-track dashes, NAVY EDGES, 120 wide)'. Neither path carries a stroke, so the trail has no edge at all. Measured: trail interior (236,243,239) against plate ground (249,252,250) = 1.06:1; the outer band (222,237,229) = 1.13:1. Worse, the deliberately faint continuation ABOVE the road (#DEEDE5, correctly edgeless) measures 1.13:1 and so out-reads the real trail, inverting the hierarchy. §F's acceptance line 'road, trail, right angle, bar, lane all legible' fails on trail, and with it on the right angle.

Replace the eight isolated sage strokes at lines 84-88 with two continuous #ABCDB8 dashed runs (4 units, stroke-dasharray 18 22) at x≈472 and x≈528 down the full trail so they read as tire tracks.

defects.where: .img.png at (500,396) and (500,526); visible in the true-700 crop and the frame sheet at every time

defects.where: .img.png (t=0) and .rm.png; the road is empty in both

strengths: _check.py returns OK: 11,673 bytes (47 % of the 25 KB plate budget), viewBox 1000x600, no width/height, role="img", <title> as first child, no <text>, every id carries the xc- prefix.

Palette is strictly the §0.1 token list — #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #3B8266, #ABCDB8, #DEEDE5, #ECF3EF, #F9FCFA, #B5446E, #46555A, #D6DFDA — with exactly ONE #B5446E in the whole file (the stop bar). U2 and U7 both clean.

Reduced motion is exact: an image diff of .rm.png against .img.png returns bbox None — pixel-identical. Every one of the six animated classes is switched off with animation:none and given an explicit parked value, with no delays.

The 16 s loop closes with no seam. At 100 % quad 2 sits at y=402 and quad 3 at y=532 — precisely where quad 1 and quad 2 sit at 0 % — with both sight lines lit and the car off-plate at both ends. Because all three are <use> instances of one symbol the wrap is invisible, and the queue-advance idea ('the group crosses as individuals') survives the loop rather than fighting it. This is the best-engineered thing in the file.

No machine ever turns, hesitates or stops on the pavement. Quad 1's road transit is ~655 ms, square to the road, and quad 2 never enters until quad 1 is gone. SF5 and §F's 'never show a machine turning or pausing on the road' both hold.

The traffic ordering is right: the car is on-plate ~5.4-10.45 s and quad 1 does not begin crossing until 11.55 s, so 'no crossing while traffic is present' is genuinely demonstrated rather than asserted. The car also runs in the correct near/eastbound lane.
The departing quad is occluded by the top-of-plate conifer group (drawn after the quads in document order) — a cleaner solution than §F's suggested opacity fade, and it costs nothing.
The crossing lane over the pavement reads well: measured (127,140,141) against a (70,85,90) road, clearly legible without shouting, and the dashed centre line correctly survives on top of it.

The sight-line masks reveal from the helmet outward (dashoffset 100→0 on a path whose start point is the rider) so the terminus circles arrive last — the correct direction for a gaze, and the right instinct even though the origin is currently buried.
Ground treatment follows §0.2 exactly: full-bleed #F9FCFA rect plus three contour polylines at stroke-opacity 0.07, 1 unit.
review.notes:
Round 2 verdict: FIX. I ran _check.py (OK) and _render.py myself and viewed .img.png, .rm.png and .frames.png, then split the sheet into 12 individual frames, downscaled to the real 700 px display width, and took 8x crops plus pixel probes.

reduced_motion_equals_complete_state is TRUE in the literal sense the harness tests — .rm.png is byte-for-byte the t=0 rest state. But note that the rest state the file defines is itself short of §F's specification: it has no car (defect 4), and its two most important elements (the sight-line origin and the trail) are effectively invisible (defects 1 and 2). So the frame that must 'teach alone' currently teaches: forest, road, a magenta bar, two green machines, and two dotted lines along the pavement whose ends are nowhere. A first-time learner would not derive 'stop completely, look completely' from it.

Acceptance list, line by line, against the renders:
- 'road ... legible' — PASS (road band, centre line, edges all clean).
- 'trail ... legible' — FAIL, 1.06:1 against ground with no navy edge (defect 2).
- 'right angle ... legible' — FAIL by consequence; the junction cannot read when one of its two limbs cannot.
- 'bar ... legible' — PASS, unambiguous.
- 'lane ... legible' — PASS, measured and clear.
- 'the look-look-look rhythm is visible in the frame sheet' — FAIL, no frame in the sheet shows a right-only look (defect 10).
- 'quads never stop on the road' — PASS, verified frame by frame.
- 'one magenta (the bar)' — PASS, exactly one #B5446E in the file.
- '≤ 25 KB' — PASS, 11,673 bytes.
- '_check.py OK' — PASS.

Motion law: every individual keyframe segment is ≤ 704 ms except the 800 ms run-out on the crossing (defect 12) and the 5.6 s linear car transit, which is a physically-motivated single move rather than a beat. Loop period 16 s ≥ 8 s. The rest is thin, however: the complete state holds only ~2.45 s (15.95 s → 2.40 s across the seam), clearing §0.3's ≥ 2 s by 0.45 s, and the only other quiet window is 0.75 s. §F budgeted 58-100 % (6.7 s). The plate is in motion for roughly 13.5 of its 16 s, which is more restless than the house recipe.

The four P1s are all fixable inside the existing structure — none require redrawing the plate. The order I would work them: (1) trail edges, (2) sight-line origin and halo, (3) handlebar/sleeves, (4) park the car on-plate. The machine language items (helmet crescent, jersey panels, tube racks, car glass) are one pass over the xc-quad and xc-carg symbols and would bring the plate into line with scene-crossing-768w.png and keylist-tcloc-768w.png, which it currently diverges from on four separate objects.

residuals: 6 of the 12 frame-sheet samples (t=0 to t=3 s) are the rest state. The car's return leg relies on animation-timing-function: steps(1,end) inside a keyframe to snap from off-plate right to off-plate left.
