defects.where: scene-crossing.img.png and .rm.png (static furniture, present in every frame); verified at true display size (700 px) with a 6x nearest crop of all eleven
defects.what: Not one rock reads as a rock. Two compounding faults: (i) the symbol is a smooth #D6DFDA ellipse carrying a #46555A lens over its upper half — that lens is the plate's ONLY shading device (§0.2 'Fills flat'; everything else is a flat fill) and it is painted in the road colour, so each stone reads as a coin or a crescent moon; (ii) every single one of the eleven is placed touching or under a conifer, and in ten of eleven the tree covers 50–90 % of it. What survives at 700 px is a grey-and-white crescent peeking from behind a trunk (164,418 / 286,424 / 852,522 / 146,122 / 880,140) or a pale hook hanging off a tree's flank that reads as a break in the tree's own outline (708,414 / 128,524 / 248,140 / 612,546). This is U5 verbatim: 'No stray specks, colour noise, or artifacts in flat fields'. The shipped batch-13 plate uses small angular warm-grey stones sitting in open ground.
defects.fix: Redraw #xc-rock as a single flat #D6DFDA faceted polygon — 4–5 straight edges, 3-unit navy rim, no interior lens, no shading. Then reposition every instance into open ground with a clear margin from any conifer footprint (firP ±20.5 x, −28.5..21.5 y; firQ ±15.2; firR ±25.4, −35.5..26.7), and delete any that cannot be cleared — the plate does not need eleven.

strengths: _check.py passes clean: 14,338 bytes against the 25 KB plate budget, viewBox 1000×600, role="img", <title> first child, no width/height on the root, no <text>, no external refs, no CSS variables, no interactivity.

Palette is disciplined — every one of the ten hexes present is a DESIGN-001 token, and #B5446E appears exactly once, on the stop bar, which is the correct focal placement for this plate (U2 and U7 both clean).
Unique id prefix (xc-) with no collision against the other twelve files in qa/svg/, no duplicate ids, and ids only where referenced.

Reduced motion is exact and verifiable: the @media block sets animation:none on all six animated classes and restates the 0 % values (q1/q2 translateY 0, q3 translateY 180, car translateX 110, both dashoffsets 0). I rendered .rm.png and my own t = 0 seek independently and they are identical — .rm.png IS the rest/complete state §F asks for.

The loop seam is genuinely invisible, and it is a clever piece of authoring: q1/q2/q3 are staggered so the 100 % state (q2 at the bar, q3 one length back, q1 off-plate) is compositionally identical to the 0 % state (q1 at the bar, q2 back, q3 below the frame). I rendered t = 14.5, 15.9 and 0 s side by side — indistinguishable.

Rest budget is comfortably met: the last motion settles at 13.95 s and nothing moves again until 5.3 s of the next cycle — about 5.5 s of continuous stillness in the complete state, well past the ≥ 2 s floor, on a legal 16 s period.

The t = 0 frame teaches on its own: road band, dashed centre line, trail arriving at a right angle, stop bar, crossing lane, both sight lines terminating in limit-of-view markers, one machine stopped at the bar and one waiting behind. A viewer who never sees it move still gets the procedure.

§F's hard acceptance lines hold: road / trail / right angle / bar / lane are all legible; the look-left, look-right, look-left rhythm is readable in the harness sheet at t = 4 / 5 / 6 s; one magenta; under budget.
No quad is ever stationary on the road band — the crossing is a single uninterrupted 1.18 s move and I checked every sampled frame from 9.1 to 10.3 s. "Quads never stop on the road" is satisfied.

Safety clauses are clean throughout: four wheels correctly placed on every machine (S1), white full-face helmet with a dark visor arc, navy gloves on the bars, pale sleeves, navy boots (S2/S3), no stunt or airborne pose, no bare head, no passenger, no speed lines or dust plumes (SF1–SF6). The plate is calmer than its prose.
The trail's hand-wobbled navy edges and staggered #ABCDB8 tire-track dashes are a nice touch — they read as a dirt track rather than a road, which is the distinction the brief cares about.
review.notes:
Round 3 review, adversarial. I ran _check.py (exit 0) and _render.py myself and viewed all three delivered PNGs (.img, .rm, .frames), then — because the harness's FRAME_T tops out at 12 s while this file loops at 16 s — I built my own seek harness in the scratchpad and rendered 30 additional paused frames covering 3.7–16 s, plus pixel-accurate 700 px true-size crops of the quad, the stop bar, the sight lines, all eleven rocks, and the tree/road boundary, and a scaled side-by-side against web/src/assets/raster/scene-crossing-768w.png. I also sampled raw pixel values along the sight-line row and the stop-bar row rather than trusting a zoomed crop — that check made me retract an initial "the dots are white" reading and restate it correctly as a paper ring dominating a navy core, which is the defect actually visible at true size.

Where I judged the candidate against the brief rather than the shipped raster: §F explicitly asks for the sight lines to leave "quad 1's helmet", so the origin itself is brief-compliant — what I have written up as P2 is the execution, i.e. dots printed on the #B5446E accent and scattered across the machine, which the shipped plate avoids and which no clause permits. Likewise the trail's low interior contrast (#ECF3EF at ~5 % above the #F9FCFA ground) is inherent to the brief's own colour pins, so I did not book it as a defect; if the owner wants the trail to read the way the shipped plate's tan corridor does, the ground either side needs to carry #ECF3EF and the trail the paper value, which is a brief change, not a build fix.

Two things I could not fully resolve. First, the car's handedness: it is in the far lane heading right, which is wrong-way for right-hand traffic, but the palette forces a pale centre line so the road could equally be read as two same-direction lanes, and the shipped raster has the same arrangement — hence P3 rather than higher, and the fix I propose (near lane) is worth taking anyway because it also repairs the P2 about the lit sight line never meeting the car. Second, the rock verdict: I checked all eleven at true display size rather than sampling, and every one is occluded by a conifer. Under a strict reading of "an element that reads as the wrong thing" that is a P1; I held it at P2 because they are inert background furniture that misleads nobody about the procedure. It is nonetheless the first thing I would fix, and the cheapest.

Verdict is fix on six P2s. None of them touch the file's structure, which is sound — the motion architecture (one 16 s duration per element with percentage beats, staggered machines for a seamless seam, a mask-driven dashoffset reveal) is the best-built of the animated candidates I have seen in this folder, and the reduced-motion contract is exactly right. The work remaining is drawing and placement, not plumbing.

§G specifies the stack rising '~220 above the rack'. At 1250x500 with the ground at y=400 and a 10 degree tilt about the downhill contact, a 220-unit stack puts the leaning stack's top corner at world y≈10 — hard against the top edge. I used 168 (two 84-unit boxes), which lands the corner at y≈47 and matches the shipped raster's own stack height (~191 units at its slightly larger machine scale). The machine is 180x218 units rather than the raster's 220x226 for the same reason.

§G's beats say the right plumb 'lands at the outer tire edge' at 10 degrees. A machine with a 180-unit track only tips at 10 degrees if its CoG sits ~635 units up, which is impossible at this scale. I resolved it the way the shipped raster does and the way the brief's own 'loosely strapped' wording implies: the stack sits offset right on the rack and leans 10 degrees, moving the load CoG outboard, so the plumb reaches ~22 units from the tire edge at the specified 10 degree ground tilt instead of overshooting it. Margin is a short red stub rather than literally zero so the recolour has something visible to land on.

The CoG marks show the LOAD's centre of gravity, not the combined machine+load CoG — a realistic combined CoG would sit at nearly the same height on both machines and the plate would teach nothing. This follows §G/§C and the shipped raster, and relies on the caption ('same kilograms, worse geometry') to carry the mass equivalence.

On the right machine the console is fully hidden behind the leaning stack while on the left ~13 units of it peek above the case. The machines are provably the same symbol, but a reviewer comparing the two silhouettes closely will see this occlusion difference. I added brake levers to the grips so the handlebar ends still read as a handlebar on both.

On top of that the near and far tires on each side overlap by 10 units with no gap, so at 700 px each side reads as one wide track with a seam and the four wheels are not countable at a glance. The shipped raster (scene-loading-cargo-768w.png, keylist-tcloc-768w.png) draws chunky rounded tires with a fine mottled tread and no green outline — C4 failure: the set now draws the same object two ways. §0.2's 'four black knobby tires' and its 'no gear-tooth tires' ban both point away from this treatment.
defects.fix: Rework the symbol to ~46x96 with rx≈22; replace the five full-width chevrons with staggered knob blocks that stop short of the sidewall; drop the #2F6B52 full-perimeter outline (keep at most a small hub/rim mark); and separate the near and far tires by 6–10 units so four wheels are countable.

defects.element: Stack straps M900 146 V247 and M946 146 V247 (navy, stroke-width 6, round caps) vs the left machine's M298 195 V263 / M362 195 V263
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png right machine, x≈985–1010 y≈145–250; see the 3x stack crop and the 5x right-bars crop
defects.what: On the right they read as two rods planted in the machine, not straps. They begin at y=146 — 5 units above the LOWER box's top edge, i.e. partway up the stack — so the upper box has no strap at all, and they end at y=247, 12 units below the box with round caps floating loose on the green fender. Nothing is being wrapped. The left machine's version of the same device does span its whole case and continue onto the rack, so it reads correctly as a strap: the two halves of the plate disagree on how a strap is drawn (C4/C5).
defects.fix: Draw each strap as an inverted-U over the top of the stack and down both sides, or at minimum extend them to span the full 67→247 height, and terminate them on the rack tube (y≈259) rather than as round caps in mid-fender.

defects.element: Lower stack rect (x=871.7 y=151 102x84) bottom edge under <g transform="rotate(10 922.7 235)">
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png right machine, x≈872–973 y≈226–244; also at t=5 s where the machine is level
defects.what: After the inner 10° rotation the box's bottom edge runs (872.5,226.1)→(972.9,243.9), which cuts diagonally through the rack tube (y 229–259) and into the fender (y 250–286), and the box's #F9FCFA fill paints over the left half of the rack tube. The load looks embedded in the machine rather than resting on the rack — a learner reads it as the box passing through the frame. The shipped raster keeps the rack tube drawn in front of the box so the load sits on it.
defects.fix: Raise the stack so both bottom corners clear the rack top (bottom edge ≤ y=226 after rotation), and re-draw the rack tube after the load so the tube crosses in front of the box.

defects.element: .slc-mgl (M420 440 H330) and .slc-mgr (M1010 440 H920) — stroke-width 7, stroke-linecap="round"
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, both ground brackets at the outer tick; see the 5x and 6x bracket crops
defects.what: Each margin stroke ends exactly at the bracket end, so its round cap projects ~3.5 units past the bracket's vertical tick. Both the spruce and the brick segments visibly stick out beyond the tick they are supposed to stop at, which reads as a measurement overshoot on a plate whose whole point is a measurement.
defects.fix: Set stroke-linecap="butt" on both margin strokes (keep round caps on the bracket bar), or shorten each path by 3.5 units at the outer end.

defects.element: #slc-quad console rect x="-20" y="-212" width="40" height="36" fill="#2F6B52"
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png left machine, x≈310–350 y≈188–197; see the 5x left-machine top crop
defects.what: The console/riser is drawn before the cargo case (case top at y=197, console top at y=188), so ~9 units of unexplained spruce pokes above the case's top edge between the handlebar grips. It reads as a small green nub sitting on top of the load with no referent.
defects.fix: Lower the console to y=-204 (top at 196) so the case fully covers it, or move the case group so it clears the console and the console reads as part of the bar assembly.

defects.element: CoG halo circles: <circle r="19" fill="#F9FCFA"> in .slc-pl (330,300) and in .slc-pr (937.3,152.3)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png; compare the two 10x CoG crops
defects.what: The same marker presents as two different symbols. On the left the halo lands on the dark under-body and shows as a bold white ring (which also reads a little like a headlight); on the right it lands on the paper box and is invisible, so that disc has no ring — and the plumb line's first ~19 units are swallowed by the invisible halo, leaving a gap between the disc and the first dash that the left one does not have.
defects.fix: Give both discs the same treatment: either drop the r=19 halo and rely on the 2.6-unit navy rim, or add an explicit paper ring stroke to both, and start each plumb path at the disc's rim (y = cy+14) instead of at the centre.

defects.element: Navy tube/outline gauges across #slc-quad: handlebar 7, rack tube 6, fender/body 3.75, rack deck 3, tire inner ring 2.6, detail 2; plus preserveAspectRatio="none" on the 30-wide tire instances
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png left machine rack region, y≈184–290; see the 5x left-machine top crop
defects.what: Three nested navy outlines of three different weights (6, 3.75, 3) stack within 30 units at the rack, producing a muddle of parallel navy lines with a paper sliver between them; and because the tire symbol is scaled non-uniformly (30/42 = 0.71 on x), the far tires' 2.6-unit spruce ring renders at 1.86 horizontally against 2.6 vertically, so the same ring is two weights on one machine. U6 (line weight consistent with the set spec) is not clean.
defects.fix: Settle on one outline weight (3.75) for all body/rack outlines and one tube gauge for bar and rack; and give the tire symbol a uniform scale (same width for all four instances, or preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet") so its stroke is isotropic.

defects.element: @keyframes slc-tilt / slc-wl / slc-wr / slc-mr / slc-mk — the level 'reset' phase at 44–56 %
defects.where: .frames.png t=5 s (level, unmarked) and t=6 s (tilted, still unmarked)
defects.what: The reset is held ~1.2 s at 44–56 % plus ~1.1 s of transitions in and out, so for roughly 2.3 s of every 10 s the right-hand machine shows a long spruce margin, no brick ✗ and a plumb well inside its bracket — the plate briefly asserts the tall load is fine. The brief allots 500 ms to this reset (5–10 %). The red box outline keeps SF4 technically satisfied, but the unmarked window is long enough to be caught on a glance.
defects.fix: Shorten the level hold to ≤ 600 ms (e.g. 44 %→50 %, then tilt 50 %→57 %, consequence 57 %→63 %, hold to 100 %), and keep .slc-mk at opacity 1 through the reset so the ✓/✗ never leave — only the margin recolour needs to reset.

strengths: Reduced motion is exactly the complete state: a numeric diff of .rm.png against .img.png (t=0) over all 1400x560 px gives a maximum per-channel delta of 0 — pixel-identical, no delays, no partial beats.

The plumb-line geometry is exact, not approximate. Rotating the left CoG (330,300) 10° about its downhill contact (420,400) gives (348.73,285.89); the authored translate is (18.7,-14.1) → (348.7,285.9). The right: (937.3,152.3) about (1010,400) gives (981.41,143.44); the authored translate is (44.1,-8.9) → (981.4,143.4). The CoG stays glued to the load while the line itself never rotates.

Both plumb lines are verifiably vertical at every sampled time — the .slc-pl/.slc-pr groups only ever receive translate, never rotate — confirmed in all 12 frames including the mid-transition frame at t=6 s. Linear-vs-arc interpolation error during the transition is under 1 unit (sagitta 0.98 right, 0.51 left), so nothing detaches.

The dash-offset margin segments are computed to land on the plumb foot in both states, not eyeballed: left tilted, margin drawn 420→354.7 against a plumb foot at 354.8; right tilted, 1010→988.0 against a foot at 987.75; level, left 420→330 against a foot at 330 and right 1010→937.3 against a foot at 937.3.

Motion law is respected: 10 s loop, three beats of 400 ms (level out + marks fade), 700 ms (tilt) and 600 ms (margin recolour + marks return), with ~7.1 s of rest in the complete state; nothing flashes, no spring, no decorative beat.
The t=0 frame teaches on its own: two machines on the same slope, one plumb well inside its bracket with a long spruce margin, one out at the tire edge with a brick stub, ✓ and ✗ present.

Contract clean: _check.py OK, 8421 bytes of a 25 KB budget, unique slc- prefix on both ids, <title> first child, role="img", no width/height, no text, palette entirely DESIGN-001 tokens, no magenta anywhere, and brick red confined to the stack outline, the right margin segment and the ✗ (SF4 satisfied).

The two halves are geometrically identical by construction — same <symbol>, machine at pivot-90 on both sides, brackets at ±90 from each machine centre, same 10° — so the comparison is honest rather than drawn twice.

Edges are quiet: the topmost element (rotated stack corner) sits at y≈47, the outermost at x≈91 and x≈1173 inside a 1250x500 canvas, and the pale dashed seam at x=625 is correctly centred between the two halves.
review.notes:
Round 2. Ran _check.py (OK, 8421 bytes) and _render.py myself and viewed .img.png, .rm.png and all 12 tiles of .frames.png, plus 4x-10x crops of both machines, both contact patches, both brackets, both CoG discs, the stack, and the left machine's rack; also rendered the plate down to 700 px and 360 px to test U10. Read BRIEFS.md sections 0 and G in full, VISUAL_ASSETS Part 5 (U1-U10, S1-S6, SF1-SF6, C1-C5), the retired web/src/assets/svg/scene-loading-cargo.svg, the house recipe keylist-three-leaks.svg, and viewed scene-loading-cargo-768w.png and keylist-tcloc-768w.png.

Where the machinery is concerned this is the best-engineered candidate in this folder: the tilt/plumb/margin maths is exact to a decimal, reduced motion is pixel-identical to t=0, and the loop obeys the motion law. Every failure is in the DRAWING, and three of them are load-bearing.

The three P1s in one sentence each: two of the four wheels hover above the ground while the bracket measures support to their outer edges, so the plate's own physics claim is over-stated; the right machine's handlebars are dismembered by the load into a stub and a floating navy pill, so the two machines no longer read as the same machine; and the tall load renders as one hollow leaning panel rather than two stacked boxes, so "same kilograms, worse geometry" has nothing to stand on. None of these needs the animation touched - they are static drawing fixes in the symbol and the right-hand group.

Two acceptance lines from section G currently have no evidence in a render: "two identical machines" (broken by the right machine's severed bars) and "low case vs tall stack obvious" (the height contrast is obvious; the stack is not). The rest - plumbs vertical at all times, red only on the stack/margin/cross, everything inside the canvas with quiet edges, under 25 KB, _check.py OK - are all evidenced.

One reference-fidelity note the builder should weigh: the shipped batch-13 raster's tires are chunky, rounded, finely treaded and unringed, and its stack is two separately outlined offset boxes with the rack tube drawn in front. The candidate departs from both, and those are exactly the two places a learner's eye lands. C4 ("an ATV drawn two ways is a set failure even if both are good") is the clause at risk if this ships as-is.

Housekeeping: qa/svg/renders/ still holds a stale scene-loading-cargo.rmtrue.png from an earlier round - the current _render.py does not emit that file for plates. Delete it so nobody reviews it by mistake.

self_review: [D1] 5x crop of both contact patches: all FOUR tires bottom out on the single ground line (near tires y=-118..0, far tires y=-68..0, both bottom at 0). No hover gap at any frame. Bracket 222-438 / 812-1028 is exactly outside-to-outside of the real contact width, so the measurement the plate makes is now true.

[D2] 3x and 5x crops of both machine tops: the handlebar is ONE continuous tube grip-to-grip (M-72 -222 q28 0 52 2 h40 q24-2 52-2), drawn last, so both grips and both levers are attached and visible on BOTH machines. Verified in .img.png, .rm.png and every frame of .frames.png. No detached navy pill anywhere.

[D3] 3x crop of the stack: two separate volumes read - lower 132x88 sitting flat on the rack, upper 104x68 with its own 10 deg lean about its bottom-right corner, so the gap between them opens from 8 units (right) to 26 units (left). Separate closed outlines, own lid seam inside each. Not a single hollow panel.

[D4] 6x crop of a tire: 48x118 rx24 near / 32x68 rx16 far, chunky rounded, #46555A chevron knobs stopping ~7% short of each sidewall, NO spruce perimeter ring, 8-unit paper gap between near and far so four wheels are countable unaided at 700 px. Construction now matches the accepted sibling keylist-stability-model.svg (C4).

[D5] 3x stack crop and 5x left-case crop: each strap is a pair of full-height navy bands with butt caps, flush with its box's own top and bottom edges - lower box 154-242, upper box 78-146, case 210-242. Nothing ends in mid-air; the rack loop crosses them. Same device on all three loads (C5).

[D6] 3x right-machine crop at t=0 and at t=5 s (level): the lower box's bottom edge is horizontal at y=242, exactly the rack deck top, with no corner dipping into the deck or fender. The rack loop is drawn AFTER the load and crosses in front of the box's lower part, so the load reads as resting on the rack.
[D7] 5x bracket crops both sides: .slc-mgl / .slc-mgr carry stroke-linecap="butt"; the spruce and brick segments stop dead at the outer tick with no round-cap overshoot.

[D8] 5x left-machine top crop: the console is a full 40x32 spruce pod with a #46555A screen, drawn as part of the machine and with the handlebar tube running across its top out to both grips. No bare green nub above the case.

[D9] Side-by-side 7x crops of both CoG discs at their tilted positions: identical construction (r=15 paper disc, 3-unit navy rim, two navy quadrants), no halo. The left disc was moved onto the spruce fender (330,284) so the rim reads there exactly as it does on the paper box (930.7,103.5). Both plumb paths start at cy+15 (299 / 118.5), so the first dash begins at the rim on both.

[D10] Stroke audit: 3.75 is the single outline weight for every body, rack, deck, console, case and box outline; 6 is the single tube gauge for the handlebar, the rack loop and the straps; 3 for the plumb/CoG instruments, 2 for interior detail. preserveAspectRatio is gone - no symbol is non-uniformly scaled, so no stroke is anisotropic.

[D11] .frames.png: t=0/0.5/1/1.5/2/3/4 tilted with the brick margin, t=5 level, t=6/8/10/12 tilted. Level hold is 46-52% = 600 ms (transitions 400 ms in, 600 ms out). The .slc-mk opacity animation is deleted entirely, so the check and the cross are present in EVERY frame including the level one; only the right margin recolours.
Reduced motion: .rm.png is pixel-identical to the t=0 resting frame (both machines at 10 deg, both plumbs shown, brick margin on the right, both verdict marks) - the complete state, no delays.
Plumb lines stay vertical in every frame: both live outside the rotating groups and only translate (19->23.2,-16.9 left; 54.4,-12.3 right).
Palette: only #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #ABCDB8, #D6DFDA, #46555A, #A93226, #F9FCFA. Zero #B5446E. Brick red appears only on the two stack boxes, their lid seams, the right margin and the cross.

Canvas: at 10 deg tilt the stack top sits at y~41, its right edge at x~1046, the cross diamond spans 1107-1193, the left check 97-183, brackets end at y=460. Nothing clips; edges stay quiet. 8598 bytes, _check.py OK.
Legibility at size: a 360 px proof still reads as two identical quads, low case vs tall stack, check vs cross, green vs red margin.
residuals: The handlebar tube crosses the right machine's lower box (a navy horizontal line through the white box) at y=190. This is the direct consequence of the fix the review prescribed for defect 2 - drawing the bar/console group AFTER the load so both grips stay attached. The grips (814-848 and 992-1026) and the box (858-990) do not overlap, so the tube reads as bars in front of the load rather than an orphaned stub, but a reviewer may still prefer the shipped raster's choice of hiding the right grip behind the box.
On the right machine the console pod is fully occluded by the lower box, so the console is visible on the left machine only. The bar assembly itself reads whole on both.

The stack is 164 units tall (74 + 8 gap + 58, i.e. lower box 88 and upper 68) rather than the brief's '~220 above the rack'. 220 is not reachable on a 1250x500 canvas with the machine at this scale: after the 10 deg ground tilt and the upper box's own lean, a 220-unit stack puts the top corner above y=0. The height contrast against the 32-unit case is still roughly 5:1.

defects.element: Right stack, upper box — <g transform="rotate(10 976 146)"> / <rect x="872" y="78" width="104" height="68">
defects.where: .img.png and .rm.png (identical); every tile of .frames.png; unmistakable at t = 5 s (the level frame) and t = 4.5 s
defects.what: The upper box does not touch the lower box. Its bottom edge is authored at y = 146 while the lower box's top edge is at y = 154, and rotating it 10° about (976,146) lifts its bottom-left corner to y ≈ 128 — so it hovers 8 units above the stack at the pivot corner and 26 units at the far corner, with a wedge of #F9FCFA plate ground visible straight through the gap. It reads as cargo that has already come off the machine, not as 'a tall load'. Worse, the CoG quartered circle and therefore the entire right plumb line hang off this detached object, so the plate's measuring device is anchored to nothing. It also escalates past the caption (VISUAL_ASSETS 5.4.1 calmer-than-the-prose): §G teaches geometry, not a load departing the rack. The shipped raster (scene-loading-cargo-1536w.png) shows the two boxes contiguous, sharing an edge.
defects.fix: Drop the top box so its bottom edge coincides with the lower box's top edge (rect y="86" height="68", i.e. bottom at 154) and pivot it on the lower box's top-right corner — transform="rotate(8 990 154)". Keep the lean ≤ 8° so the far corner rises no more than ~15 units and the two boxes still visibly overlap along the shared edge.

defects.element: Right stack, lower box — <rect x="858" y="154" width="132" height="88" fill="#F9FCFA" stroke="#A93226"> with #slc-bars, #slc-rail and the two 6-unit navy straps crossing it
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, right machine, abs y 154–242; all 12 frames
defects.what: The box is filled with the same #F9FCFA as the plate ground and five foreign lines run across its interior: the handlebar tube plus both grips and both brake levers (abs y ≈ 186), the rack rail's top bar (y = 226), the rack (y = 242), a thin red divider, and two navy straps that are 6 units against the box's own 3.75 outline. The result is a red-outlined lattice with a handlebar sticking out of both sides — it reads as a window sash or a gate rather than a box of cargo, and the bars appear to pass through the load (S6, machine anatomy). Nothing crosses the boxes in the shipped raster.
defects.fix: Move the two <use href="#slc-bars"> / <use href="#slc-rail"> calls BEFORE the cargo so the opaque paper fill occludes the bar and rail (keep the paper fill — §G asks for it), or raise the stack so its bottom edge clears y = 186. Drop the straps from 6 to 3 units so the load's own outline stays the strongest line on it.

defects.element: Left plumb line — .slc-pl path d="M330 299 V456" (3-unit #0D1E2E dashed) crossing the quad's navy centre mass (#slc-quad path "M-50 -115h100v36…", abs y 293–338) and the #46555A rect (abs y 330–358)
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, left machine, abs y ≈ 299–352 — the crop directly under the CoG mark
defects.what: Navy dashes on a navy mass: the plumb line vanishes for ~53 units immediately below the CoG circle, reappearing only as a single tick on the grey rect. A learner cannot trace centre-of-gravity → ground, which is the entire mechanism the plate exists to show. The right plumb suffers a milder version where its lower dashes brush the near rear tire's edge below abs y ≈ 375.
defects.fix: Case each plumb: draw the same path twice inside .slc-pl / .slc-pr — first a solid 7-unit #F9FCFA stroke, then the 3-unit #0D1E2E dashed stroke on top — so the line stays readable over dark masses and tires without leaving the palette.

defects.element: Left load — <rect x="250" y="210" width="160" height="32" fill="#ABCDB8"> with <use href="#slc-rail" x="330" y="408"> drawn after it
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, left machine, abs y 210–260
defects.what: The rail's top bar (6-unit navy, abs y = 226) runs straight through the middle of the 32-unit-tall case, cutting it into two pale slats; the two 6-unit straps then divide those into six cells, and the spruce rack sits below as a third bar. The assembly reads as a three-slat luggage rack, not as 'a low flat case strapped on the rear rack' — so the left-hand half of the comparison loses its load entirely. The case is also 32 units tall against §G's 160×60, which makes it slat-like before the rail even crosses it.
defects.fix: Draw <use href="#slc-rail"> BEFORE the case so the rail sits behind the load; restore the case to the briefed height (y="182" height="60"); drop the straps to 3 units so the case's 3.75 outline reads as the object boundary.

defects.element: #slc-quad inner tire pair — <rect x="-52" y="-68" width="32" height="68" rx="16"> and <rect x="20" y="-68" …> plus their #46555A tread notches
defects.where: every render; clearest in the t = 5 s level frame and in a side-by-side against web/src/assets/raster/scene-loading-cargo-1536w.png
defects.what: The front tires are drawn full-width with the same tread, bottoms on the same ground line, and only 8 units clear of the rear tires — so the machine reads as four wheels abreast on one axle (a dually/tractor), not as a quad seen from behind. The shipped batch-13 rear-view quad in this very slot, and keylist-tcloc, occlude the fronts completely behind the rears. VISUAL_ASSETS C4: the same ATV drawn two ways is a set failure even when both are good.
defects.fix: Either delete the inner pair and let the rear tires carry the machine as the shipped plate does, or tuck them directly behind the rears as slivers (x ≈ ±56 to ±64, top no higher than −70) so they read as occluded fronts. Leave the ground bracket on the rear track either way — it is already correct at ±108.

defects.element: @keyframes slc-tilt / slc-wl / slc-wr / slc-ml / slc-mr — the 42–58 % window of the 10 s loop
defects.where: .frames.png: only t = 5 s catches the level state; t = 4 s and t = 6 s are already fully tilted
defects.what: Timing is 42–46 % rotate to level (400 ms), 46–52 % hold level (600 ms), 52–58 % rotate back (600 ms). The control condition of the whole comparison — both machines level, both plumbs centred, the right margin spruce — is on screen for 0.6 s out of 10 s (6 % of the loop), so the animation reads as the plate twitching once every ten seconds rather than demonstrating anything. §G's beats give the level state 77–100 % (≈ 2.3 s) and the tilt a 700 ms arrival; §0.3's 'every beat must carry meaning' is not met by a 600 ms glimpse.
defects.fix: Re-time to the brief inside the same 10 s period and keep the tilted state at t = 0: hold tilted 0–42 %, ease to level 42–49 % (700 ms), hold level 49–71 % (≈ 2.2 s), ease back to tilt 71–78 % (700 ms), hold 78–100 %.

defects.element: .slc-mgr stroke keyframes — #A93226 → #2F6B52 across 43–46 %, and back across 56–58 %
defects.where: seeked frames t = 4.4 s and t = 5.7 s; visible as an olive-brown bracket segment in the t = 4.5 s frame
defects.what: Animating the stroke property interpolates colour, so the danger-margin marker is painted #8C3F30 at t = 4.4 s and #913D2F at t = 5.7 s — neither is a DESIGN-001 token, and the risk marker briefly turns muddy brown twice per loop. This is a live U2 breach that _check.py cannot see because it only greps source hex. The owner-accepted house recipe (keylist-three-leaks.svg) animates only transform, opacity and stroke-dashoffset for exactly this reason, and §0.3 says to prefer those properties.
defects.fix: Draw two coincident margin strokes — one #2F6B52, one #A93226 — and cross-fade their opacity, or put animation-timing-function: steps(1) on the colour keyframes so no intermediate value is ever painted.

defects.element: <title> — '…while the tall stacked boxes carry it out to the outer tire edge.'
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, right bracket, abs x 985 vs the downhill tire edge at abs x 1028
defects.what: At 10° the right plumb foot lands ~43 units inside the outer tire edge and leaves a red margin of 16.9 % of the bracket — a visibly healthy margin, not a plumb 'at the edge'. §G asks for the right plumb to land at the outer tire edge (margin ≈ 0). Either the drawing under-delivers the point or the alt text over-claims it; as rendered the ✗ is not visually earned by the geometry, only by the red outline.
defects.fix: Raise the stack's CoG (or lift the tilt to ~13°) until the right plumb foot coincides with the rotated bracket's downhill end, so slc-mgr's tilted dashoffset goes to ~97–99 and the red margin collapses to a stub. Then the title is true.

defects.element: Interior stroke weights across the file — 6 units on the straps, #slc-rail and #slc-bars; 8 on the suspension diagonals; 4–5 on the tread notches; against the file's 3.75 outline
defects.where: every render; the straps visibly out-weigh the #A93226 box outlines in the right stack
defects.what: §0.2 allows ONE outline weight per file (3.75 at 1250-wide) plus 2-unit interior detail. This file paints at 2, 3, 3.75, 4, 5, 6 and 8, and the heaviest strokes in the plate are interior details on the cargo — which inverts the reading hierarchy so straps read louder than the objects they hold (U6, C2).
defects.fix: Outline 3.75, interior detail 2 (2.5 at most for the handlebar tube); nothing interior heavier than the outline.

defects.element: Instrument pod — <rect x="-20" y="-222" width="40" height="32"> in #slc-quad, left machine only
defects.where: .img.png / .rm.png, left machine, abs y 186–218, sitting on the case top edge at y = 210
defects.what: The pod's stem is never drawn — its bottom (abs 218) is 24 units above the rack top (242) with nothing joining them — and the case, drawn after the quad, covers its lowest 8 units, so it reads as a small green box resting ON the cargo with the handlebar passing through it. On the right machine the same pod is hidden entirely by the stack, so the two machines present different anatomies in the same plate.
defects.fix: Add a short spruce steering stem from the pod down into the body (abs y 218 → 260) inside #slc-quad, so the bars are visibly attached on whichever machine the load does not cover.

defects.element: ✓ and ✗ verdict diamonds at translate(140 112) and translate(1150 100) — static, no animation class
defects.where: .frames.png, t = 5 s

Round 3. Ran _check.py (OK, 8598 bytes) and _render.py myself at the default 700 px and again at --width 1250 for defect hunting, then wrote my own Playwright seek harness to sample the 42–58 % transition at t = 4.3/4.4/4.5/5.6/5.7 s, which is where the off-token colour interpolation shows. Viewed .img.png, .rm.png and all twelve tiles of .frames.png, plus tight crops of the left load, the right stack, both plumb runs and a side-by-side of the candidate quad against the shipped raster. Reference material read/viewed: BRIEFS.md §0 and §G, VISUAL_ASSETS Part 5 (U1–U10, S1–S6, SF1–SF6, C1–C5, 5.4.1), web/src/assets/raster/scene-loading-cargo-768w.png and -1536w.png, keylist-tcloc-768w.png, the retired web/src/assets/svg/scene-loading-cargo.svg, and web/src/assets/svg/keylist-three-leaks.svg for the house <style>/@keyframes/RM recipe.

The one blocking defect is the floating top box: at t = 5 s it is unambiguous, and because that box carries the CoG mark and the whole right plumb, the failure is not cosmetic — the plate's measuring device is attached to an object that is not attached to the machine. Everything else is fixable without redrawing.

Two verdict-relevant notes for the builder. (1) The tilted-at-rest composition is per §G, but with only a bare tilted stroke for ground and the plate's own horizontal contour texture behind it, the resting frame is close to reading as a crooked image rather than two slopes; once the level hold is lengthened to the briefed ~2 s that risk mostly resolves itself, so I have not raised it as a separate defect. Acceptance-line audit against the renders: 'two identical machines' — evidenced (same <use>). 'low case vs tall stack obvious' — evidenced, though weakened by the left case reading as rack slats. 'both plumb lines vertical at all times' — evidenced in all 12 frames plus both static renders. 'red only on the stack, its margin and the ✗' — evidenced in source and in .img.png, but broken in motion by the brown interpolation at t = 4.4 / 5.7 s. 'everything inside the 5:2 canvas with quiet edges' — evidenced (top box reaches y ≈ 41, ✗ diamond stops 56 units from the right edge, brackets bottom out at y ≈ 459). '≤ 25 KB / _check.py OK' — evidenced. The two lines that lack render evidence are §G's 'the right lands at the outer tire edge' (it lands 43 units inside) and the beat structure in §G's motion spec.

self_review: true.png at 40 px reads as one hand, one lever, cold: a sage gloved hand curled down over a dark blade, a green grip at the left, teal weather marks above.

zoom.png: four fingers are individually countable, each a sage tube with a 2-unit navy outline and 2-unit navy separators, each ending in a rounded tip clear of and below the lever - the wrap reads as closing, not hanging.
The thumb is part of the hand's single outline (one merged palm+thumb path plus a 1.8 crease line) - it is a lobe on the hand's lower right, not the floating navy-ringed capsule that v2 rendered.
The handlebar grip reads as a cylinder in the render: spruce tube with a #3B8266 elliptical end face, not the flat slab/battery that v1-v4 rendered.

The brake lever reads as a lever, not a stick: a tapered navy blade whose butt carries the paper pivot dot inside the spruce perch lug, sweeping under the fingers and emerging with a rounded ball tip clear of the hand at the right. Both ends are visible; nothing dangles.

Cold marks read as weather across the top band: three teal (#1E8A6E) snow asterisks built as three crossed strokes, plus two teal drizzle strokes of differing length and height so they do not pair as a '//' glyph. None of them touch the hand or the grip.
No red and no amber anywhere in the render - v1's brick-red paw and its red asterisk are gone. Palette in the file is exactly #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #3B8266, #ABCDB8, #F9FCFA, #1E8A6E; zero magenta.

Silhouette is distinct from sort-gear-gloves rendered at the same 40 px: that one is an upright glove, fingers pointing up, wide cuff bar, isolated; this one is a horizontal curled hand on a lever with a grip and weather.
rm.png is identical to img.png - the file is static (check reports animated=False), so no @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block is required or present.
Nothing is clipped or edge-flush: smallest margin in the render is ~2.4 units (top of the left snow asterisk); bottom margin ~9 units below the longest fingertip.
_check.py prints OK: 2269 bytes against the 8 KB icon budget, no <text>, no external refs, no CSS vars, no duplicate ids, all four sac-ch-* ids referenced.
residuals: The third snow asterisk sits upper-RIGHT (centre 55,9) rather than upper-left as §H literally specifies. Deliberate: with two flakes it left the top-right empty against the hand's mass and the icon read left-heavy. Trivial to move if the owner wants the letter of the brief.

The handlebar grip is mostly occluded by the hand, so 'short handlebar grip' reads as a bar END (cylinder + end face + perch) rather than a length of grip. Unavoidable if the hand is genuinely ON the grip at 64 px; four earlier layouts that showed more grip all read as a vehicle body or a slab.

The grip's end face uses #3B8266 (mid spruce), a second green not named in §H's draw list. It is a §0.1 token and exactly the 'second green where two must read apart' case - it is the single change that made the grip read as a cylinder instead of a box. Flagging it in case §H is meant to be exhaustive.
The paper pivot dot is the smallest legible element: ~1.3 px of paper inside a navy ring at 40 px. It registers as a bolt in true.png but is at the floor of legibility.

Process note: I removed and immediately recreated qa/svg/renders/_tmp while clearing my reference renders. That directory is scratch space _render.py recreates on every run, but sibling agents are rendering into the same folder, so a run mid-flight at that moment could have needed a retry.

defects.element: brake lever (path "M11 34.5 C24 40 38 43 52 44 …", fill #0D1E2E) vs. the four finger strokes
defects.where: sort-cond-cold-hands.zoom.png (crop x6–60 / y28–56) and .true.png at 40 px; also visible in the 32 px contact sheet
defects.what: The lever is painted LAST, so it lies in FRONT of all four fingers and cuts each one into an upper rectangle and a lower rounded tab. Nothing wraps it. Together with the hand-back edge at y=33 and the three knuckle ticks it produces five stacked horizontal bands, so at 40 px the object reads as a dark bar/twig/strap laid across a mitt — a grille or a mouthful of teeth with a band across it — not a lever inside a closing hand. The taper is also backwards for a lever (pointed at the pivot at x≈11, thickest 4.4 units at the free end at x≈52) and there is no ball end. The one element that carries the teaching reads as the wrong object.
defects.fix: Move the lever path BEFORE the finger group so the fingers occlude it, and let only its pivot end (near the perch) and its ball end (past the little finger) emerge; reverse the taper so it is ~4 units at the perch narrowing to ~2.5, and finish it with a round ball end (r≈2.5) rather than a blunt cap. Curl fingertips 2 and 3 over it so the silhouette shows fingers in front of, not under, a bar.

defects.element: handlebar grip end — ellipse cx=7 cy=24.5 rx=3.2 ry=6.5 fill #3B8266, plus the white pivot circle cx=11.6 cy=36.4 r=2.1

A dark oval with a heavy navy outline set in a green mass reads as an EYE, and the white dot below it reads as a nostril/second eye. At 32–40 px the left cluster therefore reads as an animal's head in profile and the whole icon as a green creature with a striped body — a variant of the exact misread ("a brick-red blob that reads as a paw") that §H exists to correct.
defects.fix: Delete the ellipse and the second green; draw the bar end as the set does — a single flat navy-outlined cap flush with the tube end, or a plain rounded terminus in #2F6B52 with a 1.8-unit flange ring 3 units inboard so it reads as a grip. Replace the white pivot dot with a navy-outlined perch bracket at least 3 units across, joined to the grip (see next defect).

review.notes:
Round 1, reviewer. I ran _check.py (OK, 2269 bytes, animated=False) and _render.py --icon 40 myself, and viewed all four PNGs plus two nearest-neighbour blow-ups of .true.png and two 5x crops of .zoom.png (grip cluster, lever/finger crossing). I also built 40 px and 32 px contact sheets of the candidate beside sort-gear-gloves, sort-cond-frost, sort-cond-dust, sort-cond-wet-roots, sort-cond-fading-light, sort-cond-swollen-creek and sort-gear-boots (scratchpad contact40.png / contact32.png) to judge C1–C5 and the §H silhouette line; and I read the retired icon, the four named reference icons, the rest of the sort-cond family, keylist-three-leaks.svg, and VISUAL_ASSETS lines 504–590.

Acceptance list, §H, line by line against the renders:
- "a hand on a lever with cold marks" — HALF EVIDENCED. The hand reads at 4x zoom and is weak-but-present at 40 px; the LEVER does not read (P1 #1) and the handlebar is 86 % occluded (P2 #6). Cold marks are present but read as an ornamental sparkle rule (P2 #8).
- "silhouette distinct from sort-gear-gloves" — MARGINALLY TRUE and not for the right reason. On the 40 px sheet both cells are dominated by the same sage hand-mass at the same size with the same navy outline; the separation comes from the flipped finger direction, the dark bar and the weather band, not from a distinct silhouette. Once the hand gains the cuff that P2 #5 calls for, re-check this line explicitly — a cuffed sage hand is very close to sort-gear-gloves.
- "<= 8 KB" — TRUE, 2269 bytes.
- "no red anywhere, no amber" — TRUE, verified by grep.

Two things drove the P1s. First, paint order: the lever sits on top of the fingers, which is both anatomically backwards for a squeezed lever and the direct cause of the grille/teeth read. Second, the grip end: the #3B8266 ellipse straddles the tube's flat edge instead of capping it, so its inner arc draws a closed lens inside the green mass and reads as an eye — which, with the white pivot speck under it, makes the whole icon read as a green creature in profile at 32 px. That is the same class of misread (an animal shape) that §H was written to eliminate, so it cannot ship as a fix for it.

Note for the builder: the sort activity renders these icons at BOTH 40 px (tray, size-10) and 32 px (placed chip, size-8, web/src/activities/sort_categorize/index.tsx:169). U10's "smallest intended render size" is therefore 32 px, not 40 — render --icon 32 as well next round and judge that one first.

Not defects, recorded so they are not re-litigated: bare href on <use> renders correctly because nothing in this pipeline rasterises SVG outside a browser (no cairosvg/resvg/sharp/inkscape in web/src/assets, ops or artgen); U7 (clay-500 once) is N/A for this icon set; S1/S2/S4/S5/S6 are N/A (no machine, no rider); SF1–SF6 clean.

self_review: [D1] In .zoom and .true the lever is painted BEFORE the hand: no dark bar crosses any finger. Only its two ends show - a ball end (r 3, x 8-14) past the outermost finger and a squared hinge end (x 49-57) past the little finger; the fist occludes everything between. Taper now runs 4.6 units at the hinge to 3.4 at the ball (was pointed at the pivot, 4.4 at the free end).

[D1] At 32 and 40 px the two exposed ends sit in one band and the eye completes the rod through the fist - I A/B-rendered a no-stub variant at 32/40/64 px and the single-ended version read as a pin, so the stub stayed.
[D1] The five stacked horizontal bands are gone: hand-back edge, three knuckle ticks and the front-facing lever were all deleted. Lower half now has one dark line (the lever) and paper notches.

[D2] The #3B8266 ellipse is deleted. The bar end is now the tube's own rounded terminus in #2F6B52 with a navy outline flush with the silhouette, plus a full-height flange seam at x=11. No closed lens inside the tube; nothing protrudes outside the silhouette; the eye/nostril read is gone in .zoom and in the 32 px contact sheet.

[D3] Fingers are three curled lobes of varied width (index 8.5, middle 7.5, little 6.6 units), varied length (little is 5-6 units shorter than the middle), with silhouette notches, not four identical 9.5/5.5 double strokes. They read as a closed fist in .zoom, not a hanging open hand or a comb.

[D4] At 32 px, in a contact sheet against frost / dust / wet-roots / fading-light / swollen-creek / gloves / boots, the icon does not smear: three knuckle ticks, thumb crease and the fourth finger are gone; interior detail is a flange seam plus two 1.8 ribs inside the green tube only. Its density matches the family.

[D5] The cuff is a sage navy-outlined band that runs off the RIGHT edge of the viewBox at the wrist (drawn to x=66 so the edge clips), mirroring sort-gear-gloves' cuff. No lobe sits where the wrist belongs; the hand is no longer a detached mitten.

[D6] Grip is visible x 5 to 28.6 on its top edge and x 5 to 23.4 underneath - about 23 units, up from ~9. It carries a flange seam and two ribs, so it reads as a grip tube rather than a featureless stub.

[D7/D8] Snow is now ONE flake built with sort-cond-frost's construction - six arms plus six two-stroke sprigs at the same radius ratios - drawn in teal at r 7.5. Verified in an 8x crop that the sprigs render as barbs, not a bare asterisk. Set no longer disagrees with itself.

[D8] Weather is clustered upper-left over the bar (x 4.4-35), split into two lanes at different altitudes: the flake at y 4-21 on the left, three steeper 2.2-unit drizzle strokes of decreasing length in a descending diagonal lane to its right (y 6-19). No single ornamental row along the top edge; nothing at upper-right.
[D9] The paper-white pivot dot is gone. Nothing in the file is #F9FCFA; there is no bright speck in the lower half at 40 px.
[D10] Palette audit of the source: only #0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #ABCDB8, #1E8A6E. One green for the grip; the navy outline does the separating. No second green, no red, no amber, no magenta.

[D11] Subject now spans x 4.4-57 (plus the cuff bleeding right) and y 3.9-51.6, and the horizontal grip is the icon's spine, so the cell no longer floats or reads darker than its neighbours in the 32 px sheet.
[D12] No <defs>, no <use>, no href of any kind - every path is inline. 2093 bytes, well under the 8 KB icon budget; _check.py prints OK with no warnings.

[Sec H] At 40 px (.true.png) it reads as a hand on a lever with cold marks; its silhouette (fist on a horizontal bar, cuff off the right, rod with a ball) is clearly distinct from sort-gear-gloves (flat glove, four fingers up, cuff bar) - both viewed side by side in the same sheet.
[Sec 0] Static file: .img.png, .rm.png and .true.png are byte-identical (md5 852d68a6...), so there is no motion and no reduced-motion state to diverge.
residuals: No separate thumb lobe. I built the reviewer's version (a sage lobe hooking under the bar at x 18-26, y 34-40) and A/B-rendered it at 32/40/64 px: it read as a beak/claw pointing left and swallowed ~5 more units of visible grip, so the shipped file wraps the thumb into the hand's leading edge, which crosses the grip diagonally. The icon therefore shows three fingers and an implied thumb, not Sec H's 'four fingers + thumb clearly separate'.

No visible perch bracket. At this viewing angle the perch is inboard, behind the fist, so drawing one under the visible part of the bar would have put the lever mount outboard of the hand. Instead the lever's thick hinge end emerges squared at x 49-57. If the owner wants the perch literally drawn, the hand has to be shifted right ~6 units and shrunk, which costs the finger read.

Finger curl is expressed as stubby silhouette lobes (4.8-6.4 units deep) rather than a full 60-80 degree sweep with tips pointing back at the grip. Once the lever's 4-unit band is cleared and the subject is held to y <= 52, that is the deepest curl the budget allows.
The two 1.8 grip ribs are nearly invisible at 32 px - they neither help nor hurt at that size; they only carry at 40 px and above. Say the word and I will drop them and leave the flange seam alone.

The lever's hinge-end stub is a squared navy tab; at 4x zoom it reads slightly blocky against the fist's right edge. It is legible as the rod continuing at 32/40 px, but it is the weakest join in the drawing.

defects.what: The hand ends in exactly THREE finger lobes (contours closing at ≈(43,44.6), (35.5,45.2), (27,45.8)) and has no thumb at all — the upper-left edge from (28.6,25.8) to (36,18.8) is a smooth blob edge with no separating crease, so the thumb the source comment claims is 'wrapped on the near face of the grip' does not exist in the render. §H requires 'four fingers + thumb clearly separate'; VISUAL_ASSETS S3 requires hands to read as gloved hands (P1); and C4 fails against the shipped `sort-gear-gloves.svg`, which draws the same object with four finger tops plus a thumb bulge. At 40 px a learner counts three lumps hanging off a mitten.
defects.fix: Redraw with four finger lobes plus a thumb, using `sort-gear-gloves.svg`'s digit construction (individual ~3-unit rounded lobes, each separated by a navy contour); put the thumb as a distinct lobe on the near face of the grip at ≈(30,28) with a 2-unit navy crease separating it from the palm.

defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.true.png at 40 px (confirmed in .zoom.png)
defects.what: The opaque `#ABCDB8` hand is painted after the blade and hides it from x≈27 to x≈48. The two surviving fragments sit at different heights — left fragment centreline y≈43.2, right fragment y≈40.6, a 2.6-unit offset against a blade only 3.4–4.6 units thick — so the eye cannot join them across the occlusion. They read as two unrelated navy marks: a lollipop-headed pin at the left and a blunt 9-unit tab (5.6 CSS px at 40 px, square-cut, no tip) at the right. §H's 'Must read at 40 px: one hand, one lever, cold' is not met, and the acceptance line 'a hand on a lever with cold marks' has no evidence in .true.png.
defects.fix: Give the blade one constant centreline so both exits are at the same y; tuck the inboard end under the FINGERS rather than under the palm; lengthen the outboard fragment to ≈16 units ending in a rounded ball tip; and paint a 2-unit navy segment of the blade OVER the sage between two finger lobes so the occlusion reads as fingers wrapping a continuous lever.

defects.element: hand / lever / grip relationship (whole composition)
defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.zoom.png and .true.png
defects.what: Nothing is being gripped. The three finger lobes hang from y≈44 to y≈51.6, entirely BELOW the blade's lower edge (y 42.9–44.9), with pale ground visible between the fingertips and the blade; and the palm mass sits below and to the right of the grip (grip occupies y 24–36) instead of wrapping it. At 40 px the composite read is 'a fist/mitten floating past a dark green capsule in snow' — the capsule reads as a battery or marker, not a handlebar, because nothing holds it. C-087's entire content ('hands are clumsy on the levers') is therefore absent, and the `<title>` ('a gloved hand curled round the brake lever') over-claims what the art delivers, failing U8.
defects.fix: Raise the blade to y≈40, drop the palm 3–4 units so its top contour rides the grip's upper edge and its left contour wraps the grip's front face, and let two finger lobes cross IN FRONT of the blade with the fingertips closing just under it. Shrink the fist to ≈2× the grip diameter (it is currently ≈2.7×) so hand and bar read at one scale.

defects.element: lever pivot `<circle cx="10.9" cy="43.2" r="3" fill="#0D1E2E">`

It is also on the wrong end of the lever: the cuff enters from the right, so right is inboard; a real lever pivots at the perch INBOARD of the grip and its tip extends past the bar end. The drawing has the pivot outboard and the blade running inboard under the wrist, i.e. exactly reversed.

defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.true.png at 40 px, top-centre, directly above the knuckles

At 40 px they visually attach to the fist and read as comic-book speed/impact lines rather than falling drizzle — SF6 explicitly bans motion lines, and 'fist + impact lines' is a materially wrong read for a rider-care card.
defects.fix: Move them out of the hand's airspace into the sky lane under the flake (x 6–22, y 22–34), steepen them toward vertical, vary their lengths (≈5/8/6 units) so they stop reading as a rank, and keep ≥5 units of clear ground between any stroke and the hand contour.

defects.element: snowflake `<g stroke="#1E8A6E">` — 6-arm dendrite at (12,12.5) plus 12 barbs
defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.true.png at 40 px, upper-left; 40 px contact sheet beside sort-cond-frost.svg
defects.what: §H asks for 'two or three small snow asterisks (three crossed 4-unit strokes)'. The candidate draws ONE 15-unit six-arm dendrite with twelve barbs — the same construction as the hero flake in the shipped `sort-cond-frost.svg`, which sits in the same M5 L1 S2 deck. On the contact sheet the two cards both lead with a big dendrite, and they disagree on how it is drawn (frost: `#0D1E2E` at 2.8; candidate: `#1E8A6E` at 2.2/1.8) — a C4 set failure. It is also the highest-contrast object in the icon at 40 px, so it wins the first read from the hand, inverting the brief's hierarchy. The 1.8-unit barbs are ≈1.1 CSS px at 40 px and clump into noise (U10/U5).

defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.true.png right edge (probe of x=61.5/62.5/63.5 shows ink at y≈12.5 and y≈28.8 only); 40 px contact sheet
defects.what: The cuff crosses the frame — its rotated corner reaches x≈67 at y≈27 and x≈64.2 at y≈13.3 — so the arm is cut off by the viewBox. strengths: File contract is clean and verified: `_check.py` OK, 2093 bytes (≤ 8 KB), root matches the set exactly (`viewBox="0 0 64 64" role="img" fill="none" stroke="#0D1E2E" stroke-width="2"` with round caps/joins), `<title>` is the first child, no width/height, no `<text>`, no ids, no gradients/filters/foreignObject.

The defect that motivated the rebuild is genuinely gone: the retired `web/src/assets/svg/sort-cond-cold-hands.svg` used `#A93226` twice (the paw blob and the asterisk); the candidate contains no `#A93226` and no `#DBA12E` anywhere, so the wrong 'unsafe' semantics no longer sit on a rider-care card.
Every colour is a literal hex from the §0.1 table — `#0D1E2E`, `#2F6B52`, `#ABCDB8`, `#1E8A6E` — no named colours, no 3-digit hex, no CSS variables.
Static file: `.img.png` and `.rm.png` are pixel-identical (ImageChops difference bbox = None, extrema 0), so the reduced-motion state is trivially the complete state.

The §H acceptance line 'silhouette distinct from `sort-gear-gloves`' does hold — on the 40 px contact sheet the grip capsule and the flake separate the two cards; gloves reads as a bare mitt pair, this one does not.
The 'cold' half of the subject registers at 40 px: the flake plus strokes read immediately as winter weather in `.true.png`.
review.notes:
Round 2, adversarial. I re-ran `_check.py` (OK: 2093 bytes, viewBox 64x64, icon, animated=False) and `_render.py --icon 40` myself, then viewed all four PNGs (.img, .rm, .true, .zoom), an 8x nearest-neighbour upscale of `.true.png` to judge the honest 40 px read, and 3x crops of the lever and hand regions from `.zoom.png`. I also built a 40 px contact sheet in the scratchpad rendering the candidate beside the shipped `sort-cond-frost`, `sort-cond-wet-roots`, `sort-cond-dust`, `sort-cond-swollen-creek`, `sort-cond-fading-light`, `sort-gear-gloves`, `sort-gear-layers`, and probed the right-most columns of the render for clipped-stroke slivers (none — the bleed is clean, just out of family). I changed nothing in the repo; all working files are in the session scratchpad.

Verdict is FIX on three P1s. The decisive one is that the icon does not depict its own subject: the fingers close on air (lobes at y 44–51.6, entirely below the blade at y 42.9–44.9) while the opaque sage hand hides the blade from x≈27 to x≈48 and the two surviving fragments sit 2.6 units apart in y against a 3.4–4.6-unit-thick blade, so they read as a lollipop pin and a stray tab rather than one lever. At 40 px the honest read is 'a three-fingered mitten floating past a green capsule in snow'. §H's acceptance line 'a hand on a lever with cold marks' therefore has no evidence in `.true.png`, and `.true.png` is the only render that counts for this file.

Two clauses to flag as brief-vs-set tensions rather than builder error: §H specifies `#2F6B52` for the grip and `#1E8A6E` for the snow, but neither hex appears anywhere in the 27 shipped `sort-*.svg` icons, and `sort-cond-frost.svg` — same M5 L1 S2 deck — draws its snowflakes in `#0D1E2E`. The builder followed the brief; the owner may want to rule on whether teal snow and a large spruce solid enter this set at all (C4/C1). Shrinking the flake to the two-or-three small asterisks the brief actually asks for resolves the duplication either way.

Note also that P1-3 makes the `<title>` untrue as written ('a gloved hand curled round the brake lever'), so U8 fails until the drawing is fixed — fix the art, not the alt.

Not applicable to this file: all motion clauses (§0.3, beat length, rest period, t=0 teaching frame, frame sheet) — static icon; and S1/S2/S4/S5/S6/SF1–SF5 — no machine and no rider depicted. S3 and SF6 do apply and both fail (P1-1, P2-5).

Hard rules: no <text>, no CSS variables, no scripts or external refs, no gradients/filters; static file so the reduced-motion render (.rm.png) is byte-identical to .img.png; 2218 bytes against the 8 KB icon budget; _check.py prints OK with no warnings.

§H acceptance at 40 px (.true.png): a hand on a lever with cold marks reads at true size; the silhouette (horizontal fist on a bar, fingers DOWN, lever bar across the lower third) is unmistakably different from sort-gear-gloves (upright glove, fingers UP, wide cuff), confirmed on a 40 px contact row with frost / wet-roots / dust / gloves / creek / fading-light / helmet.
residuals: Reviewer item 7 asked me to end the cuff inside the frame with a closed navy edge and a wrist band line. I removed the cuff instead: every version I drew of a sleeve stub read in the render as a folded paper flap or pennant (a thin wedge with a band line near its tip), so the hand now ends in a rounded fist back with a knuckle crease. This satisfies the underlying asks (nothing crosses the frame, one union silhouette, no seam splitting the sage mass) but there is no sleeve, so the top-right corner of the icon is empty paper.

Reviewer item 8 asked for four or five ribs at 2.5-unit spacing. I have four evenly spaced verticals but one of them is the bar-end cap seam (x 11, 1.6 weight) rather than a rib - the thumb covers the grip from x 18.6 rightward, so a fifth rib would have been fully occluded.

Reviewer item 1 asked for a 2-unit navy crease at the thumb root; the crease is the thumb lobe's own closing contour at outline weight 2, which is heavier than the 1.5-1.6 interior detail called for by item 9. I judged a digit outline to belong with the finger outlines rather than with the ribs, and it is what sort-gear-gloves does.

Reviewer item 3 asked me to shrink the fist to about 2x the grip diameter; measured, the hand is 35 units tall against a 13-unit grip (2.7x). The extra height is the finger reach down past the lever - shrinking further pulled the fingertips up into the blade band and the four lobes stopped reading at 40 px.

The lever passes BEHIND all four fingers rather than in front of two of them. I tried the front-crossing version the reviewer suggested: painting the blade over the two inboard lobes cut their tips off from the palm and they rendered as two detached sage pegs below a navy bar. Continuity is instead carried by the two exits sharing one centreline plus the navy finger-gaps sitting exactly on that line.

Flake colour stays #1E8A6E per §H rather than matching sort-cond-frost's #0D1E2E; the reviewer offered that swap conditionally. Teal groups the flakes with the drizzle as one weather system and keeps them quieter than the navy hand at 40 px.

defects.element: gloved hand — the four finger lobes (svg y 40.5–49.9, x 24–50) against the brake-lever blade (y 41.4–45.8)
defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.zoom.png and the 'lever thru fingers' crop (svg x 20–64, y 36–54); same read in .true.png @40 px and @32 px DPR1
defects.what: Nothing is being gripped. The four fingers are straight, parallel, equal-width (5 u) round-tipped tines drawn IN FRONT of the lever, hanging 3–4 u past its lower edge with no wrap, no crook and no contact. Compounding it, the 2-unit navy slots between the fingers are the same colour and near the same weight as the 4.3-unit solid navy lever, so blade and finger-gaps fuse into one navy grid. The result reads as a hand resting on a rail, or as a comb/rake — i.e. the same straight-parallel-lobe 'paw' construction as the retired icon and as sort-gear-gloves, which is precisely the defect §H was opened to fix. §H acceptance line 1 ('a hand on a lever') is not delivered.
defects.fix: Curl the fingers: end each tip on an arc that turns back inboard (+x) and stops at or above y=45 so the tips sit on the lever, not below it; then redraw the lever's outboard third (x≈5–24) IN FRONT of the fingertips so the blade visibly passes through a closed fist. Vary the finger widths (index widest, pinky narrowest) and break the dead-straight sides with a first-knuckle bend. Drop the blade to ~3 u thick so it is no longer the same visual weight as the slots between the fingers.

defects.element: handlebar grip (#2F6B52 capsule x 11–33, y 22–35, three 1.5-u ribs) versus the lever rod (x 3.4–60)
defects.where: renders/sort-cond-cold-hands.true.png @40 px; 32 px DPR1 contact sheet; 'thumb+grip junction' crop (svg x 8–34, y 18–42)
defects.what: The hierarchy is inverted, so both objects read as the wrong thing. The lever is the longest, heaviest, full-width horizontal in the frame (with a ball tip left and a bolted boss right), while the handlebar is a short dark capsule that stops dead inside the hand. A learner therefore reads the navy rod as the handlebar and has nothing left to read as a lever; the spruce capsule with its four vertical bars clustered in the outboard third reads as a separate object — at 32 px the ribs fuse into a dark core and it reads as a battery / flashlight / grille. At true size the icon says 'a mitten over a bar', not 'a hand on a brake lever'.
defects.fix: Make the bar the dominant horizontal: one spruce tube running from the bar-end cap at x≈6, behind the fist, and out the right side to x≈58, with the sage hand drawn over it. Delete the rib cluster or reduce it to two ribs at 1.8 u spanning only the visible outboard section (1.5 u is under the set's interior minimum and aliases to a smudge at 40 px). Then hang the lever off that tube on a small navy perch block at x≈50 and taper the blade down-and-outboard from it, ending inboard of the fist's outer edge.

defects.element: the two #1E8A6E snow asterisks (x 4.9–12.1 y 6.3–14.7, and x 18.4–23.6 y 5–11, stroke 1.8)

defects.element: lever pivot boss circle (57,43.6) r3 with #F9FCFA bolt r1.3, and the right-hand termination of the handlebar
defects.where: 'right of hand: bar absent' crop (svg x 44–64, y 14–50); visible in .zoom.png
defects.what: The pivot sits on blank paper — no perch, no clamp, nothing above or behind it — while the handlebar has two ends (a rounded cap at x=11 and an end swallowed by the hand at x=33) and never reaches the machine. A brake lever pivoting on nothing plus a bar that is capped at both ends is implausible machine anatomy (VISUAL_ASSETS S6) and a diagram-hygiene failure (an element attached to nothing). It is the first thing an adult sees at 4x, which is the zoom the owner inspects.
defects.fix: Carry the bar through to x≈58 as in the P1 fix and clamp the pivot to it with a ~6×8 navy perch block so the blade has something to hinge on. Delete the white bolt dot: r1.3 is 0.8 px at 40 px and does not survive anyway.

defects.where: 'thumb+grip junction' crop (svg x 8–34, y 18–42) at 8 px/unit; .zoom.png
defects.what: The thumb is a fully closed D-shaped lobe laid on top of the grip at the bar's mid-height, so it reads as an applied pad, flap or ear rather than a thumb wrapping the bar — a thumb on a grip must come round from the far side and appear below the tube, not sit on its face. Its closing chord runs parallel to and within about 1 u of the hand's left outline, producing a navy channel where the two strokes nearly touch. And its lower curve, the grip's bottom edge and the hand's outline trap a small paper wedge at roughly (21–27, 36–39) — a stray light speck in a flat field at 40 px (U5). §H's 'four fingers + thumb clearly separate' is only marginally met at 40 px and not met at 32.
defects.fix: Move the thumb below the bar so it wraps from the far side, tip pointing down-right at about (26,40); open its top edge into the hand's outline instead of closing the lobe; taper it from root to tip; and confirm no paper is trapped between thumb, grip and palm.

defects.element: palette relative to the shipped sort-* set — #2F6B52 (grip), #1E8A6E (snow/drizzle), #F9FCFA (bolt)
defects.where: 40 px and 32 px contact sheets, candidate beside sort-cond-frost, -dust, -wet-roots, -fading-light, -swollen-creek (all seven other cards of the m5-l1-s2 deck)
defects.what: The entire shipped 26-icon sort set uses exactly four hexes — #0D1E2E, #ABCDB8, #A93226, #DBA12E — and none of them is spruce, teal or paper. The candidate adds three. Worse, sort-cond-frost sits in the SAME deck (slotmap.ts m5-l1-s2) and draws its snow NAVY at 2.8 u, so shipping this makes snow drawn two ways side by side on one screen — C4, the clause VISUAL_ASSETS calls the one that fails silently — and the spruce grip becomes the only dark saturated mass in the deck (C1/C2, 'one product by one hand'). Brief §H does mandate these hexes, so this is a brief-versus-shipped-set conflict for the owner to settle rather than a builder error, but it cannot ship unsettled.
defects.fix: Pick one and apply it across the deck in the same pass: (a) keep teal and re-cut sort-cond-frost's flake to #1E8A6E so the deck agrees; or (b) draw the flakes navy like frost and the grip in sage with a navy outline like every other object in the set, leaving #1E8A6E for the water cards.

review.notes:
Round 3 review, nothing changed on disk. Ran _check.py (OK: 2218 bytes, viewBox 64x64, icon, animated=False) and _render.py --icon 40, then viewed all four renders: .img.png, .rm.png, .true.png, .zoom.png. Because the harness passes --icon as the width, .img/.rm/.true are the same 40 px shot (identical md5), so the only real inspection surfaces are .true.png and .zoom.png; I generated four extra views to compensate — 512 px for construction, 40 px and 32 px at DPR 1 (the harness renders at DPR 2, which hides the small-size failures), three 8 px/unit crops of the thumb-grip junction, the lever-through-fingers band and the area right of the hand, and 40/32 px contact sheets against the whole m5-l1-s2 deck plus sort-gear-gloves.

Two things the brief did not anticipate. First, 40 px is not the smallest shipped size: web/src/activities/sort_categorize/index.tsx renders the icon at size-10 (40 px) in the tray and size-8 (32 px) on the placed chip, so U10 must be judged at 32 px — where this icon is the weakest of the eight cards in its deck (frost, dust, wet-roots, fading-light and swollen-creek all still read; this one goes to 'a pale mitten, a dark green thing, two teal crosses'). Second, a set-level fact worth an owner decision: the shipped 26-icon sort set uses only #0D1E2E, #ABCDB8, #A93226, #DBA12E — the brief's mandated #2F6B52 and #1E8A6E are new to the set, and sort-cond-frost draws snow navy in the same deck. That conflict should be settled before this or §I/§J land, since §J will bring teal rain in too.

One claim I tested and dropped: the lever blade tip is flush with the bar end's outer edge (3.4 vs 3.5), not past it, so it is not a defect.

Verdict is fix on two P1s. The colour defect §H was opened for is genuinely gone, but the geometry defect underneath it is not: this is still a sage lobed mitten in the sort-gear-gloves / retired-icon construction family, now laid over two unconnected horizontal bars, and at 32–40 px neither 'lever' nor 'handlebar' arrives. The single highest-leverage change is to run one spruce bar all the way through the fist and out both sides, hang a tapered blade off a perch on it, and curl the fingertips onto that blade — after which the flake, thumb and crease fixes are small.

residuals: Thumb is crease-defined, not a separate lobe. Dossier item 5 asked for a thumb wrapping from the far side as its own shape; I built three separate-lobe versions (root at the fist's inboard edge, tip down-outboard) and every one rendered at 40 px as a fifth finger or a beak, and one of them ate the lever's right exit. Grip ribs deleted rather than reduced to two at 1.8. With the fist where it now sits, only ~6 units of bar end are exposed outboard of the fist; two 1.8 ribs would have been ~3 units apart and aliased to a smudge at 40 px. The dossier's own fix for item 2 permits deletion. The bar end therefore reads as a plain rounded bar end, not a ribbed grip.

The lever blade is a constant-width 3.4 stroke with a round tip, not a taper. Dossier item 2 asked for a taper down-and-outboard; at 40 px the difference between 3.4 constant and 3.4->2.6 tapered is under half a pixel, and the polygon cost complexity for no visible gain. The down-outboard slope is there (root y 36.4 at x 52.7, tip y 39.4 at x 4.4).

The band below y 46 is empty paper. The composition is a horizontal band (weather 3-18, bar 21.5-32.5, fist 12-42, blade 34-41). Putting weather in the bottom-left would have collided with the lever's outboard exit, which is the element carrying the P1 fix, so I left it.

With the set's mandatory 2-unit outline in a 64-unit box I could not get four separated digits to survive 32 px - every version that did (separate outlined finger shapes) failed worse at 40 px as claws. The fist, bar, lever, flake and drizzle all still read at 32 px.

Round 1, adversarial, nothing changed. Ran _check.py (OK, 681 bytes, icon, animated=False) and _render.py twice — once with --icon 40 and once with --width 512 for defect hunting — and viewed all four PNGs plus a 6x nearest-neighbour blow-up of .true.png, four 3x magnified detail crops (bolt/cloud junction, cloud top-right, rightmost rain vs cloud corner, bolt tip), and a 40 px contact sheet of the candidate beside all eight shipped sort-cond icons.

VERDICT: fix, on the strength of P2-1 alone. The two P2s are cheap: P2-1 is a four-number geometry edit to one path; P2-2 is a sentence in the <title> plus a handoff note. Everything else about the file is sound, and I looked hard — three hypotheses I formed and then DISPROVED with measurement rather than reporting: (a) that the sage cloud was an out-of-family mass (it is inside the set's range); (b) that the rightmost rain streak collided with the cloud's corner while the others floated (all four clear the base by 1–3 raster px at DPR2 — consistent, and consistent with rain); (c) that the rain streaks were uneven in length (all four are exactly 11.2 units).

Not held against the candidate: the amber bolt and the omitted front line are both explicitly briefed in §J, and teal in a sort-cond icon is new to that sub-set but established in 18 files across the wider asset library. S1–S6 and SF1–SF6 do not apply — no machine, no rider. U7 (clay-500 once) does not apply — no icon in this set carries magenta.

Re-review after the fix should re-measure the amber run at 40 px: the acceptance bar is amber continuous to within ~1 unit of the bolt's point, i.e. a non-zero amber run in every row of the .true.png scan down to the tip.
