self_review: true.png at 40 px: reads as one quad pulling one small box trailer - machine left, box-on-a-wheel right, joined by a bar; the learner's first word is 'towing'.

zoom.png: the amber hitch mark does NOT float - it sits ON the drawbar with navy line visibly entering from the machine side (x 36.7-38.8) and leaving toward the trailer (x 46.4-49), so it reads as a coupling, not a loose dot (the retired file's defect).

zoom.png: the amber disc is clearly above the ground line and has no hub ring, so it cannot be misread as a third wheel; it is the only amber in the file and it is the eye's first stop (correct for the sun-400 'needs a check first' bucket).

zoom.png vs sort-cond-dust.zoom.png: same machine language - identical body-profile proportions (low front deck, seat hump, rear deck), sage #ABCDB8 fill, navy outline, two sage wheels with navy rims and navy hub rings; no toaster box, no gear-tooth tires.
zoom.png: the quad carries handlebars (front riser + crossbar) and a rear rack (rail on two legs) - both anchored to the body, per the 'racks and bars' rule.

zoom.png: no dangling leaders - the drawbar's left end is tucked under the rear tire and its right end under the trailer box's paper fill; the rack rail is carried by two legs; the handlebar stem lands on the seat top.

zoom.png: the trailer wheel hangs below the box body (iteration-1 defect fixed, where the wheel sat inside the box face and read as a washing machine); the box + lid seam + wheel + tongue read as a small utility trailer, not a suitcase.
zoom.png: one navy ground line runs under BOTH machine and trailer and all three wheels touch it - the two objects read as one scene.
img.png and rm.png are pixel-identical: the file is static (checker reports animated=False), so no reduced-motion block is required or present.

true.png compared with sort-cargo-rack-limits.true.png and sort-cond-dust.true.png: distinct silhouette at 40 px (rack-limits is a bracket + strapped box + tag; dust is a quad + arcs), and the line weight/scale sit in the same family.

Source + render: colours are only #0D1E2E, #ABCDB8, #F9FCFA, #DBA12E - no brick red, no magenta, no gradients, no filters, no text; one 2-unit outline weight with 1.5-1.8 interior detail and the set's 2.4 ground line.
_check.py prints OK at 1165 bytes, viewBox 64x64 - 14% of the 8 KB icon budget.
residuals: Section K contradicts itself: it says the quad faces RIGHT but also puts the trailer in the right third 'behind it' with the tongue going 'to the quad's rear'. Those cannot both hold. I kept the brief's LAYOUT (quad left two-thirds, hitch, trailer right third) and drew the quad facing LEFT, which is the only physically coherent towing arrangement and matches the shipped set - sort-cond-dust trails its dust to the right and every set quad carries its whip flag at the right rear, i.e. the set's side-view quad already faces left. Mirroring is a one-line change if the owner wants the machine nose-right with the trailer on the left instead.

Section K's acceptance line says 'the quad matches sort-cargo-rack-limits' silhouette', but sort-cargo-rack-limits contains no quad at all (it is a rack bracket, a strapped box and a luggage tag). I matched the set's real side-view quad, taken from sort-cond-dust / sort-cargo-two-up / -kid-behind / -lap, scaled 0.95.

Side view shows two wheels, per Section K's own wording ('two visible wheels with navy rims') and every shipped side-view quad in the set. The global 'four wheels' rule cannot be honoured in a 64 px side profile without the far wheels turning to mud; it is honoured on the plates and rear views instead.

The amber mark is a FILLED #DBA12E disc r 3 with a navy outline rather than a hollow ring. The set's amber language is filled (sort-cargo-heavy-high's arrow, sort-cond-loose-tools' wrench), and a hollow r-3 ring with a 2-unit stroke disappears at 40 px. It is centred on the drawbar so navy line enters and leaves it, which is what stops it floating.

The subject is inherently wide and flat, so roughly the top third of the 64 box is empty (content spans y 25-54, centre y 39). That is in the same range as the shipped sort-cond-dust, but the set's fuller icons buy their height from riders or dust clouds - nothing in Section K's element list could fill the top without adding an unexplained mark, so I left it clean rather than padded.

defects.where: renders/sort-cargo-towing.true.png (40 px) and .zoom.png; 10x zoom vs sort-cargo-two-up
defects.what: The chassis renders as a solid navy slab, so the machine does not read as the set's quad — at true size it reads as a ride-on mower / pedal go-kart pulling a toolbox. Cause: the deck top (y 40.5) and the slanted underside (y 46.4 to 42.7) are only 5.2 units apart at the front and 2.9 at the rear; two 2-unit strokes eat 2 of that. A pixel probe of the 10x render finds sage only at y 42.0-43.5 at x=12 and y 42-43 at x=32 (1.5-2.5 units), against 7 units of sage in sort-cargo-two-up's equivalent band (probe: sage y 42-48 at x=30). At 40 px that is ~1 px of sage between two 1.25 px navy strokes. Root cause: this path is the RETIRED sort-cargo-towing body translated verbatim by (-26.5, +2.6) — every vertex matches — i.e. the file reuses the exact shape §K calls 'an unreadable shape beside the trailer', with no rider to give it scale.
defects.fix: Redraw the body at the set's scale instead of reusing the retired path: body ~38 units wide, deck top to underside >= 9 units (two-up: 41 to 50), FLAT underside (start and end the path at the same y, as two-up does, not 46.4 to 42.7), wheels r 6.3 with hub r 2.3 to match kid-behind/lap. Buy the room by shrinking the trailer and deleting the rear rack.

That satisfies the set convention, keeps the trailer physically behind the tow vehicle, and resolves §K's own contradiction (it asks for a right-facing quad with the trailer 'behind it' in the right third, which cannot both be true).

residuals: The ridge's hidden crest passes behind the card between (25.1,73.2) and (101.9,76.8), so the terrain under the compass is implied rather than drawn. This is deliberate (it is what lets both crossings be near-perpendicular and kills the burr family of defects) but a reviewer who wants the map continuous across the card will not see it.

The trail's two ends are round caps floating inside the sage rather than running off the disc edge. This matches level-5-ridge-runner and level-7-trail-boss, whose trails also terminate inside their terrain, but it is a floating terminus if judged in isolation.

The ground is a single sage tone; L5 and L7 stack two and three terrain tones. A second (spruce) tier was tried in planning and rejected because the card is already spruce and the two masses would be separated by only 5-7 px of sage at 96 px. Result: the candidate's terrain is lighter in the contact sheet than L5's, even though its silhouette is comparably articulated.

A 5-deg radial scan reports the dial-rim ink running 6.7 units deep at 20 and 160 deg. This is the ridge stroke itself crossing radially (the scan ray runs down its length), not a tangential burr - confirmed by eye in crop_dial_left.png and crop_dial_right.png - but the same numeric test the reviewer used will flag those two angles again.

defects.element: Middle contour band fill #DEEDE5 (line 14: <path d="M1 41.1 Q23.5 26.9 46 41.1 L46 48 L1 48 Z" fill="#DEEDE5"/>)
defects.where: Source, not a render — but it is a hard integration blocker. Verified by simulating the shipping lint against the file.
defects.what: #DEEDE5 is NOT in the shipping asset lint's token set. web/src/assets/lint_assets.py defines TOKENS = {#0D1E2E, #1E8A6E, #2F6B52, #46555A, #A93226, #ABCDB8, #B5446E, #D6DFDA, #DBA12E, #ECF3EF, #F9FCFA} — eleven values, no #DEEDE5 — and check 6 does `stray = hexes - TOKENS`, so the moment this file lands in web/src/assets/svg/ the lint prints `badge-b-terrain: non-token colours ['#DEEDE5']` and exits 1. I ran the comparison: file uses [#0D1E2E, #2F6B52, #ABCDB8, #B5446E, #DEEDE5, #F9FCFA]; stray = ['#DEEDE5']. Zero of the 100+ shipped SVGs in web/src/assets/svg/ use #DEEDE5 — it exists only as a CSS token in web/src/styles/tokens.css. qa/svg/_check.py passed this file only because its own palette list (line 14: includes #1E4440, #DEEDE5, #F4F9F6) is WIDER than the shipping lint's, so `_check.py: OK` is a false green here. BRIEFS.md §0.1's colour table also lists #DEEDE5, so the brief and the lint disagree — but the lint is what gates the repo.
defects.fix: Swap #DEEDE5 for #ECF3EF (in TOKENS, and the value the rest of the badge set uses for a mid band — see badge-b-terrain retired, badge-b-prepared). Do not 'fix' this by widening lint_assets.py TOKENS without owner sign-off. Then re-run `python web/src/assets/lint_assets.py` mentally against the file, or at minimum re-run the hex-vs-TOKENS diff, before declaring it ready — _check.py alone will not catch this class of defect.

defects.element: Hill silhouette `M3 45 Q24 9 45 45 Z` plus the eye group plus the detached brow `M11.5 13.5 Q24 5.5 36.5 13.5`, taken together as one emblem
defects.where: badge-b-terrain.true.png (32 px, the shipping size), .zoom.png, and my BadgeMedal mock at both 32 px (size m) and 44 px (size l)
defects.what: The emblem reads as the Eye of Providence — an eye on top of a striped pyramid, with a radiance arc above it. It does not read as 'an eye reading terrain'. Cause is geometric: x(t) on that quadratic is exactly linear (x = 3 + 42t), so the flanks are near-straight lines running from the frame's bottom corners up to a narrow apex directly under the eye — a cone, not a hill. The three near-parallel banding lines then read as stripes wrapped around that cone, and the brow arc floating 6 units clear above the lid completes the radiance. Side by side with badge-b-mindset and badge-b-graduate at 32 px, a first-time learner names this one 'the all-seeing eye' before 'terrain'. That is 'an element that reads as the wrong thing' — the brief's own P1 definition — and it is worse on a progress shelf where badges are scanned, not studied.
defects.fix: Kill the cone. Make the mass a RIDGE, not a peak: apex off-centre (x ≈ 19 or 29, not 24), two or three overlapping rounded mounds of unequal height, and flanks that taper out through the LEFT and RIGHT edges of the frame rather than converging on the bottom corners — so the mass is wider at the eye's height than the eye is. Drop the brow entirely (§M's draw list does not ask for one, and the hill is already the second element). Sit the eye lower and larger so it is bedded into the ridge rather than perched on its point.

defects.element: Eye almond `M10 22.5 Q24 8.5 38 22.5 Q24 36.5 10 22.5 Z` against the hill silhouette and the top contour `M1 41.1 Q23.5 26.9 46 41.1`
defects.where: badge-b-terrain.true.png at 32 px; clearest in the 4x .zoom.png and in my 480 px probe
defects.what: The §M defect being fixed — 'the eye floats above the contour arcs with a gap; the two elements do not read as one emblem at 32 px' — is only fixed at dead centre. The lower lid's low point is (24, 29.5) and the silhouette apex is (24, 27), so they overlap by 2.5 units on the centre line and the flanks emerge from behind the lid at only x ≈ 18.3 and x ≈ 29.7. Outside that 11.4-unit window the eye is over open paper: at the almond's left tip (10, 22.5) the hill flank is at y = 35, a 12.5-unit gap — 8 px of bare paper at 32 px, LARGER than the retired badge's 7-unit centre gap. And the emblem's own contour system never reaches the eye: the top contour's crest is at (23.5, 34.0), 4.5 units below the lid. So at 32 px the eye still reads as a separate white lens balanced on a point, with its wings overhanging.
defects.fix: Widen the mass so it is broader than the eye at y ≈ 22–30 (see the P1 fix), and raise the top contour so its crest runs at y ≈ 30–31, passing behind the lower lid and re-emerging on both sides — the eye then interrupts a line that visibly continues, which is what welds two shapes into one emblem.

defects.element: The three banded fills inside clipPath #sacbt-hill: `<rect fill="#ABCDB8">`, then the #DEEDE5 band, then the #ABCDB8 band (lines 13–15)
defects.where: badge-b-terrain.zoom.png and .true.png. Verified by pixel probe down the x = 24 column: y31–33 = (171,205,184) #ABCDB8, y34 navy, y35–38 = (222,237,229) #DEEDE5, y39–40 navy, y41–44 = (171,205,184) #ABCDB8, y45 navy.
defects.what: The banding is non-monotonic — sage, then LIGHTER pale pine, then sage again. Elevation shading has to run one way for a contour band to read as a step in height. Two bands of identical value separated by a lighter one reads instead as a ribbon or a lit stripe wrapped round the cone — or, to a learner, as a road or a snow line cutting across it. It also makes the top mass (behind the eye) and the bottom sliver the same colour, so the eye cannot tell summit from base. On the unearned medal state (BadgeMedal renders `opacity-45 grayscale`), the sage/pale/sage ramp collapses into one flat grey mass and the terrain disappears entirely.
defects.fix: Monotonic ramp, lightest at the summit: #F9FCFA (summit, behind the eye) → #ECF3EF → #ABCDB8 (base), which is the retired badge's own order and uses only lint-approved tokens — this also resolves the P1 palette blocker in the same edit.

defects.element: The closing `Z` on the hill silhouette `M3 45 Q24 9 45 45 Z`, stroked #0D1E2E at 1.5
defects.where: badge-b-terrain.true.png at 32 px; and my BadgeMedal mock, both size m (32 px art in a 44 px diamond) and size l

defects.element: Stroke widths: brow and eye almond at stroke-width 1.8; hill silhouette, both contours and the iris at 1.5

strengths: File contract is clean: root <svg> with viewBox and role="img", <title> as first child carrying a real one-sentence alt, no width/height, no <text>, no external refs, no filters or gradients, single prefixed id (#sacbt-hill) that is actually referenced. 1718 bytes against an 8 KB budget. qa/svg/_check.py returns OK.
Fireweed is used exactly once (U7): the rotated rounded-square blaze in the pupil, and it IS visible at the 32 px shipping size — that §M acceptance line has evidence in .true.png.

The eye's internal construction genuinely does copy badge-b-mindset: paper almond, spruce #2F6B52 iris, rotated rounded-square #B5446E blaze, offset paper glint, and the iris circle merging into both lids so the sclera reads as two thin crescents. Blaze-to-iris ratio (0.44) is close to mindset's (0.40).
The silhouette apex lands exactly on the briefed (24, 27) — the quadratic M3 45 Q24 9 45 45 evaluates to (24, 27) at t = 0.5, so the coordinate spec was honoured, not eyeballed.

The clip-path construction is technically sound: the contour strokes are cut exactly at the silhouette boundary and the un-clipped 1.5 outline covers the cut, so there are no butt-cap stubs or fill/stroke seams anywhere along the hill edge — verified at 10 px/unit.
Static file, so the reduced-motion question is trivially satisfied: no @keyframes, no <animate>, no <set>, and .rm.png is byte-identical to .img.png (md5 94d4f2ce…).
review.notes: Round 1. Renders produced myself and viewed: .img.png, .rm.png, .true.png, .zoom.png (all four; note _render.py defaults width to icon_px, so .img/.rm/.true are the same 32 px DPR-2 shot and are byte-identical — no separate large render exists for this file). I additionally built (a) a nearest-neighbour 12x blowup of .true.png to judge the emblem at true pixel resolution, (b) a 480 px probe for pixel-level colour and stroke-width measurement, and (c) a six-badge contact sheet at 32 px and 44 px plus a BadgeMedal frame mock (64 px and 96 px frames, rotated diamond plate, earned and unearned/grayscale states) so the badge could be judged where it actually ships rather than on a white square. Scratch files in the session scratchpad: sheet.png, crop_row32.png, crop_medal_l.png, true_nearest12.png, junction.png, full480.png, probe480.png. The single most important finding is the #DEEDE5 palette blocker, because it is invisible to the builder's own toolchain: qa/svg/_check.py carries a WIDER palette list (it accepts #1E4440, #DEEDE5, #F4F9F6) than web/src/assets/lint_assets.py, whose TOKENS set has only eleven values and does not include #DEEDE5. What is still imperfect: the eyebrow sits only 1.2 units clear of the upper lid, so at the true 32 px size the brow, lid and iris crown smear into one dark cap and the eye looks hooded rather than open - raising the brow ~1.7 units fixes it and also improves the vertical balance; and inside your prescribed ramp the middle and inner bands are only 5 grayscale counts apart in the unearned state, so the inner nesting is carried by the contour lines rather than the fills.
